title: G1.2: Catalog roots — reclaim from known-safe caches on a pressured device with no configured root
description:
# G1.2 - Catalog roots: reclaim from known-safe cache locations on a pressured device that has no configured scan root

## Context
`daemon/loop_main.rs:2801-2840` (B5 device-affinity gate): under elevated pressure on a device with no `root_path` and `cross_devices=false`, the daemon logs once per `DEVICE_AFFINITY_WARN_INTERVAL` and returns; no ballast handling, no scan. This is deliberate (it replaced a hot loop that scanned unrelated roots) but it leaves the pressured volume untouched. On the operator's host `/` fills from `$HOME` caches while roots are `/tmp` and `/data/tmp`. The macOS PAL already has a rich cleanup catalog (`platform/macos/cleanup_catalog.rs`, 28 rules: Xcode DerivedData, Electron caches, release-work buildroots); Linux has 7 (`platform/linux/cleanup_catalog.rs`). The catalog is used as a classifier, not as a root source.

## Goal
When pressure is on a device with no configured root, derive a bounded set of catalog roots that live on that device and scan only them as opaque candidates, with every existing veto intact.

## Design
- `platform/cleanup_catalog.rs`: add `CatalogRoot { template: &'static str, disposition: CandidateOpaque, min_age: Duration, confidence: f64 }` with templates such as `$HOME/.cache/*`, `$HOME/.cargo/registry/cache`, `$HOME/.cargo/registry/src`, `$HOME/.cargo/git/checkouts`, `$HOME/.npm/_cacache`, `$HOME/.cache/pip`, `$HOME/.local/share/Trash/files`, `/var/tmp`, `/var/cache/apt/archives`; and `fn catalog_roots_for_mount(mount: &Path, homes: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<PathBuf>` that expands `$HOME` for every real user home on that mount (PAL `user_homes()`: current user, plus `/etc/passwd` UIDs >= 1000 when root), resolves globs one level, and keeps only paths whose device id equals the mount's.
- Linux catalog: add the entries above plus `~/.rustup/toolchains/*` as SignalOnly (never a candidate; toolchains are not artifacts). Unknown subtrees are never enumerated.
- `daemon/loop_main.rs` B5 branch: if `config.scanner.catalog_roots_on_pressured_device` (default true) and the derived set is non-empty, dispatch `ScanRequest { paths: derived, root_source: RootSource::Catalog, catalog_only: true, budget: bounded }` at most once per pressure epoch (re-armed when the level rises or after `scanner.catalog_rescan_interval_secs`, default 900); otherwise fall through to the existing back-off. Log every derived root once.
- `scanner/engine.rs` + walker: `catalog_only` means each root is treated as an opaque candidate unit (size estimate bounded, no recursive descent beyond the catalog rule's own depth); scoring uses the catalog confidence as the name factor; all pre-flight vetoes unchanged (`HardcodedSourceTree`, `LooksLikeSourceCode`, `.git`, open files, leases).
- `scan_complete` details gain `root_source: "catalog"`, `catalog_roots: n`.
- CLI parity: `sbh scan --catalog [MOUNT]` runs the same derivation for a mount so operators can preview.

## Files
`src/platform/cleanup_catalog.rs`, `src/platform/linux/cleanup_catalog.rs`, `src/platform/macos/cleanup_catalog.rs` (root templates), `src/platform/pal.rs` (`user_homes()`), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/scanner/{engine,walker,scoring}.rs`, `src/core/config.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (`scan --catalog`), docs.

## Tests
- Unit: `catalog_roots_for_mount` on a fixture home tree returns only existing paths on the same device; `$HOME` expansion for multiple homes; glob depth 1.
- Unit (`loop_main.rs`): B5 branch with derived roots dispatches exactly one catalog scan per epoch; with empty derivation falls back to back-off; re-arms on level rise.
- Integration (`tests/daemon_host_protection.rs`, new): fixture at synthetic Orange, no configured root -> the loop (mock PAL) derives roots, scans, produces candidates only under catalog paths, and a planted `$HOME/projects/foo/Cargo.toml` tree is never a candidate. Log lines asserted.
- e2e: `sbh scan --catalog / --json` lists derived roots and candidates; `--explain` shows `root_source=catalog`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sbh scan --catalog / --json` returns candidates under `~/.cache` or `~/.cargo/registry` and nothing under `/data/projects` or `~/.rustup/toolchains`.
- [ ] Daemon integration test green; no candidate ever passes without the standard pre-flight.

## Considerations
- Catalog scanning is opt-out by config for shared multi-user hosts; document in README "Catalog roots".
- Never derive roots on network or read-only mounts (reuse coordinator skip rules).
notes: Related from bd-rc-master-ajg1: bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.1 makes pressure control per-mount (ObserveOnly/Maintain/Reclaim/Recovery/Idle) so a pressured mount without roots never suppresses routine work elsewhere; catalog roots are the natural `reclaim_capability` for such a mount. Sandbox evidence (v0.5.1): with `/` Orange and a healthy /data root, 0 scans in 45 s; with cross_devices=true both engines scanned but dispatched nothing because the behavior matrix maps Orange to IdentifyOnly (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.2).
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.12 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G1.3: Daemon liveness via kernel-locked daemon.lock; remove /proc substring heuristic; report reasons and service gates
description:
# G1.3 - Daemon liveness truth: a kernel-locked `daemon.lock` replaces the `/proc` substring heuristic; status reports why the daemon is not running

## Context
`cli_app.rs:6565-6595`: `daemon_running` is true if `state.json` is fresher than 90 s, else `detect_daemon_running_fallback()` (`:7031-7070`): `systemctl is-active sbh.service` == "active", or any `/proc/*/cmdline` containing both "sbh" and "daemon". During the audit this matched the auditor's own zsh process (its cmdline contained the words), so `sbh status` reported the daemon running three days after it was stopped. The dashboard adapter and `check --predict` reuse the same state-file logic. The state file itself is not an exclusive-ownership signal.

## Goal
Exactly one source of truth for "a daemon owns this state directory": an exclusive advisory lock held for the daemon's lifetime; everything else is diagnostic detail.

## Design
- `daemon/self_monitor.rs`: `DaemonLock::acquire(state_dir) -> Result<DaemonLock>` opens `<state_dir>/daemon.lock` (0o600, create), `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` via `nix`, writes `{pid, started_at, version}` JSON, keeps the fd open; drop releases. `DaemonLock::probe(state_dir) -> LockProbe { held: bool, owner: Option<{pid, started_at, version}> }` tries `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` on a fresh fd and releases immediately. A second daemon start fails fast with SBH-3003 "daemon already running (pid N)".
- `cli_app.rs` status/check/dashboard adapters: `daemon_running = probe.held`; `daemon_state_reason` in `{locked, no_lock, no_lock_stale_state, unit_inactive, unit_condition_failed, lock_dir_unreadable}`; when the CLI user cannot read the state dir (root daemon, user CLI) it reports `lock_dir_unreadable` and falls back to `systemctl is-active` / `launchctl print` only, never to `/proc` substrings. Remove `detect_daemon_running_fallback`'s Method 2 entirely.
- Service gates: on Linux, `systemctl show sbh.service -p ActiveState,SubState,ConditionResult,ConditionTimestamp,LoadState` and parse drop-ins (`systemctl cat`) for `ConditionPathExists=` lines; report `service_gates: [{kind: "condition_path_exists", path, satisfied}]` in status JSON and a human hint "service disabled by /etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED". macOS equivalent from `launchctl print` (`daemon/service/launchctl.rs`).
- Daemon: acquire the lock before spawning workers; include `lock_path` in the startup log; release on shutdown after the final state write (G3.2).

## Files
`src/daemon/self_monitor.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs`, `src/tui/adapters.rs`, `src/daemon/service/{systemd,launchctl}.rs`, `src/core/errors.rs` (new code), README state-file protocol section.

## Tests
- Unit: acquire/probe/release; second acquire fails; probe after drop reports not held; JSON payload round-trip; permission-denied path yields `lock_dir_unreadable`.
- Integration (`tests/integration_tests.rs`): spawn `sbh daemon --config <tmp>` in the background, wait for the lock, `sbh status --json` -> `daemon_running=true reason=locked`; kill the daemon -> `false reason=no_lock_stale_state`; meanwhile run a decoy process whose argv contains "sbh daemon" (for example `sh -c 'sleep 30 # sbh daemon'`) and assert it does not flip the answer.
- Unit (`systemd.rs`): parse fixture `systemctl show`/`cat` output with a `ConditionPathExists=!/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED` drop-in -> gate reported unsatisfied when the file exists.
- e2e: status liveness case.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host today: `sbh status --json` -> `daemon_running=false`, `daemon_state_reason=unit_condition_failed`, gate path shown.
- [ ] `sbh daemon` refuses to start twice against one state dir.
- [ ] No reference to `/proc` cmdline scanning remains in `cli_app.rs`.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.1, closed as duplicate): also expose `state_age_secs` and `state_stale: bool` in status JSON and print "state N stale" in human mode; report `policy_mode` only from fresh state; keep `--pidfile` as an override of the default pidfile written next to daemon.lock. Observed on the operator host: JSON said daemon_running=true while human mode said "not running (degraded mode)" in the same minute.
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.1 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G1.4: Loud degradation — reclaim_capability/reserve_state in status, doctor FAILs, ReclaimUnavailable notification
description:
# G1.4 - Loud, actionable degradation: "pressured mount has no scannable root" and "no reserve on pressured mount" become doctor FAILs, status fields, and notifications

## Context
Today the only trace of "sbh cannot help this mount" is a stderr line once per `DEVICE_AFFINITY_WARN_INTERVAL` (`loop_main.rs:2827`) and an `ActivityEvent::Info`. `doctor --system` already has `ballast.reserve` (FAIL on this host) but nothing about reclaim capability. The README operator-perspective table promises the daemon reacts in seconds; silence is the worst failure class (bd-r7m7: "operator surprise is failure").

## Goal
Every mount in `status`/`check` carries a `reclaim_capability` and `reserve_state`; `doctor --system` FAILs when a mount at Yellow+ has neither; the daemon notifies at Orange+ when it is backing off.

## Design
- `status --json` `pressure.mounts[]` gains `reclaim_capability: "configured" | "catalog" | "none"` (computed from configured roots on that device, then catalog derivation from G1.2), `reserve_state: { configured_bytes, present_bytes, releasable_bytes, floor_pct }`, and `protection_summary: "protected" | "reserve_only" | "reclaim_only" | "unprotected"`. Human status prints an `UNPROTECTED` badge in red for any non-Green mount with `none`.
- `doctor --system` checks: `reclaim.pressured_mount_no_root` (FAIL when level >= Yellow and capability none; WARN when Green), `ballast.reserve_floor_limited` (WARN with numbers), `service.gated` (FAIL when a Condition gate disables the unit; from G1.3).
- Daemon notification: `NotificationEvent::ReclaimUnavailable { mount, level, reason }` at Orange+ with `min_notify_interval` throttling; journal + file channels by default.
- `check` (pre-build check) exits 2 with the same message when the target mount is unprotected and at Orange+ (opt-out `--allow-unprotected`).

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs` (status/check/doctor), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (event), `src/daemon/notifications.rs` (variant, template placeholders), `src/tui/adapters.rs` (badge), README status/doctor sections.

## Tests
- Unit: capability derivation for configured/catalog/none with mock PAL; doctor check matrix by level.
- Integration: `sbh status --json` on a fixture config with roots off-device -> `reclaim_capability=none`, `protection_summary=unprotected`; `doctor --system --json` FAIL entry with remediation text; `check` exit code.
- Unit (`notifications.rs`): event dispatch + throttle.
- e2e cases for status and doctor.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host (pre-G1.2) `sbh doctor --system` FAILs `reclaim.pressured_mount_no_root` for `/`; after G1.2 it PASSes with capability `catalog`.
notes: Related from bd-rc-master-ajg1: bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.8 defines state.json v2 (per-mount controller state, idle_reason, rates/forecast, threads, counters, cpu_secs_total, stopped_at/exit_reason); `reclaim_capability`/`reserve_state` should live in the same per-mount block.

title: G1.5: Steady-state CPU and no-spin proof harness for the daemon binary (tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs)
description:
# G1.5 - Steady-state CPU and no-spin proof harness for the daemon binary

## Context
The design doc (docs/scanner-redesign-event-driven.md section 7) requires "< 1% of one core averaged over 10 min" at Green with no FS activity, and the operator kill switch on this host cites a spin at Red urgency when the pressured volume has no root and no reserve. `loop_main.rs` has a duty-cycle limiter (:404-482), an empty-pass back-off (:5362), and the B5 device-affinity gate (:2801-2840), each unit-tested in isolation, but nothing measures the whole daemon's CPU under the failing scenario. The last real run consumed 33 s CPU in 5 min with a `CPUQuota=10%` cap (consistent with saturating the quota).

## Goal
A reusable integration harness that runs the real `sbh daemon` binary against a synthetic environment for N seconds, samples its CPU time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` utime+stime, or rusage via `wait4`), counts scan dispatches from the JSONL log, and asserts budgets. It becomes the regression net for every hot-loop fix (v0.4.29, v0.4.38, v0.5.0, #15 all addressed spins).

## Design
- `tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs` (new, Linux; skipped elsewhere with a logged reason): helper `DaemonRun::start(config_toml, env) -> handle` using `CARGO_BIN_EXE_sbh`, temp state/log dirs, small `poll_interval_ms`; `handle.cpu_seconds()`; `handle.jsonl_events()`; `handle.stop()` (SIGTERM, wait, assert exit 0).
- Scenarios: (a) Green, no FS activity, 60 s -> CPU < 0.6 s (1%), zero scans; (b) synthetic Orange on a device with no root and no reserve (config pointing `root_paths` off-device and a tiny tmpfs fixture as the "pressured" mount, or a debug-only `SBH_TEST_FORCE_PRESSURE=<mount>=<free_pct>` override gated behind `cfg!(debug_assertions)`) -> CPU < 1%, zero scan dispatches, exactly one `no_scannable_root` event per epoch; (c) with G1.2 catalog roots enabled -> exactly one bounded catalog scan per epoch.
- Every scenario writes a JSON artifact (`$SBH_TEST_ARTIFACT_DIR/daemon-cpu-<scenario>.json`: cpu_seconds, wall, events, dispatches, rss_peak) matching the style of the scanner-v2 validation artifacts, so CI uploads it.
- Wire into CI (`ci.yml` `stress` job or a new `daemon-budget` job) and `scripts/quality-gate.sh` as a HARD stage.

## Files
`tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` (helpers), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (test-only pressure override if needed, clearly gated), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/quality-gate.sh`, docs/testing-and-logging.md.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Scenario (b) fails on the commit before the fix that the kill-switch note describes (bisect once, document) and passes after G1.1/G1.2/G1.4.
- [ ] Artifacts uploaded in CI; budget numbers documented in a "Daemon budgets" section of docs/tui-acceptance-gates-and-budgets.md.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.11, design; this bead owns the harness): charge scanner, prescan, maintenance, index and monitor-tick time to one token bucket (rate = max_scan_duty_cycle_pct/100 cores, burst 5 s) and expose `cpu_secs_total` in state.json; budgets: <= 2% of wall at Green/host-layout, <= 33% under sustained Orange with bounded work (Q7 in the 2026-09-02 plan). Suggested harness scenarios beyond (a)-(c): sustained Orange with a stale Definite fixture (work present) and Red with an empty pool (emergency events must be emitted once, not 100 times/min as on 2026-08-18).

title: G9: Policy engine semantics — make the documented progressive-delivery safeguards real, configurable, and tested
description:
# G9 - Policy engine semantics: make the progressive-delivery safeguards the docs describe real, configurable, and tested

## Background (2026-09-01 audit of `src/daemon/policy.rs`)
README L1023-1054 and AGENTS.md describe observe -> canary -> enforce with automatic demotion to FallbackSafe on calibration breach (3 consecutive Fail windows), guardrail drift, canary budget exhaustion (>10/hour), serialization failure, and kill switch; explicit promotion only ("the system never auto-promotes"); recovery after 3 clean windows to Canary. Code:
- `initial_mode` default is `Enforce` (`:149`), not Observe.
- `calibration_breach_windows = 25` (`:154`) and the breach path is advisory-only: it logs "continuing in current mode" and never demotes (`:760-768`); the counter hard-resets at 100 (`:747`).
- `FallbackReason::CanaryBudgetExhausted` and `FallbackReason::SerializationFailure` are never constructed in production (only in `decision_plane_tests.rs`); canary overflow returns `Keep` (`:1047`) and nothing else.
- E-process alarm demotes only when pressure >= Orange and >= 30 observations (`:1074-1079`).
- `check_emergency_escalation` auto-promotes FallbackSafe -> Enforce after 5 min at Yellow+ with a 30-min grace (`:441`, `:788-822`), contradicting "never auto-promotes".
- `recovery_clean_windows` default 10 (`:153`) plus `min_fallback_secs = 300` (`:155`).
- Guardrails (`monitor/guardrails.rs:143-258`): window 500 (doc 50), Pass after 60 observations (doc 10), reward `ln(2/3)` (doc `ln(0.8)`), penalty severity-scaled, clamp [-5.0, 3.5] (doc [-5, 5]); the fleet log on this host showed `guard=PASS(e=14.9 med_err=0.00 cons=100% obs=215)` 5 minutes after a fresh start at Orange, 75% of the way to the alarm (20.0) with perfect median error.

These relaxations were incident-driven (a fleet that runs Enforce and cannot afford to stop reclaiming). They are legitimate design choices, but the docs describe a different product, dead enum variants suggest unfinished work, and the e-process observation is unexplained.

## Decision (recorded; operator may override)
Restore the documented safeguards as configurable behavior with defaults that keep the existing fleet unchanged: new installs get the safe defaults (Observe first, demote on breach, no auto-promotion beyond Canary); configs that set `initial_mode = "enforce"` keep today's behavior unless they opt in.

## Children
G9.1 configurable fallback actions and auto-recovery target, wiring the dead variants; G9.2 guardrail steady-Orange regression (explain or fix e=14.9); G9.3 docs regeneration and the initial_mode wizard decision.

title: G9.1: Configurable fallback actions + auto_recover_to; wire CanaryBudgetExhausted/SerializationFailure; explicit auto-promotion
description:
# G9.1 - Configurable fallback actions and recovery target; wire `CanaryBudgetExhausted` and `SerializationFailure`; make auto-promotion explicit

## Context
See G9. `PolicyConfig` (`policy.rs:114-160`): `initial_mode`, `max_canary_deletes_per_hour`, `recovery_clean_windows`, `calibration_breach_windows`, `min_fallback_secs`, `kill_switch`, guard penalty. `observe_window` (`:706-776`), `check_guard_triggers` (`:1060-1080`), `recover_from_fallback` (`:1098-1110`), `check_emergency_escalation` (`:788-822`).

## Design
- New config keys (all `[policy]`): `calibration_breach_action = "demote" | "advisory"` (default: `demote` when `initial_mode != enforce`, else `advisory`; explicit value wins), `canary_budget_action = "demote" | "keep"` (default `demote`), `serialization_failure_action = "demote" | "advisory"` (default `demote`), `auto_recover_to = "none" | "canary" | "previous"` (default `canary`), `emergency_escalation = true|false` (default: today's behavior for enforce fleets, false otherwise).

- Every transition emits `ActivityEvent::PolicyTransition { from, to, reason }` (exists? verify; add if not) and a notification at Warning.
- `sbh status` shows `policy: { mode, since, last_fallback_reason, auto_recover_to }`.

title: G9.2: Guardrail e-process — explain or fix the near-alarm (e=14.9) on a fresh daemon at steady Orange with perfect median error
description:
# G9.2 - Guardrail e-process: explain or fix the near-alarm observed on a fresh daemon at steady Orange with perfect median error

## Context
Journal on this host (2026-08-30 14:59:30, 5 minutes after start at Orange, no scans): `[SBH-SUMMARY] ... guard=PASS(e=14.9 med_err=0.00 cons=100% obs=215 clean=3)`. With `e_process_reward = 2/3` per good observation and the lower clamp at `exp(-5)`, 215 all-good observations should leave `e` near 0.0067, not 14.9 (alarm at 20.0). Either observations were bad on the TTE-conservatism axis while rate error stayed 0 (plausible at Orange with a flat rate: predicted TTE = infinity vs actual finite), or the severity-scaled penalty path (`guardrails.rs:240-258`) misfires on idle noise, or `median_rate_error` and the e-process disagree on what "good" means. An alarm would push the policy to FallbackSafe (no deletions) exactly when reclaim is needed.

## Work
1. Reproduce: unit test feeding 300 observations of `predicted_rate = 0`, `actual_rate = 0..tiny`, `predicted_tte = None/inf`, `actual_tte = finite` at Orange through `GuardrailMonitor`; print `e` trajectory; compare with the field log.
2. Decide the correct semantics with the design principle "fail conservative" in mind: idle (rate below the 10 B/s noise floor) observations must be *neutral* on TTE conservatism (no TTE can be predicted from a zero rate), not penalized; a bad TTE observation requires both a meaningful predicted rate and a materially earlier actual exhaustion.
3. Fix `GuardObservation::rate_danger_ratio`/`is_well_calibrated` accordingly; add `e_process` to `stats --json` guard history so the field can be checked later; add a `[SBH-GUARD]` line at `-v` per window with the classification reason.
4. Regression test: 1,000 steady accurate Orange observations keep `e < 1.0`; 15 truly bad observations still alarm within the documented bound.

## Files
`src/monitor/guardrails.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (verbose log), `src/logger/stats.rs`, README guardrails section (via G8.2 constants + prose).

## Success criteria
- [ ] The field pattern (idle at Orange) no longer accumulates e-process credit toward alarm; documented in CHANGELOG with the reproduction.

description:
# G10 - Observability correctness: stats as non-root, JSON schema honesty per platform, build metadata, ballast views, global flags, small ballast correctness items

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- `sbh stats --window 24h` as an unprivileged user against the root-owned system DB fails: `[SBH-2102] SQL failure in rusqlite: attempt to write a readonly database` because `SqliteLogger::open` always uses `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_WRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` (`logger/sqlite.rs:32-36`); the v0.5.1 root-DB hint only fires on `no_database` and hard-codes `/root/.local/share/sbh/activity.sqlite3` (`cli_app.rs:2439`), ignoring `/var/lib/sbh` and XDG.
- `status`/`check` JSON on Linux emits, for every mount, `platform: { darwin: { apfs: { ...all null... } } }` plus a hard-coded `free_excludes_purgeable: true` (`cli_app.rs:7101-7141` calls `capacity_platform_json()` unconditionally). Docs describe the block as a macOS feature.
- `sbh version --verbose` prints `git_sha/profile/target/timestamp = "unknown"` for every build: `emit_version` (`cli_app.rs:10076-10085`) reads `option_env!` vars that nothing sets; there is no `build.rs`; `release.yml` exports nothing.
- `ballast status --json` shows only the configured `ballast_dir` (`/var/lib/sbh/ballast`, empty on this host) and not the coordinator's per-volume pools (`/data/.sbh/ballast` has 5 files); `state.json` reports `"ballast": {"available": 5, "total": 10, "released": 5}` where the 5 "released" files were never released (they are missing on `/`).
- Global `-v`/`-q` are parsed everywhere and consulted in one command each (dashboard, lease); `--no-color` once. `[SBH-CONFIG] Using system config at ...` prints on every invocation regardless.
- Ballast: `verify()` takes no flock (`manager.rs:524`); `install.rs:230` `provision(None)` skips the free-space guard; unknown filesystem types default to random-data writes rather than probing `fallocate` (`coordinator.rs:567`).

## Children
G10.1 stats read-only + permission-aware hint; G10.2 platform JSON block per filesystem + schema version; G10.3 build metadata via build.rs; G10.4 ballast volumes view + state semantics; G10.5 global flags honored + ballast correctness items; G10.6 tests and snapshots.

title: G10.1: stats/explain/blame/log open SQLite read-only; permission-aware hint resolves the real system data dir
description:
# G10.1 - `stats`, `explain`, `blame`, `log` open the activity store read-only and give a permission-aware hint that resolves the real system data dir

## Context
See G10. `SqliteLogger::open` (`logger/sqlite.rs:32-36`) is used for both daemon writes and CLI reads. `run_stats` (`cli_app.rs:2430-2463`) hint logic. `core/config.rs:925-948` knows the platform system data dir (`/var/lib/sbh`, `/private/var/sbh`).

## Design
- `SqliteLogger::open_read_only(path)` with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX` and `immutable=0`; WAL read works for readers with directory read access; no schema creation on the read path.
- `StatsEngine`/`explain`/`blame`/`log` use the read-only opener. On `EACCES`/`readonly`/`unable to open`, the CLI resolves candidate DB paths in order: configured path, platform system data dir, XDG data dir of the invoking user, `/root/.local/share/sbh` (legacy) and reports which exists but is unreadable, with `hint: "sudo sbh stats ..."` and `root_db_path` set to the found path (not a hard-coded one). JSON error code stays SBH-2102 for genuine SQL failures; permission cases use SBH-3001 with `reason: permission_denied`.
- Human output: one line "activity database at /var/lib/sbh/activity.sqlite3 is owned by root; rerun with sudo" instead of the raw rusqlite message.

## Files
`src/logger/sqlite.rs`, `src/logger/stats.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (stats/blame/log/explain), README troubleshooting.

## Tests
- Unit: read-only open of a fixture DB succeeds and refuses writes; open of a 0o000 file yields the permission path (skip when running as root, logged).
- Unit: candidate-path resolution order with a mock platform (Linux user/system, macOS).
- Integration: `sbh stats --json` against a read-only fixture returns `hint` and `root_db_path`; exit code documented.
- e2e case in the Stats section.

title: G10.3: build.rs embeds git SHA/target/profile/reproducible timestamp; version --verbose never unknown in repo builds
description:
# G10.3 - Build metadata: `build.rs` embeds git SHA, target, profile, and a reproducible timestamp so `sbh version --verbose` is never "unknown" in repo builds

## Context
`emit_version` (`cli_app.rs:10076-10085`) reads `option_env!("TARGET")`, `("PROFILE")`, `("VERGEN_GIT_SHA" | "GIT_SHA")`, `("VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP" | "BUILD_TIMESTAMP")`. Cargo exposes `TARGET`/`PROFILE` only to build scripts, there is no `build.rs`, and `release.yml` exports nothing, so all four are always "unknown". `doctor --release` and bug reports cannot identify the build.

## Design
- `build.rs` (new, tiny, no new deps): `cargo:rustc-env=SBH_BUILD_TARGET=$TARGET`, `SBH_BUILD_PROFILE=$PROFILE`, `SBH_BUILD_GIT_SHA` from `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` (+ `-dirty` when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty; `unknown` only if git is unavailable or not a repo; honor `SBH_GIT_SHA` env override for tarball builds), `SBH_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when set (reproducible builds) else now, as RFC 3339 UTC; `cargo:rerun-if-changed=.git/HEAD` and the ref file so incremental builds refresh.
- `emit_version` reads the `SBH_BUILD_*` vars; `--json` shape unchanged (`build.git_sha` etc.); `release.yml` sets `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the tag commit time so artifacts are reproducible; provenance (G4.2) includes the same SHA.
- `rch`: the remote build runs `build.rs` on the synced tree; verify the `.git` dir is synced or set `SBH_GIT_SHA` in the rch profile (document in AGENTS.md).

## Tests
- Unit (`--bin sbh`): `version --json` fields are non-"unknown" when built in the repo (assert on `SBH_BUILD_GIT_SHA` presence at compile time via `option_env!` in the test, so tarball builds skip).
- Reproducibility: two builds with the same `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` produce identical `version --verbose` output (unit test on the formatting function).

## Success criteria
- [ ] `sbh version --verbose` on the next release shows the tag SHA, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `release`, and the tag time.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.4, closed as duplicate): fall back to `SBH_BUILD_GIT_SHA`/`SBH_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` env when git is unavailable (cargo install --git tarballs, rch remote builds).

description:
# G10.5 - Global `-v`/`-q`/`--no-color` honored everywhere; `[SBH-CONFIG]` noise gated; ballast `verify` flock; install provisioning floor; fallocate probe for unknown filesystems

## Context
- `-v`/`-q` parsed on every command (`cli_app.rs` global args) but consulted in one command each (dashboard `:4837`, lease `:7568`); `--no-color` once (`:859`). `[SBH-CONFIG] Using system config at ...` prints on every invocation to stderr (it appears in every audit transcript).
- `manager.rs:524` `verify()` has no flock while provision/release/replenish do; README says all four are serialized.
- `install.rs:230` `provision(None)` bypasses the free-space guard; G1.1 replaces the guard, this bead makes install pass the callback.
- `coordinator.rs:567` unknown fs types -> random-data strategy (slow, CPU-heavy) instead of trying `fallocate` and falling back on `EOPNOTSUPP`.

## Design
- A process-wide `Verbosity` (quiet < normal < verbose < debug) set once from `-q`/`-v` count and `SBH_LOG_LEVEL`; helper macros `sbh_info!`/`sbh_debug!` route the existing `eprintln!("[SBH-...]")` sites (mechanical by hand: `rg -n 'eprintln!\("\[SBH-' src | wc -l` sites; do it file by file, no scripts); `[SBH-CONFIG] Using ...` becomes verbose-only except when the implicit system-config fallback was chosen for root (keep that one at normal because it is a security-relevant choice; G8.3 documents it).
- `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR` applied through one `ColorMode` decision used by `colored` and the TUI theme.
- `verify()` takes the shared lock; `install` builds an `FsStatsCollector` and passes the floor callback; coordinator strategy: `Fallocate` for known-good types, `ProbeFallocate` for unknown (try, fall back to random on error), `RandomData` for CoW.

## Tests
- Unit: verbosity gating of a representative info line; `-q` suppresses `[SBH-CONFIG]`; `-vv` enables debug lines.
- Unit (`manager.rs`): `verify` contends with `provision` on the lock (thread test).
- Unit (`coordinator.rs`): unknown fs -> probe path chosen; mock PAL `preallocate_file` failure -> random fallback logged.
- e2e: `sbh -q status --json` emits pure JSON with empty stderr.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `sbh -q <any> --json` produces no stderr on a healthy host.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.4 narrowed, bd-rc-master-ajg1.9.1 narrowed): the verify() flock and install floor callback are owned here; the exit-code/stream contract (C-EXIT: 0 ok, 1 user/pressure, 2 runtime, 3 internal, 4 partial; clean/emergency return 4 on any failed item; check pressure -> 1; reports to stdout, diagnostics to stderr) stays in bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.4.

# G11.2 - `sbh scan --ab PATH` produces the design-doc section 7 comparison artifact in one command; `stats` reports scanner CPU-seconds per day

## Context
The A/B procedure in docs/scanner-redesign-event-driven.md (run twice with `SBH_SCANNER_ENGINE=v1|v2`, archive both JSONs and matching daemon `scan_complete` events, compare `scanned_entries`, `process_cpu_micros`, candidates, vetoes) is manual, so it was done once on one small tree. `scan --json` already emits `scanner_engine`, `scanner_dispatch`, `opaque_pruning`, `opaque_pruned_dirs`, `scanned_entries`, `process_cpu_micros`; daemon `scan_complete` events carry the same plus index/event metrics.

- `sbh scan --ab [--top N] [--min-score S] [--out FILE] PATH...`: runs v1 then v2 in-process (fresh engine per run, page cache warmed by a first untimed v2 pass so both runs see the same cache state), captures per-run `{engine, dispatch, scanned_entries, opaque_pruned_dirs, elapsed_seconds, process_cpu_micros, candidates: [{path, score, action, vetoes}]}` and a diff: `only_in_v1`, `only_in_v2`, `v2_candidates_vetoed_by_v1` (the promotion blocker from section 7: must be empty), `cpu_ratio`, `entries_ratio`. title: G2: Explainability — persist decision records and ship sbh explain
description:
# G2 - Explainability: persist decision records and ship `sbh explain`

## Background
Design principle 4 in README and AGENTS.md: "Explainability is mandatory: every action has traceable evidence and rationale." The README headline table promises "Evidence ledger + `sbh explain` shows why each action happened", the architecture diagram has an "Evidence Ledger + Explain API" box, the Quick Example runs `sbh explain --id <decision-id>`, and the FAQ says to use it to audit deletions. Reality (2026-09-01 audit): `sbh explain` is an unrecognized subcommand. `scanner/decision_record.rs` defines `DecisionRecord` with four explain levels (24 tests); `daemon/policy.rs:478-679` builds one per decision; `daemon/loop_main.rs:5585-5589` reads only `approved_for_deletion` and `mode` and drops the record. No `ActivityEvent` carries it (`logger/dual.rs:48-116`), no SQLite table stores it, nothing persists it. `scan --explain` prints factors inline without an ID. The evidence ledger is a type, not a store.

## Goal
Every policy decision (daemon, and manual `clean`) is persisted with a stable ID and can be retrieved and explained at four levels; emergency mode prints but never writes (zero-write invariant).

## Design (children carry the detail)
- G2.1: decision IDs (12-hex prefix of SHA-256 over path, device, inode, decision-time bucket, mode), `ActivityEvent::DecisionRecorded`, SQLite `decisions` table, JSONL echo, retention prune, stats aggregates.
- G2.2: `sbh explain --id/--path/--last [--level 1..4] [--json]`; IDs surfaced in `scan --explain`, `clean`, notifications, `scan_complete`/`deletion` events.
- G2.3: tests (unit, integration, e2e) including the emergency zero-write assertion and JSON schema documentation.

## Why the ID scheme
Content-addressed IDs are reproducible across daemon and CLI runs for the same candidate epoch, short enough to paste, and change when a directory is recreated (inode) so "why was this deleted twice" is answerable.

## Acceptance
`sbh explain --id` on a real daemon decision returns the record; dashboard Explainability screen (G5) reads the same table.
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.3 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G2.1: Decision IDs, DecisionRecorded event, SQLite decisions table, JSONL echo, retention, stats aggregates
description:
# G2.1 - Decision IDs, `DecisionRecorded` activity event, SQLite `decisions` table, JSONL echo, retention, stats aggregates

## Context
`scanner/decision_record.rs` has `DecisionRecord { path, factors, posterior, keep_loss, delete_loss, uncertainty, guard_status, vetoes, mode, action, explain levels }` and `format_explain(level)`. `daemon/policy.rs:478-679` builds it inside `decide()`. `loop_main.rs:5585-5589` discards it. `logger/dual.rs` `ActivityEvent` has no decision variant; `logger/sqlite.rs:375-414` creates three tables (`activity_log`, `pressure_history`, `ballast_inventory`); `dual.rs:231-233` prunes rows older than 30 days every 3,600 events.

## Design
- `DecisionRecord::id(&self) -> DecisionId`: `sha256(path_bytes || dev || ino || (decided_at.unix_secs / 60) || mode as u8)[..6]` hex (12 chars). Add `device_id`, `inode`, `decided_at`, `outcome: Option<DecisionOutcome { executed, freed_bytes, error, at }>` fields (serde default).
- `ActivityEvent::DecisionRecorded(Box<DecisionRecord>)` and `ActivityEvent::DecisionOutcome { id, outcome }`; `DualLogger` writes both to SQLite and JSONL (JSONL line `{"event":"decision_recorded", ...}`); the logger channel stays bounded (records are small; factors JSON < 4 KiB).
- SQLite: `decisions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ts INTEGER, path TEXT, dev INTEGER, ino INTEGER, mode TEXT, action TEXT, posterior REAL, keep_loss REAL, delete_loss REAL, uncertainty REAL, guard_status TEXT, vetoes TEXT /*json*/, factors TEXT /*json*/, explain_l1 TEXT, explain_l2 TEXT, explain_l3 TEXT, explain_l4 TEXT, outcome TEXT /*json*/)` with indexes on `ts` and `path`; schema migration is additive (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), version bump in the existing schema table if present. Prune with the same 30-day retention.
- `logger/stats.rs`: `decisions_by_action(window)`, `top_veto_reasons(window, n)`, `decisions_for_path(path, n)`, `decision_by_id(id)`, `recent_decisions(n)`.
- Daemon: `loop_main.rs` emits `DecisionRecorded` for every candidate decision (Delete, Keep, Review), then `DecisionOutcome` after the executor reports; the executor's `DeletionBatch` entries carry the ID so the outcome can be joined.
- Manual `clean`: same path via the shared planner; `emergency`: builds records, prints IDs and level-1 explanations, logs nothing (guarded by the existing zero-write mode flag; add an assertion helper that the logger is a `NullLogger` in emergency).
- Notifications: `CleanupCompleted` carries the top decision IDs; webhook template placeholder `${DECISION_IDS}`.

## Files
`src/scanner/decision_record.rs`, `src/logger/{dual,sqlite,jsonl,stats}.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/daemon/policy.rs` (return the record, not just approval), `src/scanner/deletion.rs` (ID on batch entries), `src/daemon/notifications.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (`clean`/`emergency` paths), docs/testing-and-logging.md (JSONL schema).

## Tests
- Unit: ID determinism (same inputs -> same ID; inode change -> different ID; minute bucket boundary documented).
- Unit (`dual.rs`): round-trip `DecisionRecorded` + `DecisionOutcome` to SQLite and JSONL; prune removes old rows; a full channel drops and counts.
- Unit (`stats.rs`): aggregates over a fixture DB.
- Unit (`policy.rs`): `decide()` returns the record for Delete/Keep/Review.
- Integration: daemon loop with mock PAL produces `scan_complete` details listing decision IDs and the DB contains matching rows with outcomes after execution.
- Integration: `sbh emergency --yes` against a fixture leaves DB and JSONL byte sizes unchanged while stdout contains IDs.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `select count(*) from decisions` grows during a daemon run; `stats --json` shows `decisions_by_action`.
- [ ] Zero-write invariant test green.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.3.1, closed as duplicate): alternative id scheme considered — `<run_id>-<seq:08>` with a random base32 run_id minted at daemon start and `cli-<token>` for CLI runs; the content-hash scheme here is fine as long as ids are unique across daemon restarts (verify the minute bucket). Add `[telemetry] log_decisions_jsonl` (default true) to bound JSONL growth. bd-rc-master-ajg1.3.4 (regret labels + conformal risk control of per-category thresholds) depends on this bead and adds a `decision_outcome` regret notion: identity recreated within 30 min while a process with cwd/open files under the parent is alive.

title: G2.2: sbh explain --id/--path/--last and decision IDs in scan/clean/events/notifications
description:
# G2.2 - `sbh explain` command and decision IDs everywhere a decision is shown

## Context
README L60/L406/L1766/L1848 and AGENTS.md L379 document `sbh explain --id <decision-id>`; the binary has no such command (`cli_app.rs:110-162` command enum). `scan --explain` prints scoring factors but no ID; `clean` output has no ID; notifications carry none.

## Design
- `Command::Explain(ExplainArgs { id: Option<String>, path: Option<PathBuf>, last: Option<usize>, level: u8 /*1..4, default 2*/, json: bool })`. Exactly one of `--id/--path/--last` required (clap group). Output: human (the existing `format_explain(level)` text plus outcome line) or JSON (the full record). Exit 3 when the ID is unknown, with a hint to `sbh explain --last 20`.
- Data source: `StatsEngine` queries from G2.1 over the configured SQLite path; when the DB is root-owned and unreadable, reuse the G10.1 permission-aware hint (`sudo sbh explain ...`). Fallback: scan the JSONL tail for `decision_recorded` lines when SQLite is disabled (degradation chain).
- IDs surfaced: `scan --explain` and `scan --json` candidates gain `decision_id` (computed with the same function even when not persisted, so operators can correlate a preview with a later daemon decision); `clean` prints `id` per action; `deletion` and `scan_complete` activity events carry `decision_ids`; human `status` "Recent Activity" shows IDs.
- Shell completion: `explain` added; `sbh --help` lists it (doc-parity test in G8 will enforce README/AGENTS tables).

`src/cli_app.rs` (enum, args, handler, scan/clean output), `src/logger/stats.rs` (queries), `src/scanner/decision_record.rs` (`format_explain` outcome line), README/AGENTS command tables, CHANGELOG.

title: G3: systemd lifecycle honesty — READY=1, coordinated shutdown, self-monitor truth, unit drift
description:
# G3 - systemd lifecycle honesty: READY=1, coordinated shutdown, self-monitor truth, unit drift detection

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs:120-124` emits `Type=notify` + `WatchdogSec=60` for system-scope units; `sd_notify_linux` (`:339-347`) sends only `WATCHDOG=1\nSTATUS=...` over a `UnixDatagram`. There is no `READY=1`, `STOPPING=1`, or `MAINPID=` anywhere (`rg READY=1 src tests` -> 0). With `Type=notify`, systemd keeps the unit in `activating` until READY=1 and kills it at `TimeoutStartSec` (default 90 s), then `Restart=on-failure` loops. No test starts a real unit; the unit on this host is a hand-written `Type=simple` file, which is presumably why nobody noticed.
- Abstract `NOTIFY_SOCKET` paths (`@...`) are not handled; send errors are silently discarded.
- Shutdown (`loop_main.rs:3597-3640`): shutdown flag checked at the top of the loop (no "complete current cycle"), no final `state.json` write, worker join timeout 5 s (`WORKER_SHUTDOWN_JOIN_TIMEOUT`), logger joined unbounded. `ShutdownCoordinator` (`signals.rs:160-195`, 30 s) is dead code with tests. README L1440-1445 describes a different sequence.
- Self-monitor (`self_monitor.rs`): only scanner and executor heartbeat (`loop_main.rs:1767-1768`); `ThreadStatus::Dead` is never produced; stall threshold passed is 10 s (README says 60 s); README says thread statuses are in the state file (they are not; the TUI Diagnostics screen therefore has nothing to show).
- Unit drift: bootstrap only detects a stale `ExecStart` binary; the hardened directives (Nice, IOSchedulingClass, ProtectSystem, MemoryMax, CPUQuota, WatchdogSec) are not verified against the installed unit; operator drop-ins and `Condition*` gates are invisible to `doctor`.

## Goal
A system-scope install starts and stays `active` under systemd's own supervision; shutdown leaves a truthful final state; the self-monitor reports all workers; `doctor` can tell an operator that the installed unit is not the one sbh generates.

## Children
G3.1 sd_notify protocol + unit text; G3.2 shutdown + self-monitor; G3.3 unit drift in doctor; G3.4 tests (fake NOTIFY_SOCKET, opt-in `systemd-run` transient unit, state schema).
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.6 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G3.1: sd_notify READY=1/STOPPING=1/STATUS/MAINPID, abstract sockets, TimeoutStartSec, single unit generator
description:
# G3.1 - sd_notify protocol: READY=1 after startup, STOPPING=1 on shutdown, STATUS= updates, MAINPID, abstract sockets, TimeoutStartSec

## Context
See G3. `systemd.rs:316-347`: `systemd_notify_socket()`, `systemd_watchdog_enabled()`, `sd_notify_watchdog()` -> `sd_notify_linux(status, socket_path)` sends `WATCHDOG=1\nSTATUS={status}\n` via `UnixDatagram::unbound().send_to`. Heartbeat cadence `watchdog_sec/2` from `signals.rs:230`, called at `loop_main.rs:2306`.

## Design
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs`: `pub struct SdNotify { socket: Option<UnixDatagram>, target: SocketTarget }` with `SocketTarget::{Path(PathBuf), Abstract(Vec<u8>)}` parsed from `NOTIFY_SOCKET` (`@` prefix -> abstract; use `std::os::linux::net::SocketAddrExt::from_abstract_name`). Methods: `ready()` -> `READY=1\nMAINPID=<pid>\n`, `stopping()` -> `STOPPING=1\n`, `status(&str)`, `watchdog()` -> `WATCHDOG=1\n`, `errno(i32)` on fatal startup errors. First send failure logged once at `[SBH-DAEMON] sd_notify unavailable: <err>`; subsequent failures counted in self-monitor diagnostics.
- `loop_main.rs`: call `ready()` after config load, PAL detection, lock acquisition (G1.3), worker spawn, and the first successful state write; call `status()` with a compact pressure summary every state write; `stopping()` at the start of shutdown.
- Unit text: system scope adds `TimeoutStartSec=30` and keeps `Type=notify`/`WatchdogSec=60`; user scope unchanged (`Type=simple`). `NotifyAccess=main` explicit.
- README service section regenerated from the unit template (G8).

## Files
`src/daemon/service/systemd.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/daemon/signals.rs` (heartbeat uses the new type), `src/daemon/service.rs` (unit text duplicate at `:444-449` must be unified with `systemd.rs:120-124`; one generator), README.

## Tests
- Unit: parse `NOTIFY_SOCKET` path and abstract forms; a bound `UnixDatagram` in a temp dir receives `READY=1` + `MAINPID=` first, then `WATCHDOG=1`, then `STOPPING=1`, in order, from a `DaemonLoop` driven for two ticks with a mock PAL; abstract-socket variant on Linux.
- Unit: unit text contains `TimeoutStartSec=30` and `NotifyAccess=main` for system scope, neither for user scope; snapshot (`insta`) of both unit files.
- Integration (Linux, opt-in `SBH_SYSTEMD_TESTS=1`, non-root via `systemd-run --user` when a user manager exists): transient `Type=notify` unit running the built `sbh daemon` reaches `active` within 10 s and stays active for 30 s; skipped with a logged reason otherwise (G3.4 owns the harness).

## Success criteria

notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.6.1, closed as duplicate): parse `WATCHDOG_USEC`/`WATCHDOG_PID` at startup and heartbeat at half the interval (keep `--watchdog-sec` as override); the generated unit's `ExecStart={binary} daemon` currently passes no `--watchdog-sec` so heartbeats are disabled today. bd-rc-master-ajg1.6.2 (ReadWritePaths derived from config: root_paths, special locations, every ballast dir incl. <mount>/.sbh/ballast, data/config dirs; re-rendered on install/config set/bootstrap; unit snapshot test) is related.

title: G3.2: Coordinated shutdown with final state write; heartbeats for all workers; real Dead status; threads in state.json
description:
# G3.2 - Coordinated shutdown with a final state write; self-monitor heartbeats for all workers and a real `Dead` status; thread statuses in state.json

## Context
See G3. `loop_main.rs:3597-3640` `shutdown()`: drops senders, `join_worker_with_timeout(5 s)` per worker, logger joined without bound; no final `state.json`. `signals.rs:160-195` `ShutdownCoordinator` unused. `self_monitor.rs:176-197` `status()` returns Running/Stalled only; heartbeats registered for scanner+executor only (`loop_main.rs:1767-1768`); `THREAD_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10 s` used as the stall threshold; `DaemonState` (`self_monitor.rs:50-61`) has no thread field.

## Design
- Shutdown sequence (documented in README exactly as implemented): (1) set flag + `sd_notify STOPPING=1`; (2) finish the in-flight tick (move the flag check to after the tick's act phase, bounded by the tick's own budget); (3) drop channel senders; (4) join workers with `shutdown_join_budget = min(config.daemon.shutdown_join_secs, TimeoutStopSec - 5)` (default 25 s) split across workers; (5) write final `state.json` with `shutdown_at`, `shutdown_reason`, `clean_exit: true`; (6) release `daemon.lock`; (7) exit 0. `ShutdownCoordinator`: DECISION for the operator: wire it as the implementation of steps 3-4 (preferred; it exists and is tested) or remove it. The bead implements the wiring; removal needs explicit permission.
- Self-monitor: heartbeat handles for monitor, scanner, executor, logger, and the memory-pressure thread; `ThreadStatus::Dead { error }` produced when the supervisor observes a finished join handle that was not respawned (`loop_main.rs:2387-2451` respawn path); stall threshold = `max(3 * tick_interval, 30 s)` documented as a constant `THREAD_STALL_THRESHOLD`.
- `DaemonState` gains `threads: Vec<ThreadHealth { name, status, last_heartbeat_age_ms, restarts }>` (serde default; empty for old daemons) so the TUI Diagnostics screen (G5.4) and `status --json` can show them.

## Files
`src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/daemon/signals.rs`, `src/daemon/self_monitor.rs`, `src/core/config.rs` (`daemon.shutdown_join_secs`), `src/cli_app.rs` (`status` prints thread health), README daemon/self-monitor sections.

## Tests
- Unit: shutdown writes `state.json` with `shutdown_at` and `clean_exit`; lock released after write (probe succeeds).
- Unit: a worker that panics past the respawn limit yields `Dead` with the panic message in the next state write.
- Unit: heartbeat staleness -> `Stalled` at the documented threshold for each of the five workers.
- Unit (`self_monitor.rs`): `DaemonState` JSON with and without `threads` deserializes (schema-default).
- Integration: SIGTERM to a running `sbh daemon` (binary) exits 0 within `shutdown_join_secs + 2`, and the final state has `clean_exit=true`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] README shutdown sequence and thread table are regenerated from constants and match tests.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.6.3, closed as duplicate): stall threshold should be the documented 60 s (code passes THREAD_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10 s); the scanner heartbeats only per request so an idle scanner reads Stalled; `ThreadStatus::Dead` only when the respawn budget is exhausted; align the worker join budget with the unit's TimeoutStopSec=30 (or document 5 s); write `stopped_at`/`exit_reason` in the final state. Removing `ShutdownCoordinator` (dead code) requires operator permission per AGENTS.md rule 1; mark `#[deprecated]` until then.
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.6.3 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G3.3: doctor --service unit drift detection (systemd + launchd) and service reinstall-unit
description:
# G3.3 - Unit drift detection: `doctor --service` compares the installed systemd unit (and launchd plist) with what sbh generates; `service reinstall-unit` remediation

## Context
On this host `/etc/systemd/system/sbh.service` is a hand-written `Type=simple` unit with none of the documented hardening (no Nice/IOSchedulingClass/ProtectSystem/MemoryMax/WatchdogSec), plus drop-ins (`10-scanner-v2.conf` env, `hotloop-guard.conf` and `zz-hotloop-disabled.conf` Condition gates, `system.control/50-CPUQuota.conf` etc.). `cli/bootstrap.rs:958-978` detects only a stale `ExecStart` binary (`SystemdUnitStaleBinary`). Nothing tells the operator the unit is not sbh's. README L1485-1515 describes the hardened unit as if it were what runs.

## Design
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs`: `UnitDrift::compute(installed_text, generated_text, dropins: &[(path, text)]) -> DriftReport { missing_directives, changed_directives, foreign_dropins, condition_gates, exec_start_matches }` using a simple `[Section] key=value` parser (multi-value keys like `ReadWritePaths` compared as sets).
- `doctor --service` (new flag; `--pal` on macOS does the plist equivalent via `launchd.rs`): PASS when no drift; WARN for foreign drop-ins that only add limits; FAIL for missing hardening directives, a different `Type=`, or a Condition gate currently disabling the unit. Remediation text: `sudo sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit` and, for gates, the exact path.
- `sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit [--keep-dropins]`: backs up the installed unit (`.bak-<stamp>` like the writeback snippet), writes the generated one, `daemon-reload`, prints the diff; never touches drop-ins unless `--purge-dropins` (explicit).
- Bootstrap (G6.1) gains `MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift` reusing `UnitDrift`.

## Files
`src/daemon/service/systemd.rs`, `src/daemon/service/launchd.rs` (plist compare), `src/cli_app.rs` (doctor/service), `src/cli/bootstrap.rs`, README doctor/service sections.

## Tests
- Unit: drift on fixtures (this host's unit + drop-ins captured as test data) reports the exact missing directives and both Condition gates; identical text -> no drift; set semantics for `ReadWritePaths`.
- Unit: `reinstall-unit` on a temp unit dir writes backup + new unit and preserves drop-ins.
- Integration: `sbh doctor --service --json` against a fixture unit dir (`SBH_SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR` override for tests) FAILs with the expected ids.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh doctor --service` FAILs today (hand-written unit + gate) and PASSes after G0 step 3.

title: G4: Release contract — one source of truth for assets, checksums, provenance, updater, installers, workflow, tap
description:
# G4 - Release contract: one source of truth for asset names, checksums, provenance, updater, installers, workflow, and Homebrew tap

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- Three asset naming schemes coexist: `release.yml` emits `sbh-v{tag}-{triple}.tar.xz` + `.sha256` + `SHA256SUMS.txt` + `release-provenance.json`; the legacy scheme is `sbh-{triple}.tar.xz`; the v0.5.0/v0.5.1 releases were hand-published (no workflow run exists for those tags) with raw binaries `sbh_linux_amd64`, `sbh_linux_arm64`, `sbh_darwin_amd64`, `sbh_darwin_arm64` and one aggregate `SHA256SUMS`.
- `scripts/install.sh:398-535` probes versioned -> legacy -> raw; root `install.sh` (91 lines, a different file) knows only raw; `src/cli/mod.rs:263-275` (`ReleaseArtifactContract::asset_name_for_tag`) and `update.rs:1096-1102` know only the first two. `curl -I` on `.../v0.5.1/sbh-v0.5.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz` -> 404; `.../sbh_linux_amd64` -> 200. So `sbh update` (apply) is broken for every v0.5.x user the moment a newer release appears; `--check` passes only because the binary is current.
- Updater `curl` calls (`update.rs:1178-1204`) send no User-Agent; AGENTS.md requires `OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0` on every web request.
- `release.yml` last succeeded for v0.4.28 (2026-06-08); the 12 later tag runs failed or were cancelled; all three workflows are `disabled_manually`; the Homebrew tap `Dicklesworthstone/homebrew-sbh` formula is at v0.4.28; the in-repo `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` holds v0.4.8 placeholder hashes.
- `SigstorePolicy::Optional` is unreachable in product code; checksum parsing handles GNU `hash  file` but not BSD `SHA256 (file) = hash`; no cosign step exists in the workflow although `cli/mod.rs:1098` models a `.sigstore.json` asset.
- bd-t951 (open) covers only a post-publish asset audit.

## Goal
The updater, both installers, the release workflow, the provenance manifest, and the tap formula are generated from or validated against one Rust `ReleaseContract`, so a naming change in one place cannot silently break another; the updater resolves today's live release; every web request carries the required User-Agent.

## Children
G4.1 `ReleaseContract` module + updater + UA; G4.2 installers/workflow/formula/tap consume it + asset audit job (absorbs bd-t951); G4.3 doctor --release drift + network/static tests; G4.4 external operator actions (re-enable workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, tap update, branch protection).
close_reason: Merged into the canonical tree bd-rc-master-ajg1 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; counterpart linked as related; description retained for reference)

title: G4.1: ReleaseContract module; updater resolves live release assets (raw + tarball + provenance); User-Agent on every request
description:
# G4.1 - `ReleaseContract` module: ordered asset schemes, checksum layouts, provenance manifest; updater resolves the live release; User-Agent on every request

## Context
See G4. `src/cli/mod.rs` `ReleaseArtifactContract` (`:230-330`) knows `Tag`/`Latest` locators and one tarball naming; `update.rs:1096-1102` builds download URLs; `update.rs:1178-1185` fetches `releases/latest` JSON with `curl -sL`; `assets.rs` verifies sha256 via `.sha256` sidecars; `mod.rs:640-658` checksum parser takes the first whitespace token.

## Design
- New `src/cli/release_contract.rs` (genuinely new functionality; `mod.rs` shrinks): `ReleaseContract { schemes: Vec<AssetScheme>, checksum_sources: Vec<ChecksumSource>, provenance_name: "release-provenance.json", signature_scheme: Option<...> }`. `AssetScheme::{VersionedTarXz, LegacyTarXz, RawBinary}` each with `name_for(tag, target) -> String`, `archive: Archive::{TarXz, None}`, and `checksum: ChecksumSource::{Sidecar(".sha256"), Aggregate("SHA256SUMS"), Aggregate("SHA256SUMS.txt")}`. Target mapping `Triple <-> {os}_{arch}` (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` <-> `linux_amd64`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` <-> `linux_arm64`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` <-> `darwin_amd64`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` <-> `darwin_arm64`). `contract.resolve(release_assets: &[AssetName], tag, target) -> Resolved { scheme, asset, checksum_source }` picks the first scheme whose asset exists in the release's asset list (from the GitHub API JSON already fetched), instead of guessing a URL.
- Provenance-first: if `release-provenance.json` exists in the release, parse it (`assets[] { name, target, sha256, archive, signature: Option<{ kind: "sigstore"|"codesign"|"notarized", ref } > , built_from: sha }`) and use it as the authoritative map; fall back to scheme probing when absent (v0.5.x). The workflow (G4.2) emits this manifest.
- Checksums: parse sidecar hex, GNU aggregate `hash␠␠name`, BSD `SHA256 (name) = hash`; aggregate lookups match on basename.
- Updater (`update.rs`): use `contract.resolve`; extract tarballs as before; for `RawBinary` install the file directly with mode 0o755; keep backup/rollback flow; `sbh update --check --force --dry-run` reports the resolved asset and its HTTP status without downloading.
- User-Agent: a single `http::fetch(url, opts)` helper in `cli/mod.rs` that adds `-A "OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0"` to every `curl` invocation (updater, assets, install from-source, `doctor --release`); grep-based test forbids raw `curl` `Command::new` outside the helper.
- `sbh release-contract --json` prints the contract (schemes in order, mapping table, checksum sources) for consumption by `scripts/install.sh` generation and CI validation (G4.2).

## Files
`src/cli/release_contract.rs` (new), `src/cli/mod.rs`, `src/cli/update.rs`, `src/cli/assets.rs`, `src/cli/from_source.rs` (UA), `src/cli_app.rs` (`release-contract` subcommand, `update --check --force --dry-run` output), README update section.

## Tests
- Unit: `resolve` over the exact asset lists of v0.4.28 (tarballs + sidecars + provenance), v0.4.40 (mixed, typo asset present), v0.5.1 (raw + SHA256SUMS) fixtures captured from `gh release view --json assets`; all four targets resolve for each; provenance preferred when present.
- Unit: checksum parsers for the three layouts; aggregate basename matching; BSD form.
- Unit: UA helper adds the header; grep test over `src/cli/**` for `Command::new("curl")` outside `http::fetch`.
- Network (opt-in `SBH_NET_TESTS=1`): `sbh update --check --force --dry-run --json` against the live latest release resolves an asset with HTTP 200 for the host target.
- Integration (`tests/installer_e2e.rs`): offline bundle path still works with the new resolver.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Against the v0.5.1 release fixture, resolution yields `sbh_linux_amd64` + `SHA256SUMS`, not a 404 tarball name.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.1, closed as duplicate): resolution order when the API is unreachable — HEAD probes of releases/download/<tag>/<name> in contract order, then the offline manifest; checksum mandatory for both schemes; sigstore Required when a bundle exists. Test matrix for a local fake release server: tarball-only, raw-only, mixed, checksum mismatch (Deny), missing sigstore with Required (Deny), offline manifest. Observed: `sbh update --version v0.5.0 --dry-run` on the operator host resolved sbh-v0.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz (404).
close_reason: Merged into bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.1 (dedupe of the two parallel 2026-09 reality-check trees; this bead's description is retained for reference)

title: G4.2: Installers, release.yml, formula, and tap consume the contract; publish both schemes + provenance; asset audit job (absorbs bd-t951)
description:
# G4.2 - Installers, release workflow, Homebrew formula, and tap consume the ReleaseContract; publish both tarball and raw schemes; asset audit job (absorbs bd-t951)

## Context
See G4. `scripts/install.sh` hand-codes three probe strategies (`:398-535`); root `install.sh` hand-codes one; `release.yml` (596 lines) names assets at `:330-332`, verifies tarball arch (`:341-381`, bd-t951 guard), writes `release-provenance.json` (`:456-464`), and updates the tap (`:476-580`) by grepping `sbh-v${version}-{aarch64,x86_64}-apple-darwin.tar.xz`; `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` has v0.4.8 placeholders; `cert-expiration.yml` exists. CI/release both still run a dead "Strip local-only TUI path deps" `sed` step (`ci.yml:39-43`, `release.yml:82-88`).

## Design
- `scripts/install.sh`: the probe table becomes a generated block between `# BEGIN sbh-release-contract` / `# END` markers, produced by `sbh release-contract --shell` and checked by a static test (`cli/mod.rs` already has installer-contract tests at `:2600-2650`; extend them to compare against the contract). Root `install.sh`: DECISION for the operator: (a) replace with a 5-line shim that `exec`s `scripts/install.sh` fetched from the same ref, or (b) remove. Default action: shim (no deletion).
- `release.yml`: matrix names come from `cargo run -- release-contract --json` (built once in the quality-gate job); publish BOTH `sbh-v{tag}-{triple}.tar.xz` (+ `.sha256`) and `sbh_{os}_{arch}` raw binaries plus one `SHA256SUMS`, plus `release-provenance.json` listing every asset with target, sha256, archive kind, signature/notarization status, and `built_from`. The bd-t951 arch check runs for both schemes. Remove the dead path-dep `sed` step. Add a final `asset-audit` job that downloads the published assets with `gh release download`, recomputes hashes, validates against provenance, and fails the workflow on drift (bd-t951 follow-up items 2-3).
- Homebrew: formula template renders from the contract (URLs for the two darwin tarballs, sha256 from provenance); the tap job pushes only when provenance validates; `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` keeps placeholder markers but the placeholder version is bumped to the current contract shape and documented as a template in the file header.
- `cert-expiration.yml`: unchanged, but `doctor --release` (G4.3) surfaces its last result.
- CHANGELOG: document the dual scheme and that v0.5.0/v0.5.1 were hand-published.

## Files
`scripts/install.sh`, `install.sh` (shim or decision), `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (dead step), `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb`, `src/cli/mod.rs` (installer contract tests), docs/installer-dx-parity-matrix.md.

## Tests
- Static: installer generated block == `sbh release-contract --shell` output (test regenerates and diffs).
- Static: `release.yml` asset names for every matrix entry match `contract.schemes[*].name_for` (parse the YAML in a test with a minimal reader or string search on the generated names).
- Workflow dry-run: `act`-style local run is out of scope; instead a `release-audit` unit test validates a fixture provenance against a fixture asset list.
- Formula: `brew style`/`ruby -c` in the existing `homebrew-formula` CI job against the rendered formula.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Next tag after re-enable publishes both schemes + provenance and the tap updates automatically.
- [ ] bd-t951 closed as absorbed with a pointer here.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.2, closed as duplicate): release builds must use `--features tui` (G5.1); add a `git push origin main main:master` mirror step (AGENTS.md); re-enable cert-expiration.yml; v0.5.1 macOS assets are ad-hoc (arm64: CodeDirectory only, flags 0x20002) / unsigned (amd64) so the next release must restore Developer ID + notarization inside the tarball. bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.5 (cut v0.5.2 through the workflow; verify `sbh update` 0.5.1->0.5.2 on the operator host, one rch VPS, one Mac; close bd-t951) depends on this bead and on G4.4.

# G4.3 - `doctor --release` drift checks and release-contract test suite (static, fixture, network-gated)

## Context

title: G4.4: External operator actions — re-enable workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, tap update, branch protection
description:
# G4.4 - External operator actions: re-enable the three GitHub workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, update the tap, add branch protection

## Why a bead
These steps need the operator's GitHub permissions and judgment; agents cannot (and must not) perform them. Tracking them here keeps the release-contract work honest: without them, G4.1-G4.3 are code without a shipped effect.

## Facts (2026-09-01)
- `gh workflow list --all`: CI (234441116), Release (234441117), Developer ID Certificate Expiration (273476379) are all `disabled_manually`. Last run of any kind: 2026-08-16 (CI, failed on clippy) / 2026-08-20 (cert check, passed).
- `main` has no branch protection and no rulesets (`gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection` -> 404).
- Latest release v0.5.1 (2026-08-26): raw binaries + `SHA256SUMS` only; no workflow run for the tag; signing/notarization unproven.

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)

The shipped `sbh dashboard` (0.5.1, in a pty) prints `sbh: TUI feature not enabled. Rebuild with --features tui` and exits 2; `--new-dashboard` same; `--legacy-dashboard` is `run_live_status_loop` (the `status --watch` loop). `--start-screen` (README L432) does not exist.
- The gate was introduced on 2026-06-13 (`0f534d8`, sbh#12) because `/dp/frankentui` path deps broke `cargo install --git`; the deps have since been git-tag deps (`v0.4.1`), so the reason is gone. `cargo check --features tui --all-targets` compiles today (verified 2026-09-02, 15 m 44 s cold build, exit 0).

title: G5.2: Ballast screen actions execute — confirmation Enter handler, release/replenish executor, toasts, events
description:
# G5.2 - Ballast screen actions execute: confirmation Enter handler, release/replenish executor, result toasts, activity events

## Context
`tui/update.rs:401-410` opens `Overlay::Confirmation(ConfirmAction::BallastRelease)` on `x`; `tui/render.rs:3592-3630` draws "Enter Confirm"; `tui/input.rs:206-251` `resolve_overlay_key` has no Enter arm for `Confirmation` -> `consumed_without_action()`; no code anywhere in `src/tui` calls `BallastManager`/coordinator. `handle_ballast_key` (`update.rs:556-583`) only navigates. README L461/L471/L492 promise release/replenish controls and a one-keystroke quick-release.

## Design
- Elm-style: `Msg::ConfirmOverlay` -> `Cmd::Ballast(BallastCmd::{ReleaseOne(volume), ReleaseAll(volume), Replenish(volume)})`; the runtime executes commands on a worker thread (never on the render thread) through a `DashboardActions` trait implemented by `BallastCoordinator` (same flock and safety path as the CLI: `manager.release(n)` / `replenish_one()`), returning `Msg::BallastResult { volume, outcome }`. Model shows a toast (success: bytes freed; failure: error text) and refreshes the ballast telemetry.
- Overlay keys: `Enter`/`y` confirm, `Esc`/`n` cancel; confirmation text names the volume and file count; a second confirmation for ReleaseAll.
- Activity event: `ActivityEvent::BallastReleased { source: "dashboard" }` so `stats`/timeline attribute it; decision ID not applicable.
- Degraded mode (no daemon/state): actions still work (the coordinator is CLI-side), but the toast warns that the daemon will not replenish until it runs.
- Tests-first: `DashboardActions` has a mock in `tui/test_harness.rs`.

## Files
`src/tui/{model,update,input,render,runtime}.rs`, `src/tui/test_harness.rs`, `src/ballast/coordinator.rs` (trait impl), `src/logger/dual.rs` (event source field), README dashboard section.

## Tests
- Unit (`tui/update.rs`): `x` -> overlay; Enter -> `Cmd::Ballast(ReleaseOne)`; result message -> toast + telemetry refresh; Esc cancels; ReleaseAll requires the second confirmation.
- Unit (`tui/runtime.rs`): command executes on the worker thread and delivers the result message; failure path.
- Scenario drill (`tui/test_scenario_drills.rs`): "quick-release under Red" end to end with the mock actions.
- Integration (`tests/dashboard_integration_tests.rs`, tui-gated): real coordinator on a temp pool: release one file via the action trait; inventory decreases; flock respected (concurrent CLI release does not corrupt).

## Success criteria

title: G5.3: LogSearch query line, filters over SQLite/JSONL adapters, pagination
description:
# G5.3 - LogSearch screen: query line, filters over SQLite/JSONL adapters, pagination

## Context
`tui/render.rs` `frame_log_search_header_styled` renders `query <not-yet-editable>`; `render_log_search` prints `mode=timeline-mirror` and "Timeline telemetry powers this preview."; `update.rs:454-463` has no LogSearch key arm; only mouse click/scroll (`:739-756`). The adapters (`tui/telemetry.rs:361-660`: SQLite read-only queries + JSONL tail) already load events for the Timeline. `docs/dashboard-information-architecture.md:130,345` specify `/` to search. README L462 promises search and filter.

## Design
- Model: `LogSearchState { query: String, editing: bool, filters: { event_type: Option<String>, min_level: Option<Level>, since: Option<Duration> }, results: Vec<EventRow>, cursor, page }`.
- Keys on screen 6: `/` starts editing (overlay-less inline input), `Enter` runs, `Esc` cancels editing, `n`/`p` next/prev page, `t` cycles event type, `l` cycles min level, `s` cycles since (15m/1h/24h/all), `c` clears.
- Query grammar: free text substring over `message`/`path`; tokens `type:<event>`, `level:<lvl>`, `path:<prefix>`, `id:<decision-id>` (G2). Case-insensitive.
- Data: `telemetry::search_events(query, filters, page)` — SQLite `activity_log` (indexed by ts; substring via `LIKE` with escaped wildcards) and, when SQLite is unavailable, a bounded JSONL tail scan (last N MiB). Results carry `source: sqlite|jsonl`.
- Rendering: header shows the query and active filters; empty state explains how to search; degraded mode explains which source is missing.

## Files
`src/tui/{model,update,input,render,telemetry,layout}.rs`, docs/dashboard-information-architecture.md (mark implemented), README.

## Tests
- Unit: grammar parser (tokens, escaping), key routing on screen 6, pagination math.
- Property (proptest): filtered result set is always a subset of the unfiltered set; `id:` token returns at most one row per id.
- Unit (`telemetry.rs`): SQLite search on a fixture DB; JSONL fallback on a fixture file; `LIKE` wildcard escaping.
- Snapshot (`test_snapshot_golden.rs`): LogSearch frame with a query and with the empty state.

## Success criteria

description:
# G6.1 - `sbh bootstrap [--dry-run] [--json]`, install-time safe repairs, `doctor --env` health report

## Context
See G6. `bootstrap.rs` API (verify exact names when implementing): `scan_footprints() -> Vec<Footprint>` (`:707`), migration planning per `MigrationReason`, `run_migration(plan, opts)` with backups (`:252-266`), `format_report_human`, health states Healthy/Degraded/Broken/NotInstalled. Bootstrap also detects the three deprecated config keys (`:878`) without aliasing them.

## Design
- `Command::Bootstrap(BootstrapArgs { dry_run, json, yes })`: scan -> plan -> (dry-run: print plan; else apply with backups) -> report. Exit 0 when Healthy or repaired, 1 when Broken remains, 2 on usage error. Human output lists each reason -> action -> backup path; JSON mirrors `MigrationPlan`.
- `sbh install`: after binary placement and before service registration, run the scan and apply only the *safe* action set (`FixPermissions`, `DeduplicateProfile`, `RemoveProfileLine` for stale entries pointing at a missing binary, `UpdateServicePath`, `CreateDirectory`, `InitStateFile`); print a one-line summary; never copy legacy config/state during install (operator runs `bootstrap` for that). `--no-bootstrap` opt-out.
- `doctor --env`: read-only scan -> health state + reasons (no mutation), sharing the check-id style of `--system`.
- Add `MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift` using G3.3's `UnitDrift`, and `LaunchdPlistDrift` for macOS.
- Deprecated config keys: keep detection; add the did-you-mean output from G8.1 so both paths agree.

`src/cli_app.rs` (command, args, dispatch), `src/cli/bootstrap.rs` (public API tidy, drift reasons), `src/cli/install.rs`, README bootstrap section (regenerated tables for reasons/actions via G8.2), AGENTS.md CLI table.

See G6. `uninstall.rs:23-33` `CleanupMode`, `:75-88` `RemovalCategory` (binary, config-file, data-directory, state-file, sqlite-db, jsonl-log, asset-cache, systemd-unit, launchd-plist, shell-completion, shell-profile-entry, ballast-pool, backup-file), `plan_uninstall`, `execute_uninstall`, `backup_first` semantics (`:62,573`). `cli_app.rs:1985-2050` `run_uninstall` removes the service then, for `--purge`, calls `install::run_uninstall_cleanup` (hard-coded flags).

## Design
- `UninstallArgs` gains `--keep-data`, `--keep-config`, `--keep-assets` (clap group, mutually exclusive with each other and with `--purge`; none = Conservative), `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--yes` (required for non-dry-run destructive modes unless stdin is a TTY and the operator confirms).
- Flow: service teardown (existing) -> `plan_uninstall(mode, paths, platform)` -> print plan (categories, backup_first flags) -> if not dry-run: `execute_uninstall(plan)` -> report (removed, backed-up, skipped, errors). `--json` emits plan and results.
- `install::run_uninstall_cleanup`: retired in favor of the module; its two call sites route through `plan/execute` (no compatibility shim per AGENTS.md).
- Ballast pools on other volumes (coordinator-managed, for example `/data/.sbh/ballast`) are included in the `ballast-pool` category from the coordinator's inventory, not only the configured dir.
- Safety: never remove anything outside the known footprint set; symlink-safe; `.sbh-protect`-irrelevant (not a scan).

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs`, `src/cli/uninstall.rs`, `src/cli/install.rs`, README uninstall section (table regenerated), AGENTS.md CLI table, CHANGELOG.

## Tests
- Unit (`--bin sbh`): flag group exclusivity; default mode Conservative.
- Integration (`tests/installer_e2e.rs`): a fixture install footprint (binary, config, sqlite, jsonl, state, completions, profile line, unit file, ballast dirs on two volumes) -> for each mode, `--dry-run --json` lists exactly the documented categories; executing `--keep-data --yes` leaves sqlite/jsonl in place and backs up config; `--purge --yes` removes everything and the backup dir holds the `backup_first` items.
- e2e section "Uninstall modes" (with `SBH_E2E_SKIP_DESTRUCTIVE` respected).

## Success criteria

notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.5, closed as duplicate): `--purge` should always back up config plus the last 1 MiB of each log; the planner today never plans `BallastPool` (add it, including coordinator per-mount pools).

title: G7.1: Pin a dated nightly in rust-toolchain.toml + CI; weekly toolchain-canary workflow
description:
# G7.1 - Pin a dated nightly in rust-toolchain.toml and add a weekly toolchain-canary workflow

## Context
`rust-toolchain.toml` = `channel = "nightly"` with rustfmt+clippy components; CI uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` (8 sites in `ci.yml`). Every new nightly can introduce lints that turn `-D warnings` red on `main` with no code change (this happened twice in August: 08-16 CI and 09-01 local, different lint sets). `.cargo/config.toml` sets `-Z threads=4`, which also depends on nightly.

## Design
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: `channel = "nightly-2026-08-25"` (the newest nightly that `rch` workers already have installed and that CI last used; verify with `rustup toolchain list` on a worker and `rch workers probe`) with `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]` and `profile = "minimal"`.
- CI: replace `@nightly` with `@nightly-2026-08-25` (or read the channel from the toolchain file via `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` + `toolchain: ${{ steps.tc.outputs.channel }}`) so local and CI agree by construction.
- New `.github/workflows/toolchain-canary.yml`: weekly cron + manual dispatch; installs the latest nightly, runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --no-run`; on failure opens/updates a single issue labeled `toolchain` with the lint summary (`gh issue create/comment`), never fails `main`.
- AGENTS.md "Toolchain" section states the pin and the bump procedure (bump pin -> run canary locally via `rch` -> fix lints in the same PR).
- `rch`: confirm workers have the pinned toolchain (`rch workers probe --all` output pasted in the bead).

## Tests
- CI itself: after the pin, `check` job green; canary job runs on dispatch.
- Static test: `rust-toolchain.toml` channel matches the CI `toolchain:` input (grep-based test in `src/cli/mod.rs` contract-test style).

## Success criteria
- [ ] `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` and CI agree (both green after G7.2).

title: G7.2: Fix the 62 clippy findings by hand (assert_is_empty, duration units, unchecked subtraction, const_is_empty, redundant_clone) + CI-nightly lints
