# G7.2 - Fix the 62 clippy findings by hand (no scripted rewrites) and the three CI-nightly findings

## Context
See G7 for the lint/file breakdown (from `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` on nightly 2026-08-31, HEAD 320d04d). Also the 2026-08-16 CI failures: `src/core/errors.rs:32` (`redundant_field_names`), `src/monitor/predictive.rs:337` and `:364` (`suboptimal_flops`).

## Rules
- AGENTS.md: never run a script that rewrites code; make each change by hand (parallel subagents allowed for the mechanical `assert!(x.is_empty())` -> `assert!(x.is_empty(), "...")`/`assert_eq!` sites, one file per agent, each verified with `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"`).
- Prefer the fix that improves the test message: `assert!(v.is_empty())` -> `assert!(v.is_empty(), "expected no {what}, got {v:?}")`; `assert!(!v.is_empty())` -> `assert!(!v.is_empty(), "expected at least one {what}")`. Do not blanket-`#[allow]` these lints.
- `duration_suboptimal_units`: use `Duration::from_secs/mins/hours` as appropriate. `unchecked_duration_subtraction`: `saturating_sub`/`checked_sub` with an explicit comment on why saturation is correct at those two sites (`loop_main.rs`). `const_is_empty` in `decision_plane_tests.rs:1805`: assert the actual version string.
- `suboptimal_flops` in `predictive.rs`: use `mul_add` only if numerically intended; otherwise annotate with a reasoned `#[allow]` and a comment (precision semantics matter in the forecaster).

## Verification
- `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` clean on the pinned nightly (G7.1) and on the newest nightly (canary).
- `rch exec "cargo test --workspace"` unchanged pass count (1,757 on Linux).

## Context
`ci.yml` jobs use `--lib`, `--bin sbh`, and `--test <name>` selectively; `installer_e2e`, `stress_harness`, `repro_*`, `regression_*` never run; clippy is `--lib --bin sbh`; examples/benches are never built. `quality-gate.sh` (21 stages) is not in CI; docs list 20. `.gate_sbh_trj.sh` (untracked root script) runs `fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `test --workspace --no-fail-fast` and logs to `/data/release-work/`; it is the only full gate anyone runs. `docs/post-rollout-monitoring-and-handoff.md:49` claims the gate runs "every PR, nightly on main".

- `ci.yml`: `check` job runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with the default feature set from G5.1 and once with the lean set); a `tests` job runs `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (replacing the per-file jobs, or keeping them as named shards but ensuring the union is the workspace); `examples`/`benches` compiled via `--all-targets`; artifacts (per-case logs under `$TMPDIR/sbh-test-logs`, e2e summary, daemon budget JSON) uploaded on failure and on success for the budget files.

## Context

Reproduction test for issue verification (placeholder).` (1 line). `git log --follow` should reveal which issue it was created for; recreate that regression or, if the case now lives elsewhere, DECISION: operator approves deletion, otherwise the file gets the pointer test.

Un-ignore the regression and flip its assertion.
- Replace the three placeholder files with the real tests described above; document in docs/testing-and-logging.md.

## Tests
- `tests/regression_path_traversal.rs` (un-ignored): nonexistent root -> error; existing root with `..` inside -> resolved; symlink-loop -> bounded error.

title: G8.1: Config strictness — unknown keys detected with did-you-mean suggestions; config validate --strict; doctor check
description:
# G8.1 - Config strictness: unknown keys are detected, warned with did-you-mean suggestions, and rejected under `config validate --strict`

## Context
`core/config.rs:20-35` `Config` and every section are `#[serde(default)]` with no `deny_unknown_fields`; `load()` (`:1135-1136`) parses leniently. Deprecated keys (`scan_interval_secs`, `max_ballast_mb`, `log_level`) are only detected by the (unreachable) bootstrap scanner (`cli/bootstrap.rs:878`). README's own example is mostly unknown keys; the operator's live config carries `[scoring.weights]`.

## Design
- Two-pass load: parse into `StrictConfig` (same structs re-declared via a derive attribute swap is not possible in serde; instead use `toml::Table` traversal): after lenient parse, walk the raw `toml::Table` and compare every key path against a generated `KNOWN_KEYS: &[&str]` (produced by a small `#[derive(KeyPaths)]`-free approach: a hand-maintained list is unacceptable; generate it in `build.rs` from a JSON schema emitted by `schemars`? No new heavy deps: derive the key list by serializing `Config::default()` to `toml::Value` and walking it, plus explicit entries for map-like sections such as `ballast.overrides.*` and `notifications.*`). Unknown paths produce `ConfigWarning { path, suggestion }` where `suggestion` is the nearest known key by Damerau-Levenshtein distance <= 3 within the same section, with special-case aliases table for the known README mistakes (`scoring.weights.location` -> `scoring.location_weight`, `monitor.pressure_green_pct` -> `pressure.green_min_free_pct`, `ballast.per_volume_file_count` -> `ballast.file_count`, `logging.sqlite_path` -> `paths.sqlite_db`, `policy.mode` -> `policy.initial_mode`, `guardrails.calibration_floor` -> `scoring.calibration_floor`, and the three deprecated keys).
- Surfaces: `[SBH-CONFIG] unknown key <path> (did you mean <suggestion>?)` on stderr at daemon start, `install`, and every CLI load (once per process); `config validate` lists them as WARN; `config validate --strict` (and `SBH_CONFIG_STRICT=1`) exits 1; `doctor --system` check `config.unknown_keys`.
- JSON: `config validate --json` gains `unknown_keys: [{path, suggestion}]`.

## Files
`src/core/config.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (validate/doctor/install), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (startup log), README configuration section (example rewritten in G8.3; here, add the "Unknown keys" paragraph), CHANGELOG.

## Tests
- Unit: every key in the README example (as of G8.3) is known -> zero warnings; the pre-fix README example yields exactly the documented set of unknown keys with the expected suggestions; deprecated keys map to their replacements; map sections (`ballast.overrides."/data".enabled`) are not flagged.
- Unit: `KNOWN_KEYS` derivation covers every field (test: serialize `Config::default()`, assert each leaf path is known; assert a deliberately unknown path is flagged).
- Integration: `sbh config validate --strict` exit 1 on a fixture with `[scoring.weights]`; exit 0 after correction.
- e2e case.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh config validate --strict` flags `scoring.weights.*` with suggestions.
notes: From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.8, closed as duplicate): also `config_version = 2` at the top with bootstrap migration of v1 files; tilde and $HOME expansion for every path-typed field (`[notifications.file] path = "~/..."` currently creates a literal `~` dir); honor `[ballast] auto_provision` (never read today); strict mode default true for system services; commit the README example as tests/fixtures/readme-config.toml parsed in CI.

## Design
- `Command::Docs(DocsArgs { json: bool, section: Option<String>, render: Option<PathBuf> })` (hidden from the main help? No: documented, it is how operators can inspect effective constants). `sbh docs --json` emits a versioned document: `defaults` (full `Config::default()` as TOML and JSON), `pressure_table` (levels, thresholds, scan interval divisor, ballast release counts, batch sizes from `pid.rs::response_policy`), `constants` (PID gains, EWMA base alpha/min/max, guardrail window/thresholds/reward/penalty/clamp/alarm, breaker threshold/cooldown, channel capacities, open-file budgets, walker caps, self-monitor intervals, repeat-deletion defaults, notification intervals, ballast header size/magic/fsync interval), `commands` (from clap: name, about, flags), `env_vars` (from a single `ENV_VARS` registry that `config.rs` reads through, so nothing is read via a bare `env::var` string elsewhere; grep test), `error_codes` (from `errors.rs`), `patterns` (count by category), `module_map` (files under `src/` with line counts, computed at test time, not runtime), `bootstrap.reasons/actions`, `uninstall.modes`, `dashboard.keymap/palette/playbook` (G5.6).
- Rendering: `sbh docs --render README.md` rewrites only the regions between `<!-- sbh-docs:begin <section> -->` / `<!-- sbh-docs:end -->` markers; same for AGENTS.md and docs/testing-and-logging.md (stage table, artifact schema). Prose outside markers is untouched.
- `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh`: build, render into a temp copy, `diff`; non-zero on drift; CI job `docs-drift` (G7.3 registers it); `quality-gate.sh` SOFT stage.
- Constants that are currently literals must become named `pub const`s at the point of use (for example `deletion.rs:76` breaker threshold, `walker.rs:369` result channel cap) so the generator reads the real values.

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs` (command), `src/core/{config,errors}.rs`, `src/monitor/{pid,ewma,guardrails}.rs`, `src/scanner/{deletion,walker,patterns}.rs`, `src/daemon/{loop_main,notifications,self_monitor}.rs`, `src/ballast/manager.rs` (named consts + `docs` collectors), `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh`, README.md/AGENTS.md (markers), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Tests
- Unit: `docs --json` snapshot (insta) so a constant change is a visible diff in review.
- Unit: every `pub const` registered appears in the JSON (registry completeness test).
- Static: README/AGENTS marker regions render byte-identical (the CI check as a cargo test too).
- Grep test: no `env::var("SBH_` outside the registry.

## Success criteria

title: Reality-check remediation 2026-09: deliver the README vision end to end
description:
# Master epic: close every gap found by the 2026-09-02 reality check

## Goal
Make every capability the README promises either (a) exist in the binary users can obtain, with a CI-run proof on Linux and macOS, or (b) leave the README. Restore the delivery pipeline. Make the daemon reclaim space *before* the volume reaches the state in which its own remediation fails.

## Workstreams (child epics)
W0 proof machinery (prerequisite) · W1 reclaim before the cliff · W2 explainability · W3 truthful CLI · W4 release contract/updater/pipeline · W5 systemd correctness · W6 logging/stats integrity · W7 scanner v2 hardening · W8 ballast integrity · W9 macOS closeout · W10 real daemon e2e suite · W11 documentation reconciliation · W12 tracker hygiene · W13 host and fleet rollout.

## Critical path
W0 -> W4 (v0.5.2: fleet updater restored, no behavior change) -> W1 with W10 as its acceptance test -> v0.6.0 canary on the operator workstation and one rch VPS for 7 days -> fleet.

## Cross-cutting invariants (must hold after every child closes)
1. No deletion without a persisted decision id.
2. No pressure above Green on a mount with a root_path or pool without a logged action or a logged idle reason within one tick.
3. No CLI command documented in README without a passing CI case.
4. No config key in README that `sbh config validate` rejects or ignores.
5. Daemon CPU time <= 2%% of wall at Green and <= 33%% under sustained Orange with bounded work, measured by the e2e suite.
6. Release assets are identical whether produced by the workflow or the manual script, and every asset verifies.
7. `sbh status` never reports `daemon_running: true` without a live probe.
8. Every SkipReason is a closed enum with errno where applicable; `stats` reports failures by reason.
9. `state.json` v2 is written at least every 30 s and on shutdown.
10. The tick interval never drops below the base poll unless at least one mount is in Reclaim with dispatchable work or releasable ballast.

## Operator decisions embedded in this plan (defaults chosen; reverse by editing the relevant child bead)
- Orange deletes definite artifacts and releases ballast by default (behavior preset v0.6).
- The TUI ships in default builds (`tui` becomes a default feature).
- Canonical release layout is tarball + sidecars with raw-binary mirrors; installer and updater accept both.
- Deleting dead files (src/cli/dashboard.rs, ShutdownCoordinator, legacy systemd module) requires explicit operator permission per AGENTS.md; until then they are feature-gated.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Consolidation note (2026-09-02)
A parallel reality check produced the bead tree `bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx` (G0-G12) with overlapping scope. Duplicated children of this epic were closed in favor of the G-tree and their unique details appended there as notes; the remaining children here are the parts the G-tree does not cover. Cross-tree blocking and related edges record the interplay. See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md section 5b.

---

(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# Reality-check bridge (2026-09-01): make `sbh` deliver the README as written, on the operator's own host first, with proof

## Why this epic exists
A full reality check on 2026-09-01 (docs/internal/reality-check-2026-09-01.md, HEAD 320d04d) walked every README/AGENTS claim to code with seven parallel audits, ran the whole test suite, clippy, fmt, and inspected the shipped binary, the live systemd unit, the live GitHub releases, the Homebrew tap, and the Actions history. Verdict: the engine (control loop, scoring, vetoes, ballast, logging, notifications, leases, scanner v2, writeback tuning, macOS PAL) is real and passes 1,757 tests, but the product as documented is not delivered:

- `sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, uninstall cleanup modes, and the TUI dashboard are absent or unreachable from any released binary (about 4,100 lines of tested dead code plus 25k lines of TUI that never ships).
- System-scope systemd units use `Type=notify` but the daemon never sends `READY=1` (start would time out).
- Self-update builds asset names that 404 against the current releases (v0.5.x were hand-published with raw names).
- The README config example silently discards about 20 keys; about 45 numeric/semantic doc claims are wrong.
- `clippy -D warnings` is red (62 findings on the current nightly); all three GitHub workflows are `disabled_manually`; no branch protection; the quality-gate script's TUI stages pass with zero tests.
- On the operator's primary host (threadripperje): `/` is at 12% free (Orange), the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (`/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED`), the root-volume ballast pool is empty because provisioning refuses below a flat 20% floor, no configured scan root lives on `/`, and `sbh status` still reports `daemon_running: true` because it substring-matches `/proc/*/cmdline` for "sbh"+"daemon" (it matched the auditor's own shell).

## Scope
Twelve gap groups (G0-G12) from the reality-check bridge plan, each a child epic or task under this one. Ordering by vision impact: host protection (G1), the explain ledger (G2), and the systemd bug (G3) first; release contract (G4); dashboard shipping (G5); dead-module wiring (G6); quality gates (G7); docs-as-contract (G8); policy semantics (G9); observability (G10); scanner v2 closeout (G11); bead hygiene (G12); operator runbook (G0).

## Non-negotiables inherited from AGENTS.md
- Never delete files without explicit written operator permission. Where removal is the best resolution (dead code, clutter, v1 walker) the child bead records a DECISION for the operator and defaults to wiring the code in.
- No script-based code edits; use `rch exec` for all compilation; keep clippy pedantic+nursery clean; no unsafe in the main crate; revise files in place, no `*_v2.rs`.
- Every fix ships with: a unit test of the mechanism, an integration or e2e test of the behavior, structured logging so a failure is diagnosable from the artifact, and, where a doc was wrong, a doc-contract test that would have caught it.

## Definition of done for the epic
All child beads closed; section 1 of the reality-check doc re-audited with every row WORKING or an explicit operator DECISION recorded; this host shows a reserve on `/`, catalog reclaim capability for `/`, `daemon_running` decided by the daemon lock, steady-state CPU under 1% of a core, and no kill switch.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Consolidation correction: the earlier consolidation note is superseded. The parallel G-tree was merged INTO this tree (all bridge beads closed with `Merged into` reasons); every bead here is canonical and carries the merged text.
- DECISION (policy default): the code default and `sbh install --auto` stay `initial_mode = Enforce` (README promises out-of-box protection; 2.3's floor, the vetoes and 2.13's quarantine are the safety net); Observe is offered only in the interactive wizard.
- W0 gating: workstream root tasks (2.1, 2.3, 2.5, 2.12, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2, 4.8, 5.1, 6.1) now depend on 1.1 (clippy green) only; not on 1.2, which contains operator-only steps.

title: W0: Restore the proof machinery (clippy, CI, honest quality gate)
description:
# W0 — Restore the proof machinery

## Why first
Nightly clippy drift broke the lint gate on 2026-08-14; instead of fixing it the three GitHub workflows were disabled (state `disabled_manually`), releases went manual, and the TUI test lanes were never part of any gate. "Green" stopped meaning anything, so no other workstream can be trusted until this one lands.

## Scope
1. Fix the 62 clippy errors by hand; pin nightly by date; weekly lint-drift job.
2. Re-enable CI/Release/cert-expiration; add a `tui` matrix dimension; remove the obsolete "strip local-only TUI path deps" step (ftui is a git-tag dependency now).
3. Make scripts/quality-gate.sh honest (executed-test counts, vacuous stage = failure, `--features tui`, `--print-stages --markdown` as the docs source).
4. Cargo workspace including crates/sbh_mach; its tests run on macOS lanes.
5. Generated test census replaces hand-typed counts in docs.

## Acceptance
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` exit 0 locally and in CI on Linux and macOS.
- Two consecutive green pushes on main across {linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64} x {default, tui}.
- TUI lane executes >= 950 tests; quality-gate.sh exit 0 with zero vacuous stages.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. title: Fix the 62 clippy errors by hand and pin the nightly toolchain by date
description:
# Fix clippy -D warnings at HEAD and stop lint drift from breaking main

## Background
`rch exec -- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at 320d04d fails with 62 errors: 37 "used assert! to check that a value is empty", 16 "... is not empty", 5 "constructing a Duration using a smaller unit when a larger unit would be more readable", 2 "unchecked subtraction of a Duration", 1 "this assertion has a constant value", 1 "redundant clone". 61 are in the lib test target, 1 in the bin test target (src/cli_app.rs:13160). Files include src/ballast/coordinator.rs:795,848; src/ballast/manager.rs:1134,1344; src/cli/assets.rs:1359,1965-2110; src/cli/dashboard.rs:645; src/cli/update.rs:1703; src/cli/wizard.rs:631,716; src/cli/mod.rs:1194; src/core/config.rs:2679; src/daemon/loop_main.rs:6607 and others (run clippy for the full list). The same class of failure is why the CI "Format + Lint" job has been red since 2026-08-14.

## Design
- Edit each site manually (AGENTS.md forbids script-based code changes): `assert!(x.len() == 0)` -> `assert!(x.is_empty())`; `assert!(!x.is_empty())` where negated; `Duration::from_millis(60_000)` -> `Duration::from_secs(60)`; `a - b` on Durations -> `a.saturating_sub(b)` or `checked_sub().expect("...")` with the invariant stated; delete the constant assertion and the redundant clone. No blanket `#[allow]`; a targeted allow is acceptable only with a comment explaining a deliberate choice (precedent: the two `if_not_else` fail-safes).
- Pin `rust-toolchain.toml` to `nightly-YYYY-MM-DD` (the date the fixes were validated against) so lint drift becomes a deliberate bump.
- Add `.github/workflows/lint-drift.yml`: weekly cron on a branch that runs clippy with the newest nightly and, on failure, opens/updates a bead via `br create` in a follow-up commit or a GitHub issue; never red on main.

## Acceptance
- clippy `-D warnings` clean for `--all-targets` with default features AND with `--features tui`, on Linux and macOS.
- `cargo fmt --check` still clean; `cargo test --workspace` still 0 failures.

## Tests
No new tests beyond the gate itself; W0.3 adds the gate self-test.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.8.1 — G7.1: Pin a dated nightly in rust-toolchain.toml + CI; weekly toolchain-canary workflow
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G7.1 - Pin a dated nightly in rust-toolchain.toml and add a weekly toolchain-canary workflow

## Context
`rust-toolchain.toml` = `channel = "nightly"` with rustfmt+clippy components; CI uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly` (8 sites in `ci.yml`). Every new nightly can introduce lints that turn `-D warnings` red on `main` with no code change (this happened twice in August: 08-16 CI and 09-01 local, different lint sets). `.cargo/config.toml` sets `-Z threads=4`, which also depends on nightly.

## Design
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: `channel = "nightly-2026-08-25"` (the newest nightly that `rch` workers already have installed and that CI last used; verify with `rustup toolchain list` on a worker and `rch workers probe`) with `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]` and `profile = "minimal"`.
- CI: replace `@nightly` with `@nightly-2026-08-25` (or read the channel from the toolchain file via `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` + `toolchain: ${{ steps.tc.outputs.channel }}`) so local and CI agree by construction.
- New `.github/workflows/toolchain-canary.yml`: weekly cron + manual dispatch; installs the latest nightly, runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --no-run`; on failure opens/updates a single issue labeled `toolchain` with the lint summary (`gh issue create/comment`), never fails `main`.
- AGENTS.md "Toolchain" section states the pin and the bump procedure (bump pin -> run canary locally via `rch` -> fix lints in the same PR).
- `rch`: confirm workers have the pinned toolchain (`rch workers probe --all` output pasted in the bead).

## Tests
- CI itself: after the pin, `check` job green; canary job runs on dispatch.
- Static test: `rust-toolchain.toml` channel matches the CI `toolchain:` input (grep-based test in `src/cli/mod.rs` contract-test style).

## Success criteria
- [ ] `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` and CI agree (both green after G7.2).


---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.8.2 — G7.2: Fix the 62 clippy findings by hand (assert_is_empty, duration units, unchecked subtraction, const_is_empty, redundant_clone) + CI-nightly lints
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G7.2 - Fix the 62 clippy findings by hand (no scripted rewrites) and the three CI-nightly findings

## Context
See G7 for the lint/file breakdown (from `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` on nightly 2026-08-31, HEAD 320d04d). Also the 2026-08-16 CI failures: `src/core/errors.rs:32` (`redundant_field_names`), `src/monitor/predictive.rs:337` and `:364` (`suboptimal_flops`).

## Rules
- AGENTS.md: never run a script that rewrites code; make each change by hand (parallel subagents allowed for the mechanical `assert!(x.is_empty())` -> `assert!(x.is_empty(), "...")`/`assert_eq!` sites, one file per agent, each verified with `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"`).
- Prefer the fix that improves the test message: `assert!(v.is_empty())` -> `assert!(v.is_empty(), "expected no {what}, got {v:?}")`; `assert!(!v.is_empty())` -> `assert!(!v.is_empty(), "expected at least one {what}")`. Do not blanket-`#[allow]` these lints.
- `duration_suboptimal_units`: use `Duration::from_secs/mins/hours` as appropriate. `unchecked_duration_subtraction`: `saturating_sub`/`checked_sub` with an explicit comment on why saturation is correct at those two sites (`loop_main.rs`). `const_is_empty` in `decision_plane_tests.rs:1805`: assert the actual version string.
- `suboptimal_flops` in `predictive.rs`: use `mul_add` only if numerically intended; otherwise annotate with a reasoned `#[allow]` and a comment (precision semantics matter in the forecaster).

## Verification
- `rch exec "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings"` clean on the pinned nightly (G7.1) and on the newest nightly (canary).
- `rch exec "cargo test --workspace"` unchanged pass count (1,757 on Linux).
- `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- CHANGELOG "Fixed" entry that corrects the v0.5.0 "clippy clean" claim with the pinned toolchain statement.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Zero clippy errors on `--all-targets` including examples, benches, and all integration tests.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: the weekly job is `.github/workflows/toolchain-canary.yml` and opens/updates a GitHub issue labeled `toolchain` (CI cannot write `.beads/` safely). Pin rule: the newest nightly that the rch workers have (`rch workers probe`), recorded in this bead when chosen.

title: Re-enable CI, Release and cert-expiration workflows; add the tui matrix; get two green pushes
description:
# Re-enable the GitHub workflows and make them cover the shipped configuration

## Background
`gh api repos/Dicklesworthstone/storage_ballast_helper/actions/workflows` shows CI, Release and "Developer ID Certificate Expiration" all `disabled_manually`. The last CI run (2026-08-16) failed at Format + Lint with every Linux test job skipped; no run exists for the 27 commits of 2026-08-21..26 or for the v0.5.0/v0.5.1 tags. ci.yml still contains a "Strip local-only TUI path deps" step and `tui = []` rewriting from the era when ftui was a local path dependency; Cargo.toml now pins ftui to a git tag, so the step is obsolete and the TUI is never compiled in CI (~955 tests never run).

## Design
- Enable all three workflows (`gh workflow enable`).
- ci.yml: remove the strip step; matrix `{ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-latest, macos-15-intel} x features {default, tui}`; clippy `--all-targets` (not `--lib --bin`) with `-D warnings`; unit + integration + `fallback_verification` (tui) + dashboard tests + decision plane + e2e script on a release build; keep macOS coverage/perf/formula jobs; `paths-ignore` limited to `.beads/**`.
- release.yml: consumes ci.yml via workflow_call (already), builds release binaries with `--features tui` (see W3.7), keeps the tarball-arch guard.
- Confirm cert-expiration runs on schedule.

## Acceptance
Two consecutive green CI runs on main across the full matrix; TUI lane log shows >= 950 tests executed; Release workflow dry-run (workflow_dispatch on a test tag or a PR) reaches the build jobs.

## Tests
`actionlint` step added to CI to lint the workflows themselves.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.5.4 — G4.4: External operator actions — re-enable workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, tap update, branch protection
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G4.4 - External operator actions: re-enable the three GitHub workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, update the tap, add branch protection

## Why a bead
These steps need the operator's GitHub permissions and judgment; agents cannot (and must not) perform them. Tracking them here keeps the release-contract work honest: without them, G4.1-G4.3 are code without a shipped effect.

## Facts (2026-09-01)
- `gh workflow list --all`: CI (234441116), Release (234441117), Developer ID Certificate Expiration (273476379) are all `disabled_manually`. Last run of any kind: 2026-08-16 (CI, failed on clippy) / 2026-08-20 (cert check, passed).
- `main` has no branch protection and no rulesets (`gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection` -> 404).
- Latest release v0.5.1 (2026-08-26): raw binaries + `SHA256SUMS` only; no workflow run for the tag; signing/notarization unproven.
- Tap `Dicklesworthstone/homebrew-sbh` at v0.4.28 (last successful workflow release, 2026-06-08).

## Checklist
1. After G7.1/G7.2 land (clippy green on the pinned nightly): `gh workflow enable ci.yml`, `gh workflow enable release.yml`, `gh workflow enable cert-expiration.yml`; trigger CI on `main`; record the run id and result here.
2. Decide the v0.5.x backfill: either (a) re-tag/republish v0.5.1 assets through `release.yml` so tarballs + provenance exist (recommended: publish a v0.5.2 from `main` once G4.2 is merged and let the workflow produce both schemes), or (b) hand-upload contract assets to v0.5.1. Record the decision.
3. Confirm the tap formula updated to the new version by the workflow; `brew install` smoke on a Mac; paste `sbh doctor --release` output.
4. Branch protection on `main`: require `check`, `unit`, `integration` (names from `ci.yml`) and disallow force-push; record settings.
5. Update bd-t951 (close as absorbed by G4.2) and bd-ykwh/bd-ykwh.3 (G12) with links.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `sbh doctor --release` (G4.3) reports all PASS.
- [ ] `sbh update --check --force --dry-run` from a v0.5.1 binary resolves an existing asset (HTTP 200).


---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.8.3 — G7.3: CI runs --workspace --all-targets, every test file, examples/benches, honest quality-gate.sh, fold .gate_sbh_trj.sh
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G7.3 - CI runs everything: `--workspace --all-targets`, every test file, examples and benches, an honest `quality-gate.sh`, `.gate_sbh_trj.sh` folded in

## Context
`ci.yml` jobs use `--lib`, `--bin sbh`, and `--test <name>` selectively; `installer_e2e`, `stress_harness`, `repro_*`, `regression_*` never run; clippy is `--lib --bin sbh`; examples/benches are never built. `quality-gate.sh` (21 stages) is not in CI; docs list 20. `.gate_sbh_trj.sh` (untracked root script) runs `fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `test --workspace --no-fail-fast` and logs to `/data/release-work/`; it is the only full gate anyone runs. `docs/post-rollout-monitoring-and-handoff.md:49` claims the gate runs "every PR, nightly on main".

## Design
- `ci.yml`: `check` job runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with the default feature set from G5.1 and once with the lean set); a `tests` job runs `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (replacing the per-file jobs, or keeping them as named shards but ensuring the union is the workspace); `examples`/`benches` compiled via `--all-targets`; artifacts (per-case logs under `$TMPDIR/sbh-test-logs`, e2e summary, daemon budget JSON) uploaded on failure and on success for the budget files.
- `quality-gate.sh`: `--ci` mode invoked by a `quality-gate` job (kept as the human-runnable superset); stage table regenerated into docs (G8.2); a `--full` mode replicates `.gate_sbh_trj.sh` (workspace, all targets, no-fail-fast, log path configurable via `SBH_GATE_LOG`). `.gate_sbh_trj.sh`: DECISION for the operator: delete after folding (needs permission) or add to `.gitignore`; default: `.gitignore` entry + note in docs.
- `docs/post-rollout-monitoring-and-handoff.md` and `docs/testing-and-logging.md`: corrected to the real triggers (no `schedule:` unless added; if a nightly is desired, add `schedule:` to `ci.yml` and say so).
- Remove the dead "Strip local-only TUI path deps" step from `ci.yml`/`release.yml` (G4.2 touches release.yml; do ci.yml here).

## Tests
- Meta-test in `src/cli/mod.rs` contract style: parse `ci.yml` and assert the `tests` job command contains `--workspace`; assert every `tests/*.rs` file name appears in at least one job or the workspace run covers it.
- `quality-gate.sh --list` prints stages; docs table equality test (G8.2).

## Success criteria
- [ ] A deliberately failing `tests/repro_*` test turns CI red (verified once on a branch).

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.8.3
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.1.2/bd-rc-master-ajg1.1.3, closed as duplicates): stage rule — a HARD/SOFT stage that executed zero tests fails with reason `vacuous` unless marked allow-empty; `quality-gate.sh --print-stages --markdown` is the single source for the stage table in docs; `--self-test` fakes an empty stage; add `actionlint` to CI; matrix `{linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64} x {default, tui}`; drop the obsolete "strip local-only TUI path deps" step.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Scope: ci.yml only (matrix rewrite + actionlint). Operator-only steps (enable workflows, branch protection, v0.5.x backfill decision, tap check) are the new W0 operator-checklist bead that 5.5 depends on; the quality-gate CI job and the `.gate_sbh_trj.sh` fold are 1.3.
- DECISION: the matrix uses explicit feature lists, `lean = --no-default-features --features cli,daemon,sqlite` and `tui = --features tui`, so it is invariant to 4.7 flipping the default.

description:
# quality-gate.sh must fail when a stage runs zero tests

## Background
scripts/quality-gate.sh (525 lines, 21 stages: 17 HARD, 4 SOFT) never passes `--features tui`. With default features `cargo test --lib tui::...` selects 0 tests and exits 0, so 9 TUI stages plus the `fallback` stage (tests/fallback_verification.rs is `#![cfg(feature = "tui")]`) pass vacuously. docs/quality-gate-runbook.md describes a different 10-stage runbook; docs/testing-and-logging.md says "20 stages"; docs/tui-go-nogo-signoff.md says "15/15 HARD, 4/4 SOFT". Three documents, three numbers, none matching the script.

## Design
- Each stage captures `test result:` lines and sums executed tests; a HARD or SOFT stage with 0 executed tests fails with reason `vacuous` unless the stage is explicitly marked `allow-empty`.
- TUI stages and `fallback` pass `--features tui`.
- `--print-stages [--markdown]` prints the stage table; docs/quality-gate-runbook.md and the gate section of docs/testing-and-logging.md embed that output (W11 wires the CI diff).
- `--self-test` runs the script against a fake target that selects zero tests and asserts the vacuous failure path.

## Acceptance
`./scripts/quality-gate.sh` exit 0 on HEAD with every stage reporting a non-zero executed count; `--self-test` passes; CI runs the gate on Linux (rch mode disabled in CI: `--ci`).

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Background

title: Fuzz targets for config, JSONL, checksum/provenance parsers, control protocol, markers, state.json (W0)
description:
# G7.6 - Fuzz targets for the parsers that face untrusted or operator-authored input

## Why (ambition round 2)
Nightly is already required, so `cargo fuzz` costs nothing to adopt. The parsers that matter: config TOML (operator-authored, now strict per G8.1), JSONL activity reader (used by `log`, the dashboard, and replay), `SHA256SUMS`/sidecar/BSD checksum parsers (network-sourced), the provenance manifest (network-sourced, G4.1), the control-socket protocol (local but privileged, G13), the sacred/protect marker TOML, and `state.json` (cross-version).

## Design
- `fuzz/` directory with `cargo fuzz` targets: `config_parse`, `jsonl_reader`, `checksum_parsers`, `provenance_manifest`, `control_protocol`, `protect_marker`, `state_json`. Each target asserts "no panic, bounded memory, and if `Ok`, round-trips or validates".
- Corpora seeded from fixtures already in the repo (README example config, e2e JSONL outputs, `gh release` asset lists).
- Runs: 60 s per target in the weekly toolchain-canary workflow (G7.1) and on demand via `scripts/quality-gate.sh --stage fuzz`; crashes are committed as regression tests under `tests/fuzz_regressions.rs`.
- AGENTS.md documents how to run a target through `rch`.

## Tests
- The fuzz targets themselves; a smoke test that each target builds (`cargo fuzz build`) in the canary.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Seven targets build and run 60 s each without findings in the canary; any finding becomes a test.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Blocked by 4.9 (control protocol), 5.1 (provenance manifest), 2.8 (state.json v2) for those targets; config/JSONL/checksum/marker fuzzers can start now. `[workspace] exclude = ["fuzz"]` in 1.4; related 1.4.

title: W9: macOS closeout (getfsstat, cold-start budget, open-file deadlines, snapshot estimate, docs, parity audit refresh)

## Background

# W10 — Real daemon end-to-end suite

## Background

## Children

## Scenarios (each asserts events, state, filesystem, CPU)

title: Pressure injection hook, fixture builder, and daemon runner for tests/daemon_e2e.rs

## Design

# G1.6 - Tests, e2e cases, and logging for host protection (G1.1-G1.4)

## Purpose
Consolidate the cross-cutting verification for the host-protection epic so no child ships without proof and the whole path is exercised end to end: graduated reserve -> catalog reclaim -> liveness truth -> loud degradation.

## Deliverables
1. `tests/daemon_host_protection.rs` (new): end-to-end library-level scenario with the mock PAL: volume at 12% free, no configured root on it, pool configured -> after one loop epoch: partial reserve exists (G1.1), one catalog scan dispatched (G1.2), `scan_complete.root_source=catalog`, candidates only under catalog roots, a planted source tree untouched; status snapshot reports `daemon_running` by lock (G1.3) and `reclaim_capability=catalog` (G1.4). Assert log lines by prefix (`[SBH-BALLAST]`, `[SBH-DAEMON]`, `[SBH-NOTIFY]`).
2. `scripts/e2e_test.sh` Section "Host protection": `ballast provision --json` floor fields; `scan --catalog`; `status --json` liveness with a decoy process; `doctor --system --json` reclaim check.
3. Structured logging review: every new decision path logs one line with stable `key=value` pairs (not free-form prose only), and every new JSON field is documented in `docs/testing-and-logging.md` artifact schema.
4. Property tests (proptest): reserve floor admission monotonicity; catalog root derivation never returns a path outside the mount.

## Success criteria
- [ ] All new tests run in CI (`cargo test --workspace`) and in `quality-gate.sh`.
- [ ] `docs/testing-and-logging.md` coverage map updated with real paths.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- Blockers added: 7.1, 6.1, 6.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.10, 2.11, 2.12, 8.1, 4.1; stale blockers on closed bridge beads removed.
- DECISION: two host-layout scenarios: `host-layout-catalog` (default: one bounded catalog scan on the pressured mount, `reclaim_capability=catalog`) and `host-layout-observe` (catalog roots disabled: observe-only with idle_reason). The merged G1.6 in-process mock-PAL test belongs to 2.12.
- Added scenarios: `green-maintenance` (Green + stale Definite -> quarantined within `maintenance_interval_secs`, space returned on Orange drain), `red-empty-pool` (emergency event count == 1 over 60 ticks), Recovery assertions in `read-only` (`policy.guard` alarm, `controller=recovery`).
- `partial-provision` numbers: injected total 10 GiB, 12%% free, orange 10%%, file_size 64 MiB, count 8 -> expect 3 files.
close_reason:
Closed by the implementing agent, not independently verified. Scenario table in tests/daemon_e2e.rs on the 11.1 runner (first part landed in another agent's sweep commit ef6ffd3, rest in the commit referenced in the follow-up comment). Evidence: local run of the test executable against the freshly built daemon: 10 unprivileged scenarios pass (orange-reclaim v2, v1/v2 engine parity run concurrently, red-ballast with a Green->Red injected series and a pool of two released before the scan, forced scan <=2 s, SIGHUP reload with a new root + matrix re-log, special-location horizon on an injected 5.5 TiB `/` at 13.9% with zero alerts over 60 s and idle CPU share 1.1% asserted <2%, host-layout, shutdown, runner negatives); the two privileged scenarios (loop-mounted ext4 image under passwordless sudo, `--ignored`) pass here: partial-provision (128 MiB volume at 22% free, five 4 MiB files configured -> created=3 skipped_for_floor=2) and read-only (volume remounted ro after the pool exists -> [SBH-RECOVERY] once, SBH-2004 error event + file notification, state recovery, no deletion attempt for 45 s, after remount rw every stale target reclaimed and the mount leaves recovery). Unit: empty_pass_cooldown tests 13/13, ballast/logger/loop tests 163/163.
Defects found by the scenarios and fixed in the same change: daemon never emitted ballast_provision/release/replenish events (per-file paths added to ReleaseReport/ProvisionReport, events at four sites); JSONL lines invisible until the next fsync-interval write (logger flushes when its queue drains); Green maintenance passes were dropped by the scanner's empty-pass cooldown (maintenance now bypasses it, duty-cycle deferral still applies, unit test); the maintenance pass scanned roots on mounts parked in Recovery (filtered to Maintain mounts); read-only skips and EROFS/ENOSPC delete errors fed the per-path repeat-deletion backoff, so a recovered mount's targets stayed suppressed for up to an hour (mount incidents no longer earn a per-path backoff).
Deviations from the bead text: (1) the read-only notification is the generic Error level "red" (SBH-2004), not Critical — recorded for 7.1; (2) the horizon scenario runs 60 s (120 polls), not 10 minutes; (3) "no retries" is asserted over a 45 s window, not 5 minutes (RECOVERY_POLL_INTERVAL is 30 s); (4) the CPU budget assertion covers the idle daemon (<2%); the host-layout scenario prints its share (2.0-2.6% at a 500 ms poll and a 5 s maintenance interval, i.e. 10x the production cadence) and does not assert — 2.11 owns the budget; (5) Red-ballast asserts the release precedes the scan in the same tick; the v0.6 matrix cell for Red/normal memory is `release`, `release_first` is the memory-warn row; (6) at Orange the startup priority pre-scan deletes the mtime-stale fixture before the age gate (filed as bd-rc-master-ajg1.15), so the orange scenario tolerates either path; (7) macOS CI not exercised; the privileged scenarios need a CI step with sudo. Also noted: ArtifactDeleted events carry an empty pressure and free_pct 0 (7.1).

Reproduction test for issue verification (placeholder).` (1 line). `git log --follow` should reveal which issue it was created for; recreate that regression or, if the case now lives elsewhere, DECISION: operator approves deletion, otherwise the file gets the pointer test.

- `tests/regression_path_traversal.rs:9`: `#[ignore = "documents current behavior; enable once path-resolution contract is hardened"]`; `core::paths::resolve_absolute_path` lexically collapses `..` across a nonexistent root so `/nonexistent_root/../etc/passwd` resolves to `/etc/passwd`. `resolve_absolute_path` is used for config normalization and (post scanner-v2) not on hot paths.

## Design
- `core/paths.rs`: `resolve_absolute_path` returns `Err(SbhError::InvalidPath)` when any component that must be traversed does not exist, and never collapses `..` past a missing component; callers that accept not-yet-existing paths (lease targets, ballast dirs) use a new `normalize_lexically_within(base, path)` that refuses escapes from `base`. - `tests/regression_path_traversal.rs` (un-ignored): nonexistent root -> error; existing root with `..` inside -> resolved; symlink-loop -> bounded error.

# G8.2 - `sbh docs --json`: generated README/AGENTS tables (defaults, thresholds, constants, commands, env vars, error codes, module map) with a CI drift check

## Context
Every numeric claim in README "How It Works" and every table in AGENTS.md is hand-maintained; about 45 are wrong today. `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh` exists (3.3 KB) but is unused. The repo already has an insta-based snapshot convention.

## Design
- `Command::Docs(DocsArgs { json: bool, section: Option<String>, render: Option<PathBuf> })` (hidden from the main help? No: documented, it is how operators can inspect effective constants). `sbh docs --json` emits a versioned document: `defaults` (full `Config::default()` as TOML and JSON), `pressure_table` (levels, thresholds, scan interval divisor, ballast release counts, batch sizes from `pid.rs::response_policy`), `constants` (PID gains, EWMA base alpha/min/max, guardrail window/thresholds/reward/penalty/clamp/alarm, breaker threshold/cooldown, channel capacities, open-file budgets, walker caps, self-monitor intervals, repeat-deletion defaults, notification intervals, ballast header size/magic/fsync interval), `commands` (from clap: name, about, flags), `env_vars` (from a single `ENV_VARS` registry that `config.rs` reads through, so nothing is read via a bare `env::var` string elsewhere; grep test), `error_codes` (from `errors.rs`), `patterns` (count by category), `module_map` (files under `src/` with line counts, computed at test time, not runtime), `bootstrap.reasons/actions`, `uninstall.modes`, `dashboard.keymap/palette/playbook` (G5.6).
- Rendering: `sbh docs --render README.md` rewrites only the regions between `<!-- sbh-docs:begin <section> -->` / `<!-- sbh-docs:end -->` markers; same for AGENTS.md and docs/testing-and-logging.md (stage table, artifact schema). Prose outside markers is untouched.
- `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh`: build, render into a temp copy, `diff`; non-zero on drift; CI job `docs-drift` (G7.3 registers it); `quality-gate.sh` SOFT stage.
- Constants that are currently literals must become named `pub const`s at the point of use (for example `deletion.rs:76` breaker threshold, `walker.rs:369` result channel cap) so the generator reads the real values.

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs` (command), `src/core/{config,errors}.rs`, `src/monitor/{pid,ewma,guardrails}.rs`, `src/scanner/{deletion,walker,patterns}.rs`, `src/daemon/{loop_main,notifications,self_monitor}.rs`, `src/ballast/manager.rs` (named consts + `docs` collectors), `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh`, README.md/AGENTS.md (markers), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Tests
- Unit: `docs --json` snapshot (insta) so a constant change is a visible diff in review.
- Unit: every `pub const` registered appears in the JSON (registry completeness test).
- Static: README/AGENTS marker regions render byte-identical (the CI check as a cargo test too).
- Grep test: no `env::var("SBH_` outside the registry.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Changing `circuit_breaker_threshold` without re-rendering fails CI.

# G8.4 - CHANGELOG hygiene: `[release]` markers for every published tag, entries for the 13 missing versions, a release-notes generator check

## Context
`CHANGELOG.md` header: "Versions with published GitHub Release assets are marked **[release]**." `gh release list` shows 29 releases; the changelog has 16 version entries; `v0.5.1` (published 2026-08-26) has no marker; missing entirely: v0.4.40, .39, .38, .36, .33, .32, .27, .24, .23, .22, .14, .8, .4, .3, .2, v0.3.17 (13+ of them published). `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh` could host the check.

## Design
- Backfill: for each missing published version, add a short entry from `gh release view <tag> --json body,publishedAt` (body verbatim when present, else "tagged; see commits <range>") marked `[release]`; add the marker to v0.5.1; note hand-published releases (v0.5.0, v0.5.1) explicitly.
- Check: `sbh docs --json` (G8.2) is not the right place (needs network); add `scripts/changelog_check.sh` invoked by the `docs-drift` CI job with `gh` available: every tag with a GitHub release must have a `## v<tag>` heading with `[release]`; every `[release]` heading must correspond to a real release. Non-network fallback: compare against `git tag` only, WARN.
- AGENTS.md "Landing the plane" gains: release tags require a CHANGELOG entry with the marker before tagging (the release workflow's quality gate can grep for it: G4.2).

## Tests
- Script unit test (bash, in `tests/` via a Rust test that shells out, or a `bats`-free inline check): fixture changelog + fixture tag list -> expected exit code.

## Success criteria

title: Claims registry: numeric claims in README prose carry <!-- claim:id --> markers resolved by sbh docs --check (W11)
description:
# G8.7 - Claims registry: numeric claims in README prose carry `<!-- claim:<id> -->` markers resolved by `sbh docs --check`

## Why (ambition round 2)
G8.2 generates *tables*; most of the 45 wrong numbers found on 2026-09-01 live in prose sentences ("Kp=0.25", "after 50 consecutive failures", "capacity 4096", "window of 50 observations", "3 consecutive deletion errors"). A registry lets prose stay prose while every number is checked.

## Design
- Syntax: `... integral cap of <!-- claim:pid.integral_cap -->100.0<!-- /claim --> ...`. `sbh docs --check <files>` (extending G8.2) finds each marker, looks up the id in the `docs --json` document, renders the value with the claim's declared format (`{:.2}`, bytes, duration), and diffs; `--fix` rewrites the value in place between the markers (only the value, never the surrounding prose).
- Registry ids mirror the JSON paths (`constants.pid.kp`, `constants.guardrails.window`, `defaults.pressure.green_min_free_pct`, ...). Unknown ids fail the check.
- Coverage guard: a test lists every bare number in "How It Works" sections that is not inside a claim marker or a generated table and fails when new unmarked numbers appear (allowlist for line numbers, dates, and versions).

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs` (`docs --check/--fix`), README.md/AGENTS.md (markers added while applying G8.3), `scripts/ci_docs_update_check.sh`.

## Tests
- Unit: marker parsing (nested/malformed cases), value rendering per format, `--fix` idempotency.
- Static: README passes `docs --check`; the coverage guard passes.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Changing `Kp` in `loop_main.rs` fails CI until README's sentence is regenerated with `--fix`.

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Test/logging addendum (OliveIbis): the coverage guard test must print every unmarked bare number with file:line; docs --check output lists claim id, expected, found, and the doc line; --fix is idempotent (second run changes nothing) and never touches text outside the markers (property test on random prose around markers).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- Related 12.1 (markers are added during the README pass).

description:
# W13 — Host and fleet rollout

## Plan
1. v0.5.2 (W0 + W4 + W3.1/W3.2): no behavior change; fleet self-updates; verify `sbh status` on every host.
2. v0.6.0 (W1 + W10 + W2 + W5 + W6): behavior change; canary on the operator workstation and one rch VPS for 7 days; gates: deletion success rate >= 90%%, zero source-tree or protected deletions, CPU <= 2%% at Green, zero false Recovery entries; rollback `SBH_BEHAVIOR_PRESET=v0.5`.
3. v0.6.x: W7, W8, W9, W11 incrementally.

## Children
W13.1 workstation runbook · W13.2 fleet canary and rollout record.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Consolidation note (2026-09-02)
A parallel reality check produced the bead tree `bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx` (G0-G12) with overlapping scope. Duplicated children of this epic were closed in favor of the G-tree and their unique details appended there as notes; the remaining children here are the parts the G-tree does not cover. Cross-tree blocking and related edges record the interplay. See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md section 5b.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- Priority P0. Blocked by W1, W2, W4, W5, W6, W10 and 8.1. Children: 14.1 workstation runbook, 14.2 v0.5.2 rollout record, 14.3 v0.6.0 cut, 14.4 v0.6.0 canary/rollout.

# G0 - Operator runbook: put threadripperje back under sbh protection and verify the outcome

## Why a bead
The reality check found the operator's primary host unprotected: `/` Orange at 12% free, `sbh.service` inactive since 2026-08-30 behind `/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED`, empty reserve on `/`, no scannable root on `/`, and a false `daemon_running=true`. Code fixes (G1, G3) are necessary but the outcome must be executed and verified on the host, not assumed.

## Preconditions
G1.1, G1.2, G1.3, G1.4, G1.5 (CPU proof green), G3.1 (READY=1) released and installed (`sbh version` shows the new version).

## Checklist (operator-run; each step records output in this bead's comments)
1. `sudo sbh doctor --system --json` -> note FAILs.
2. `sudo sbh config validate --strict` -> fix `[scoring.weights]` -> `[scoring] *_weight` (G8.1 will flag it) and enable `scanner.catalog_roots_on_pressured_device = true`.
3. `sudo sbh install --systemd --scope system` -> regenerated hardened unit; `sbh doctor --service` reports no drift and lists foreign drop-ins (`10-scanner-v2.conf`, `hotloop-guard.conf`, `zz-hotloop-disabled.conf`, `system.control/*`); decide which to keep (recommend: drop the hotloop gates and keep CPUQuota until G1.5 passes on this host).
4. Operator only: remove `/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED` (this bead does not authorize any agent to delete it).
5. `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl start sbh && systemctl status sbh` -> `active (running)`, `Type=notify` reached READY.
6. `sudo sbh ballast provision --json` -> reserve on `/` with `skipped_for_floor` explained.
7. `sbh status --json` -> `daemon_running=true reason=locked`; `/` `reclaim_capability=catalog`, `reserve_state.present_bytes > 0`.
8. Watch 10 minutes: `systemctl show sbh -p CPUUsageNSec` delta < 6 s (1%); journal shows one catalog scan and no repeated back-off lines.
9. `sbh explain --last 5` (G2) shows the catalog decisions and vetoes.
10. Record before/after `df -h /` and attach `sbh stats --window 1h --json`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Steps 5-8 verified with pasted outputs.
- [ ] Reality-check doc section 4 "Live-host evidence" gets an "after" block.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.2
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.14.1, closed as duplicate): add a 60-minute foreground dry run before enabling the service (`SBH_SCANNER_DRY_RUN=1 sbh daemon --config /etc/sbh/config.toml`, review `decision` events); keep the CPUQuota drop-in until the CPU harness passes on this host; candidate `/`-resident roots: /var/tmp, ~/.cache, ~/.cargo/registry/cache (run `sbh scan <root> --explain` first); success = 7 days active with `sbh stats` showing reclaims on `/` and `/data/tmp`, no kill switch re-created, CPU < 2% at Green.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- DECISION: primary remedy for `/` is catalog roots (2.12, default-on); explicit `/var/tmp` and `~/.cache` roots only after `sbh scan <root> --explain`; `cross_devices = true` is NOT used.
- CPU: run the daemon CPU-budget scenarios (11.1) on the workstation and attach output; the CPUQuota drop-in is removed only after step 8 holds for 7 days. Two CPU numbers kept and labelled: 10-minute step check < 1%%; 7-day gate < 2%% (2.11's bound).

title: Priority pre-scan ages candidates by mtime while the walker uses tree idleness (birth time included)
description: Found by the daemon e2e orange-reclaim scenario (tests/daemon_e2e.rs): a Definite target created seconds ago whose mtimes were set five hours back is deleted by the startup priority pre-scan within a second of start, while the walker's age = max(mtime, birth time, tree newest mtime) rule (bead 2.10) would hold it for min_file_age_minutes. Impact: a tree freshly copied/extracted with preserved old mtimes is deletable by the pre-scan only. Fix: the pre-scan's ScoringInput must use the same tree-idleness age as the walker (src/daemon/loop_main.rs priority pre-scan block; src/scanner/walker.rs tree_newest_mtime/entry_metadata). Acceptance: unit test with a just-created target whose mtimes are old is not dispatched by the pre-scan under min_file_age_minutes=1; the e2e orange scenario then reclaims only after the gate (it currently tolerates both paths).
close_reason: Closed by the implementing agent, not independently verified. Commit 52b2398: prescan_age() applies the walker's rule (mtime, birth time, bounded tree probe) in the priority pre-scan. Evidence: new unit test scanner_prescan_holds_a_young_tree_with_old_mtimes failed at the dispatch assertion before the change and passes after; daemon::loop_main tests 90/90; clippy clean on the file; e2e orange-reclaim and host-layout scenarios pass locally against the rebuilt daemon (the orange reclaim now happens after the one-minute gate via the forced scan instead of at startup). Deviation: on filesystems without birth time the unit test prints a note and returns, since the rule has nothing to hold on to there.

title: W1: Make the daemon reclaim before the cliff (per-mount control, behavior matrix, definite artifacts, ballast plan)
description:
# W1 — Make the daemon reclaim before the cliff

## Root causes (verified in code and reproduced in a sandbox with the v0.5.1 binary)
- R1 The memory x disk behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs `DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS`, `from_disk_pressure` maps Yellow|Orange -> Warn) makes Yellow/Orange `IdentifyOnly` with ballast `None` at normal memory. `behavior_allows_delete_dispatch` (src/daemon/loop_main.rs:1449) then blocks every deletion until Red.
- R2 The Green arm (loop_main.rs:2852-2915) dispatches a scan only when the predictive policy is not `Clear` or the policy is in FallbackSafe; stale artifacts accumulate until Yellow.
- R3 The device-affinity gate (loop_main.rs:2812-2839) `return`s for the whole tick when the pressured mount has no root_path; a foreign Orange mount starves all other work. Sandbox: 0 scans of a healthy /data root in 45 s while `/` is Orange.
- R4 Ballast provisioning refuses below a flat 20%% free (src/ballast/manager.rs:36 MIN_FREE_PCT) and the daemon never retries; the operator workstation's `/` pool has been empty for months.
- R5 A canonical stale cargo target (valid CACHEDIR.TAG, deps/incremental/.fingerprint, 64 MiB, no open files, in a temp root) scores 0.6475 -> `Review`; the daemon only dispatches `Delete`.
- R6 Special-location alerts are percent-only and unthrottled: 35,692 `error/critical` events in three days for /data/tmp on a 5.5 TiB volume at 13.9%% free.
- R7 With nothing actionable at Red the tick tightens to 100-125 ms; the daemon consumed 33 s CPU in 5 min pinned to its 10%% quota — the spin the operator disabled it over.
- R8 `SkipReason::NotWritable` hides EROFS/ENOSPC; 10,362 such skips as root, retried for hours, while the one action that still works (ballast release + alert) never happened.

## Target end state
A daemon that (a) maintains at Green on a slow cadence, (b) starts deleting definite artifacts and releasing ballast at Orange, (c) never lets one mount starve another, (d) provisions as much reserve as fits, (e) is measurably idle when idle, and (f) treats a read-only or metadata-exhausted volume as an incident, not a retry loop.

## Children
W1.1 MountController state machine · W1.2 behavior matrix presets and config · W1.3 definite-artifact certainty + fast lane · W1.4 Green maintenance + VOI wiring (Q6) · W1.5 ballast provisioning plan + shared discovery (Q1) · W1.6 special-location horizon rule (Q2) · W1.7 failure classification + Recovery + failure e-process (Q8) · W1.8 truthful events + state.json v2 rates · W1.9 per-mount PID feedforward/gain scheduling/anti-windup (Q3) · W1.10 opaque-root idleness (Q5) · W1.11 CPU budget invariant (Q7).

## Acceptance (measured by the W10 daemon e2e on Linux and macOS)
- Host layout (pressured `/` without root_paths, healthy `/data` root): `/data` root scanned within `maintenance_interval_secs`; CPU < 2%% over 60 s; `state.json` names the observe-only mount and idle reason.
- Orange on a root's mount: the stale fixture is deleted within one scan cycle; fresh, `.git`, open-file, leased fixtures survive; ballast on that mount released; `artifact_delete ok=true` and `ballast_released` events with decision ids.
- Read-only bind-mount root: batch stops on first `FilesystemReadOnly`; ballast released; Critical notification; no retries for 5 min.
- Mount at 12%% free with orange at 10%%: pool created with the files that fit, health `partial`.
- Special location at 13.9%% free on 5.5 TiB: zero alerts; at 10 GiB free: one warning per 15 min.

## Rollout
Ship with `[behavior] preset = "v0.6"` default and `SBH_BEHAVIOR_PRESET=v0.5` env override; 7-day canary on the operator workstation with daily review of `sbh stats --window 24h` (deletion success rate >= 90%%, zero source-tree/protected deletions), CPU, idle reasons; fleet after W4.

(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G1 - Host protection: a system disk that fills from $HOME while below the ballast floor must still be protected

## Background (from the 2026-09-01 reality check)
The operator's primary workstation is the exact scenario `sbh` was written for and it is unprotected:
- `/` (btrfs, 977 GB) at 12% free -> Orange. Consumers: `~/.local/share` 199 GiB, `~/.rustup` 33.6 GiB, `/usr` 29.7, `/opt` 17, `/var/lib/snapd` 8.8. None is under a configured scan root.
- `scanner.root_paths` (default and fleet-synced config) = `/tmp` (tmpfs) and `/data/tmp` (on `/data`). With `cross_devices=false`, `daemon/loop_main.rs:2801-2840` logs "pressure on / (Orange) but no scannable root_path resides on that device; cannot reclaim - backing off" once per interval and returns. Defaults deliberately exclude `$HOME` and `/data/projects` after the 2026-05-16/22 source-tree deletion incidents (`core/config.rs:655-670`, CHANGELOG v0.4.25).
- `BallastManager::provision` refuses when free < `MIN_FREE_PCT = 20.0` (`ballast/manager.rs:36`), a flat percent, all-or-nothing, so the pressured volume can never obtain a reserve once it is already low. `/var/lib/sbh/ballast` is empty; `doctor --system` FAILs `ballast.reserve`. `/data/.sbh/ballast` has 5 x 2 GiB (fine, but `/data` is at 45% free).
- `/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED` (re-created 2026-08-30): "sbh logs 'ballast provision skipped: free space too low (<20%)' then sits in Red urgency and spins at 100% of a core. Remove only once / is above ~20% free. A CPUQuota=10% backstop is also set." The unit is gated by `ConditionPathExists=!/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED`.
- `sbh status --json` reports `daemon_running: true` while `sbh.service` has been inactive since 2026-08-30 14:59. `detect_daemon_running_fallback` (`cli_app.rs:7031-7070`) scans `/proc/*/cmdline` for any process containing both "sbh" and "daemon"; it matched the auditor's shell. The operator has no reserve, no reclaim, and a green light.

## Goal
Under the conditions above the daemon must (1) build a bounded reserve without violating pressure thresholds, (2) reclaim from known-safe cache locations on the pressured device even when no root is configured there, (3) tell the truth about its own liveness and about "I cannot help this mount", and (4) provably not spin.

## Design summary (details in child beads)
1. Graduated reserve (G1.1): per-file admission against a reserve floor derived from the pressure thresholds; smaller files in the low-space band; never at Red/Critical.
2. Catalog roots (G1.2): when pressure is on a device with no configured root, derive opaque, catalog-listed cache roots for that device from the PAL cleanup catalog (Linux catalog expanded; macOS catalog reused) and run a bounded catalog-only scan under all existing vetoes.
3. Liveness truth (G1.3): daemon holds an exclusive flock on `<state_dir>/daemon.lock`; CLI probes it; the `/proc` substring heuristic is removed; `status` reports a reason and service gates.
4. Loud degradation (G1.4): "pressured mount has no scannable root" is a doctor FAIL, a status field, and a notification.
5. Proof (G1.5, G1.6): a daemon-binary integration harness measuring CPU time and scan dispatch; unit/integration/e2e tests with structured logs.

## Why not just tell operators to add roots?
Because the operator did not, the fleet config sync did not, and the product stayed silent. Safety of catalog roots comes from the same hardcoded vetoes that made `/data/projects` safe again (`deletion.rs` `HardcodedSourceTree`, `LooksLikeSourceCode`, `.git`, open-file, lease checks) plus the opaque/no-descent rule: catalog scanning never enumerates unknown trees.

## Acceptance for the epic
All children closed; the reality-check row V26 re-audited WORKING; G0 runbook executed on this host.
