# G9 - Policy engine semantics: make the progressive-delivery safeguards the docs describe real, configurable, and tested

## Background (2026-09-01 audit of `src/daemon/policy.rs`)
README L1023-1054 and AGENTS.md describe observe -> canary -> enforce with automatic demotion to FallbackSafe on calibration breach (3 consecutive Fail windows), guardrail drift, canary budget exhaustion (>10/hour), serialization failure, and kill switch; explicit promotion only ("the system never auto-promotes"); recovery after 3 clean windows to Canary. Code:
- `initial_mode` default is `Enforce` (`:149`), not Observe.
- `calibration_breach_windows = 25` (`:154`) and the breach path is advisory-only: it logs "continuing in current mode" and never demotes (`:760-768`); the counter hard-resets at 100 (`:747`).
- `FallbackReason::CanaryBudgetExhausted` and `FallbackReason::SerializationFailure` are never constructed in production (only in `decision_plane_tests.rs`); canary overflow returns `Keep` (`:1047`) and nothing else.
- E-process alarm demotes only when pressure >= Orange and >= 30 observations (`:1074-1079`).
- `check_emergency_escalation` auto-promotes FallbackSafe -> Enforce after 5 min at Yellow+ with a 30-min grace (`:441`, `:788-822`), contradicting "never auto-promotes".
- `recovery_clean_windows` default 10 (`:153`) plus `min_fallback_secs = 300` (`:155`).
- Guardrails (`monitor/guardrails.rs:143-258`): window 500 (doc 50), Pass after 60 observations (doc 10), reward `ln(2/3)` (doc `ln(0.8)`), penalty severity-scaled, clamp [-5.0, 3.5] (doc [-5, 5]); the fleet log on this host showed `guard=PASS(e=14.9 med_err=0.00 cons=100% obs=215)` 5 minutes after a fresh start at Orange, 75% of the way to the alarm (20.0) with perfect median error.

These relaxations were incident-driven (a fleet that runs Enforce and cannot afford to stop reclaiming). They are legitimate design choices, but the docs describe a different product, dead enum variants suggest unfinished work, and the e-process observation is unexplained.

## Decision (recorded; operator may override)
Restore the documented safeguards as configurable behavior with defaults that keep the existing fleet unchanged: new installs get the safe defaults (Observe first, demote on breach, no auto-promotion beyond Canary); configs that set `initial_mode = "enforce"` keep today's behavior unless they opt in.

## Children
G9.1 configurable fallback actions and auto-recovery target, wiring the dead variants; G9.2 guardrail steady-Orange regression (explain or fix e=14.9); G9.3 docs regeneration and the initial_mode wizard decision.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Priorities: 2.8, 2.10 and 3.1 raised to P0 (11.2's assertions depend on them).

title: Per-mount MountController state machine and tick cadence rule (ends device-affinity starvation and idle spin)
description:
# MountController: ObserveOnly / Maintain / Reclaim / Recovery / Idle per mount

## Background
Today one PID/EWMA drives the whole daemon off the worst mount (`response.causing_mount`, `response.level`), and the device-affinity gate at src/daemon/loop_main.rs:2812-2839 returns early for the entire tick when that mount has no root_path. On the operator workstation `/` (12%% free, no root_path) therefore suppresses all work on `/data/tmp` and the tick cadence still follows the Orange interval. Sandbox proof: 0 scans in 45 s.

## Design
New module src/daemon/mount_controller.rs:
- `struct MountController { mount: PathBuf, fs_type, pid: PidController, ewma: EwmaEstimator, state: MountState, level, urgency, idle_reason: Option<IdleReason>, last_action: Option<Instant>, backoff: ExponentialBackoff }`.
- `enum MountState { ObserveOnly, Maintain, Reclaim, Recovery, Idle }`.
- One controller per mount that owns a root_path, a ballast pool, a special location, or the state/config dir. Mounts with none of those are ObserveOnly: reported and notified, never drive scans, never tighten the tick.
- Transitions per tick: Maintain->Reclaim when level >= Yellow or predictive `seconds_to_red <= action_horizon` with confidence >= min; Reclaim->Maintain after `recovery_clean_windows` Green ticks; *->Recovery on executor `BatchOutcome::RecoveryNeeded(mount)`; Recovery->Reclaim when a 4 KiB probe write to `<mount>/.sbh/probe` succeeds and free >= red_min; *->Idle when a full pass yields zero dispatchable candidates and no releasable ballast; Idle->Maintain|Reclaim on dirty event roots, SIGUSR1, reload, or after `min_rescan_interval x 2^n` (cap 1 h).
- Cadence contribution: ObserveOnly/Idle/Maintain -> base poll; Reclaim -> PID interval with existing floors; Recovery -> 30 s. Global tick = min over mounts not in ObserveOnly/Idle. This is invariant 10 of the master epic.
- The monitor loop dispatches scans/ballast per mount; the `causing_mount` singleton becomes `Vec<MountResponse>`; `state.json` (W1.8) records per-mount state and idle_reason; `sbh status` prints them.

## Acceptance
- Table-driven unit tests cover every transition and the cadence rule.
- Integration test with `MockPlatform` multi-mount stats: mount A Orange without root_path, mount B Green with root_path -> B stays Maintain and is scanned on the maintenance cadence; tick stays at base poll; A is ObserveOnly with idle_reason `no_root_path_on_device`.
- W10 host-layout scenario passes.

## Notes
Keep `cross_devices = true` semantics: when enabled, a pressured mount may drive scans of all roots (fallback to all paths) as today.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Design-consistency note (OliveIbis, refinement pass): the folded 'catalog roots' bead (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.12) changes the ObserveOnly semantics: a mount with no configured root_path and no pool is ObserveOnly only when catalog derivation also yields nothing on that device; when catalog roots exist the mount has a bounded catalog surface and may enter Maintain/Reclaim with catalog_only scans. Please express that as a state-machine input (surface = configured | catalog | none) so the two beads compose, and log idle_reason=no_surface vs surface=catalog distinctly.
- DECISION (folded): the state machine takes `surface: Configured | Catalog | None` as an input; `ObserveOnly` applies only when surface is None; a Catalog surface admits Maintain/Reclaim with `catalog_only` scans; idle_reason distinguishes `no_surface` from `surface=catalog`.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: a mount with derivable catalog roots (2.12) has a work surface (`surface = Catalog`, `reclaim_capability = catalog`) and enters Reclaim at Yellow+ with catalog-only scans; ObserveOnly applies only when the surface is None. 2.12 depends on this bead (both rewrite the B5 branch).
- DECISION: dedicated key `[pressure] reclaim_exit_clean_ticks` (not the `[policy] recovery_clean_windows` key).
- Logging: activity event `mount_state_transition {mount, from, to, reason}` plus a `[SBH-MOUNT]` line, asserted in the MockPlatform integration test (master invariant 2).
- Controllers are keyed by `st_dev`; `BatchOutcome::RecoveryNeeded(mount)` maps by the candidate's device id; `cross_devices = true` makes every mount with any configured root a work surface.
close_reason: Implemented in 2caad46 by the implementing agent; not independently verified. src/daemon/mount_controller.rs (pure state machine + global_tick, 8 unit tests incl. table-driven transitions and the cadence rule) wired into loop_main: per-mount handle_pressure returning the global tick, note_scan_pass_per_mount -> Idle backoff, reload/SIGUSR1 wake, probe write for Recovery, state.json mount_controllers + all-mount pressure, sbh status Mount Control table + JSON. Sandbox evidence (cross_devices=false, / Orange with no root/pool, /data Orange with root): / observe_only idle_reason=no_root_path_on_device (one rate-limited log line), /data observe_only->reclaim, scanned, deleted stale target (100MB), ->idle nothing_to_reclaim rescan 90s; tick stayed at base poll (no hot loop). Caveat: in that run both mounts were Orange, so it is not a strict before/after of the original '0 scans in 45s' proof. Not done: executor write-failure -> Recovery signal (2.7), catalog surface (2.12), Green maintenance-cadence scans (2.4: Maintain does not scan yet), dirty-root wake, and a MockPlatform multi-mount daemon integration test (covered at controller level instead).

title: Opaque-root idleness estimator replaces birth time as directory age (Q5)
description:
# Age must mean "nothing inside changed since"

## Background
`EntryMetadata::effective_age_timestamp` (src/scanner/walker.rs:125-131) uses birth time for directories. That made rch pool dirs look maximally abandoned while builds wrote into them (v0.5.1 changelog), and in the sandbox both a "stale" and a "fresh" fixture reported the same 42-minute age because both directories were created together. v0.5.1 added a recursive idle probe only for rch marker dirs (`rch_tree_activity`, 400k-entry cap).

## Design
`tree_idle_since(p)`: bounded reservoir sample of up to 64 entries over the first 4,096 readdir results at depth <= 3, max mtime among them combined with the root's own mtime; `effective_age = now - max(sampled_max_mtime, root_mtime)`; birth time only as a lower bound. Applied to every opaque candidate root; deterministic under a seed for tests; syscall cap documented.

## Acceptance
Property test: a tree with one fresh leaf never reports idle longer than that leaf's age (exact for k >= tree size); sandbox fixtures now separate: stale (5 h mtimes) vs fresh (now) get different ages; rch tests unchanged.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

title: CPU budget as an invariant across threads (Q7): token bucket charging, idle reasons, and an e2e CPU assertion
description:
# CPU budget as an invariant across threads (Q7)

The proof harness (tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs) is owned by bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.5; this bead owns the in-daemon mechanism that makes the budget hold.

## Problem
The duty-cycle limiter (`duty_cycle_idle_debt`, `max_scan_duty_cycle_pct` 25) bounds walker passes only; prescans, index work, the monitor tick, and the 100-125 ms Red/Critical cadence are uncharged. Operator host: 33 s CPU in 5 min at Orange with nothing to do, pinned to `CPUQuota=10%`; kill switch followed.

## Design
One token bucket (rate = max_scan_duty_cycle_pct/100 cores, burst 5 s) charged by scanner, prescan, maintenance, index and monitor-tick time; per-mount Idle/ObserveOnly cadence (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.1) removes the tightened tick when nothing is actionable; `state.json.cpu_secs_total` from PAL self_stats and `daemon.idle_reason` exposed; documented bound: over any 60 s window CPU <= rate + burst amortized.

## Acceptance
G1.5 scenarios: host layout 60 s -> cpu_secs_total/wall <= 0.02; Orange with bounded work -> <= 0.33. Unit: bucket accounting.

# G1.5 - Steady-state CPU and no-spin proof harness for the daemon binary

## Context
The design doc (docs/scanner-redesign-event-driven.md section 7) requires "< 1% of one core averaged over 10 min" at Green with no FS activity, and the operator kill switch on this host cites a spin at Red urgency when the pressured volume has no root and no reserve. `loop_main.rs` has a duty-cycle limiter (:404-482), an empty-pass back-off (:5362), and the B5 device-affinity gate (:2801-2840), each unit-tested in isolation, but nothing measures the whole daemon's CPU under the failing scenario. The last real run consumed 33 s CPU in 5 min with a `CPUQuota=10%` cap (consistent with saturating the quota).

## Goal
A reusable integration harness that runs the real `sbh daemon` binary against a synthetic environment for N seconds, samples its CPU time (`/proc/<pid>/stat` utime+stime, or rusage via `wait4`), counts scan dispatches from the JSONL log, and asserts budgets. It becomes the regression net for every hot-loop fix (v0.4.29, v0.4.38, v0.5.0, #15 all addressed spins).

## Design
- `tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs` (new, Linux; skipped elsewhere with a logged reason): helper `DaemonRun::start(config_toml, env) -> handle` using `CARGO_BIN_EXE_sbh`, temp state/log dirs, small `poll_interval_ms`; `handle.cpu_seconds()`; `handle.jsonl_events()`; `handle.stop()` (SIGTERM, wait, assert exit 0).
- Scenarios: (a) Green, no FS activity, 60 s -> CPU < 0.6 s (1%), zero scans; (b) synthetic Orange on a device with no root and no reserve (config pointing `root_paths` off-device and a tiny tmpfs fixture as the "pressured" mount, or a debug-only `SBH_TEST_FORCE_PRESSURE=<mount>=<free_pct>` override gated behind `cfg!(debug_assertions)`) -> CPU < 1%, zero scan dispatches, exactly one `no_scannable_root` event per epoch; (c) with G1.2 catalog roots enabled -> exactly one bounded catalog scan per epoch.
- Every scenario writes a JSON artifact (`$SBH_TEST_ARTIFACT_DIR/daemon-cpu-<scenario>.json`: cpu_seconds, wall, events, dispatches, rss_peak) matching the style of the scanner-v2 validation artifacts, so CI uploads it.
- Wire into CI (`ci.yml` `stress` job or a new `daemon-budget` job) and `scripts/quality-gate.sh` as a HARD stage.

## Files
`tests/daemon_cpu_budget.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` (helpers), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (test-only pressure override if needed, clearly gated), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/quality-gate.sh`, docs/testing-and-logging.md.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Scenario (b) fails on the commit before the fix that the kill-switch note describes (bisect once, document) and passes after G1.1/G1.2/G1.4.
- [ ] Artifacts uploaded in CI; budget numbers documented in a "Daemon budgets" section of docs/tui-acceptance-gates-and-budgets.md.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.5
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.11, design; this bead owns the harness): charge scanner, prescan, maintenance, index and monitor-tick time to one token bucket (rate = max_scan_duty_cycle_pct/100 cores, burst 5 s) and expose `cpu_secs_total` in state.json; budgets: <= 2% of wall at Green/host-layout, <= 33% under sustained Orange with bounded work (Q7 in the 2026-09-02 plan). Suggested harness scenarios beyond (a)-(c): sustained Orange with a stale Definite fixture (work present) and Red with an empty pool (emergency events must be emitted once, not 100 times/min as on 2026-08-18).

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- OliveIbis note (from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.7): the budget should exempt ballast release, state writes, sd_notify heartbeats and the control socket, log once per minute at most when exceeded, surface status.daemon.cpu_budget {pct, used_pct_1m, deficit_secs}, and notify at Warning after 5 consecutive minutes over budget.
- Verification addendum (OliveIbis, refinement pass): (a) unit: token-bucket arithmetic (refill from wall time, drain from rusage deltas), yield computation, unlimited at Critical, protected operations (ballast release, state write, sd_notify heartbeat, control socket) never yield; (b) property: for any pressure-level sequence the protected operations run within their cadence regardless of bucket state; (c) integration (W10 runner): scanner made deliberately expensive (fixture with 200k entries, max_scan_duty_cycle_pct=100) stays under 2% at Green because of the budget, and the once-per-minute '[SBH-DAEMON] cpu budget exceeded pct=.. deficit_secs=.. level=..' line appears exactly once per minute; (d) status.daemon.cpu_budget {pct, used_pct_1m, deficit_secs} asserted in JSON; (e) notification at Warning after 5 consecutive over-budget minutes with throttling test; (f) e2e: the kill-switch scenario from threadripperje (Orange, no root, no reserve) shows < 1% CPU with no systemd quota.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: one daemon runner and one injection mechanism: the CPU harness scenarios move into 11.1's `tests/common` runner with `SBH_TEST_FS_STATS`; this bead is the in-daemon token bucket + `cpu_secs_total` only; blocked by 11.1; related 2.12 (catalog scenario).

title: Catalog roots: reclaim from known-safe caches on a pressured device that has no configured root (W1)
description:
# G1.2 - Catalog roots: reclaim from known-safe cache locations on a pressured device that has no configured scan root

## Context
`daemon/loop_main.rs:2801-2840` (B5 device-affinity gate): under elevated pressure on a device with no `root_path` and `cross_devices=false`, the daemon logs once per `DEVICE_AFFINITY_WARN_INTERVAL` and returns; no ballast handling, no scan. This is deliberate (it replaced a hot loop that scanned unrelated roots) but it leaves the pressured volume untouched. On the operator's host `/` fills from `$HOME` caches while roots are `/tmp` and `/data/tmp`. The macOS PAL already has a rich cleanup catalog (`platform/macos/cleanup_catalog.rs`, 28 rules: Xcode DerivedData, Electron caches, release-work buildroots); Linux has 7 (`platform/linux/cleanup_catalog.rs`). The catalog is used as a classifier, not as a root source.

## Goal

title: Quarantine-first deletion at Green/Yellow with sbh undo <decision-id> (W1)
description:
# G14 - Quarantine-first deletion at Green/Yellow with `sbh undo ` ## Why (ambition round 1) On 2026-05-16 and 2026-05-22 the scanner deleted ~87 working trees and ~28 crate directories (CHANGELOG v0.4.25). Hardcoded vetoes now make that specific mistake impossible, but the next mis-scoring will also be unrecoverable, because deletion is immediate even when there is no pressure. At Green and Yellow there is time; use it. ## Design - `scanner/deletion.rs`: `DeletionMode::{Quarantine, Unlink}` chosen per batch by the daemon: Quarantine when level is Green or Yellow (and for manual `clean` unless `--no-quarantine`), Unlink at Orange+ and in `emergency`. Quarantine = `rename` the candidate into `/.sbh/quarantine//` on the same filesystem (never cross-device; if the mount's quarantine dir cannot be created, fall back to Unlink with a logged reason and a `quarantine_unavailable` flag in the record). Ballast release is never quarantined. - Metadata: `/.json` with original path, dev/ino, size estimate, quarantined_at, expires_at, decision snapshot. The quarantine root carries `.sbh-protect` and is excluded from scoring; `du`-style accounting (`status.reserve_state.quarantined_bytes`) reports it as "reclaimable on demand". - Drain: expired entries (`scanner.quarantine_ttl_hours`, default 24) are unlinked by the executor on Green ticks; when pressure reaches Orange the quarantine is drained oldest-first *before* any new deletion (instant, already-decided space); `emergency` drains it first too. - `sbh undo | --path

| --all-since `: restores by rename (refuses if the original path now exists, unless `--force-suffix`), updates the decision record outcome to `restored`, logs `[SBH-UNDO]`. `sbh explain` shows `quarantined_until` / `restored_at`. `sbh scan --json` and the dashboard Candidates screen show a `quarantined` badge. - Config: `scanner.quarantine_enabled` (default true), `scanner.quarantine_ttl_hours`, `scanner.quarantine_max_bytes_pct` (default 5% of the volume; beyond it the executor unlinks oldest first). ## Files `src/scanner/deletion.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (`undo`, `clean --no-quarantine`, `emergency` drain), `src/scanner/decision_record.rs` (outcome variants), `src/scanner/protection.rs` (quarantine root protected), `src/core/config.rs`, README (Safety Layers gains "Layer 7: quarantine and undo"), AGENTS.md. ## Tests - Unit: mode selection by level; rename within device; cross-device refusal; fallback to unlink with flag; TTL drain; oldest-first drain under Orange; max-bytes cap. - Unit: `undo` restores byte-identical tree (hash before/after), refuses when target exists, `--force-suffix` path. - Integration: daemon at Green deletes a fixture target -> it is in quarantine, space not freed; pressure raised to Orange -> quarantine drained before new candidates; `explain` shows the transitions. - e2e: `clean` at Green then `undo`; `emergency` drains quarantine first. - Property: for any sequence of quarantine/drain/undo operations, no path is ever both present at its original location and in quarantine. ## Success criteria - [ ] The May incident replayed on a fixture (a mis-scored source tree at Green) is fully recoverable with one command. ## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass) - DECISION: quarantine at Green and for manual `clean` only; Unlink at Yellow+ (Yellow is the "we need space" signal). 6.2's derived `ReadWritePaths` must include `/.sbh` (not only `.sbh/ballast`). - Semantics: `artifact_delete {ok: true, quarantined: true, freed_bytes: 0}`; `stats` counts quarantines as successes and reports `quarantined_bytes` separately; the W1 rollout gate counts them as success.
close_reason:
Closed by the implementing agent, not independently verified.

Delivered (commits 9e81e65 + follow-up): src/scanner/quarantine.rs QuarantineStore (rename into <root>/.sbh/quarantine/<decision-id>/<basename> beside <decision-id>.json, .sbh-protect marker on the store root, same-device check, records/held_bytes/purge/drain_expired/drain_oldest/drain_all/enforce_cap/restore/record_for_path, quarantine_root_for = longest configured scan root containing the path, mount point only as fallback). Executor: DeletionMode {Unlink, Quarantine} on DeletionConfig and DeletionPlan, CheckedDeletion::Quarantined for the interactive paths, fallback removes for good and logs quarantine_unavailable reason=<cross_device|root error> as an info event; report items_quarantined/bytes_quarantined/quarantine_unavailable. Daemon: Green batches quarantine when scanner.quarantine_enabled (SharedExecutorConfig atomics, reloaded on SIGHUP); sweep_quarantines drains every store on an Orange/Red/Critical mount each tick (before the tick's scan) and once a minute expires entries (quarantine_ttl_hours) and caps the store (quarantine_max_bytes_pct of the volume) on Green/Yellow; reserve_state.quarantined_bytes in state.json. CLI: sbh undo <id> | --path P | --all-since W | --list [--force-suffix] [--root R] (rename back, refuses an existing original unless suffixed, ledger effective_action='restored', [SBH-UNDO] lines), clean --no-quarantine, clean summary/JSON fields, emergency drains every root's quarantine before scanning. Events: artifact_delete quarantined=true with details "quarantined" and no bytes freed; stats quarantined_count/quarantined_bytes with total_bytes_freed excluding held bytes. README Layer 7 + command row + config keys; AGENTS.md rows.

Evidence: 7 quarantine unit tests incl. the never-both-present property (300 random ops), 2 executor tests (hold under the scan root; unusable store -> removed for good with quarantine_unavailable=1), integration test clean_quarantines_at_green_and_undo_restores_the_target (clean --yes quarantines target/debug, undo --list, undo <id> restores the same entry count, second undo fails, --no-quarantine removes for good), e2e scenario green_quarantine_holds_the_stale_target_and_orange_drains_it_first (both stale targets held at Green, quarantined_bytes in state.json, Orange drains "2 entries" before the orange_pressure scan; ~4.5 min) — PASSED on binaries built from HEAD bb238cf (2026-09-02 21:29, 204 s; the first run exposed that a Green maintenance history had backed off the first Orange scan, fixed by resetting the empty-pass backoff when pressure rises over the last completed pass, `pressure_escalated` in loop_main.rs). Clippy on HEAD clean. cargo test --lib 1545 passed, --bin sbh 132 passed, clippy --all-targets clean.

Deviations from the bead text: (1) the store lives under the scan root (`<root>/.sbh/quarantine`), not the mount point; the mount point is the fallback when no configured root contains the candidate, so catalog roots outside the scan roots may hit an unwritable mount root and fall back to removal with a logged reason. (2) Quarantine applies at Green only (the bead body); Yellow removes for good. (3) No activity event for undo (stderr + ledger update only) and `sbh explain` does not show quarantine state. (4) No env overrides for the three config keys. (5) The emergency drain is unit-covered (drain_all) but not e2e-tested. (6) The daemon quarantines Definite candidates decided at Green including a git project's stale target (that is existing scanner behavior, the e2e asserts it).

title: Adaptive conformal time-to-exhaustion intervals drive urgency; guardrail conservatism becomes empirical coverage (W1, complements Q3/Q4)
description:
# G15 - Adaptive conformal time-to-exhaustion intervals drive urgency; guardrail "conservatism" becomes empirical coverage

## Why (ambition round 3)
`monitor/predictive.rs` and `pid.rs` act on a *point* TTE (urgency floors 1.0/0.90/0.70 at horizon/30, /6, /2). `monitor/guardrails.rs` judges a window "conservative" if predicted TTE <= actual TTE and folds that into a heuristic "conservative fraction >= 0.70" threshold; the e-process then alarms on streaks. There is no stated error rate for early action and no principled definition of miscalibration. Conformal prediction gives exactly that: a lower bound `TTE_lo` with a coverage guarantee that needs no distributional assumption, and adaptive conformal inference (ACI) keeps the guarantee under distribution shift (a build burst), which is the regime that matters here. The README already advertises "Guardrails (conformal/e-process)".

## Design
- `monitor/conformal.rs` (new module): online split-conformal over nonconformity scores `s_t = max(0, TTE_pred_t - TTE_actual_t) / TTE_pred_t` (relative under-prediction of time), with a bounded window (500, matching the guardrail) and ACI update `alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma * (alpha_target - err_t)` where `err_t = 1[actual < TTE_lo]`, `gamma = 0.01`, `alpha_target = 0.10` (config `pressure.prediction.coverage_target = 0.90`). `TTE_lo = TTE_pred * (1 - q_{1-alpha}(s))`. Actual TTE is observable only in hindsight; use the existing guardrail observation windows (which already pair predictions with outcomes) as the calibration stream; when a window has no exhaustion, use the censored bound the way the guardrail does today (documented).
- Wiring: `pid.rs` predictive boost keys off `TTE_lo` (falls back to point TTE while fewer than 30 calibration samples exist; reported as `coverage_state = warming`); `status.forecast = { tte_point_s, tte_lo_s, coverage_target, coverage_empirical, alpha, samples }`; decision records (G2) include `tte_lo` and coverage at decision time; guardrail: replace `min_conservative_fraction` with `coverage_empirical >= coverage_target - tolerance` (tolerance 0.05) and keep the e-process as the anytime-valid alarm on coverage failure (reward/penalty per covered/uncovered observation); G9.2's idle-neutrality rule applies (no calibration sample when the rate is below the noise floor).
- Reserve sizing (G1.7) uses the same quantile machinery for fill over the horizon.
- No new dependencies; ~300 lines plus tests.

## Files
`src/monitor/conformal.rs` (new), `src/monitor/{predictive,pid,guardrails,ewma}.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/scanner/decision_record.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (status), `src/core/config.rs`, README guardrails/control-loop sections (G8.3), docs/internal/pressure-mapping.md.

## Tests
- Unit: on i.i.d. synthetic residuals, empirical coverage within 2% of target after 1,000 samples; under a step change in fill rate, ACI recovers coverage within 100 samples while a fixed-alpha conformal set does not (regression asserting the adaptive advantage).
- Unit: warming state below 30 samples; idle samples excluded; censoring rule.
- Unit (`pid.rs`): boosts key off `TTE_lo`; a wide interval triggers earlier than the point estimate; property: `TTE_lo <= TTE_point` always.
- Integration (`tests/stress_tests.rs` traces): `stress_rapid_fill_burst` and `stress_flash_fill_ram_backed` assert action happens no later than before and coverage stays in band.
- Stats: `stats --json .forecast.coverage_by_day`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Empirical coverage of `tte_lo` on the synthetic burst suite within ±5% of target over 10,000 observations; README describes the guarantee in one paragraph with the exact update rule.

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Logging addendum (OliveIbis): add '[SBH-FORECAST] mount=.. tte_point=.. tte_lo=.. alpha=.. coverage=.. samples=..' at -v per calibration window, and a stats --json .forecast.coverage_by_day aggregate, so the coverage guarantee is auditable in the field; decision records carry tte_lo and coverage at decision time.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Blocked by 2.9 and 2.17 (all three edit `pid.rs`/`guardrails.rs`). The `G1.7` reference means Q1 (the reserve-target bead).

title: Risk-budgeted batch planner: reach the byte target with least expected loss, explainably (W1)
description:
# G16 - Risk-budgeted batch planner: reach the target with the least expected loss, explainably

## Why (ambition round 3)
The executor takes the top-N candidates by composite score up to the level's batch size (`pid.rs::response_policy` batch sizes, `loop_main.rs` batch assembly). When a target is known (`clean --target-free N`, or the bytes needed to return to Orange/Green), "highest score first" is not "least risk for the bytes we need": a 40 GiB candidate at posterior 0.85 is often a better first choice than a 200 MiB one at 0.95. The Bayesian decision framework already prices each candidate's loss; the missing piece is choosing the *set*.

## Design
- `scanner/planner.rs` (new module): inputs are candidates with `{ expected_reclaim_bytes, posterior, action }` (Delete or Review), the byte target, and a risk budget `B` (sum of `expected_loss_i = (1 - posterior_i) * false_positive_loss` allowed in one batch). `B` scales with pressure: Green 1x FP loss (at most one "average" mistake), Yellow 2x, Orange 5x, Red 10x, Critical unbounded; configurable `scoring.batch_risk_budget_by_level`. Greedy by `expected_reclaim / expected_loss`, respecting the level's batch size and stopping when the target is met or the budget is exhausted; Review candidates are never planned except in emergency (existing rule). This is the classic fractional-knapsack greedy, within a constant factor of the 0/1 optimum for these shapes, and trivially explainable.
- Output: `BatchPlan { chosen: [...], target_bytes, planned_bytes, risk_budget, risk_used, skipped_for_budget: [...] }` attached to every decision record (G2) and to `scan_complete`/`clean` output (`plan` block). `explain` says "chosen 3rd: 12.4 GiB at posterior 0.85 (loss 7.5 of budget 50) because it reaches the target with 31% of the risk that the top-scored set would use".
- Determinism: stable tie-breaks (bytes desc, path asc) so identical inputs plan identically (design principle 3).
- Manual `clean --target-free` and the daemon share the planner; `scan --json` shows the plan it *would* execute (`--plan`).

## Files
`src/scanner/planner.rs` (new), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs`, `src/scanner/decision_record.rs`, `src/core/config.rs`, README "Bayesian Decision Framework" gains "Batch planning" (G8.3).

## Tests
- Unit: greedy vs brute-force 0/1 optimum on random small instances (proptest): greedy within factor 2 of optimum in reclaimed bytes for the same budget, never over budget.
- Unit: determinism under permutation of input order.
- Unit: level-scaled budgets; Review exclusion; target met early stops.
- Integration: `clean --target-free` on a fixture chooses the large mid-posterior candidate first and explains it; the daemon path produces `plan` in `scan_complete`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] For the same fixture and target, the planned batch has lower total expected loss than top-N-by-score in every level, and the explanation names the numbers.

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Logging addendum (OliveIbis): every planned batch logs one line '[SBH-PLANNER] level=.. target_bytes=.. planned_bytes=.. risk_budget=.. risk_used=.. chosen=n skipped_for_budget=m' and the plan block is attached to scan_complete/clean output and to every decision record so explain can quote it.

title: Configurable policy fallback actions + auto_recover_to; wire the dead FallbackReason variants; explicit auto-promotion; wizard initial_mode step (W1)
description:
# G9.1 - Configurable fallback actions and recovery target; wire `CanaryBudgetExhausted` and `SerializationFailure`; make auto-promotion explicit

## Context

title: Guardrail e-process: explain or fix the near-alarm (e=14.9) on a fresh daemon at steady Orange with perfect median error (W1)
description:
# G9.2 - Guardrail e-process: explain or fix the near-alarm observed on a fresh daemon at steady Orange with perfect median error

## Context
Journal on this host (2026-08-30 14:59:30, 5 minutes after start at Orange, no scans): `[SBH-SUMMARY] ... guard=PASS(e=14.9 med_err=0.00 cons=100% obs=215 clean=3)`. With `e_process_reward = 2/3` per good observation and the lower clamp at `exp(-5)`, 215 all-good observations should leave `e` near 0.0067, not 14.9 (alarm at 20.0). Either observations were bad on the TTE-conservatism axis while rate error stayed 0 (plausible at Orange with a flat rate: predicted TTE = infinity vs actual finite), or the severity-scaled penalty path (`guardrails.rs:240-258`) misfires on idle noise, or `median_rate_error` and the e-process disagree on what "good" means. An alarm would push the policy to FallbackSafe (no deletions) exactly when reclaim is needed.

## Work
1. Reproduce: unit test feeding 300 observations of `predicted_rate = 0`, `actual_rate = 0..tiny`, `predicted_tte = None/inf`, `actual_tte = finite` at Orange through `GuardrailMonitor`; print `e` trajectory; compare with the field log.
2. Decide the correct semantics with the design principle "fail conservative" in mind: idle (rate below the 10 B/s noise floor) observations must be *neutral* on TTE conservatism (no TTE can be predicted from a zero rate), not penalized; a bad TTE observation requires both a meaningful predicted rate and a materially earlier actual exhaustion.
3. Fix `GuardObservation::rate_danger_ratio`/`is_well_calibrated` accordingly; add `e_process` to `stats --json` guard history so the field can be checked later; add a `[SBH-GUARD]` line at `-v` per window with the classification reason.
4. Regression test: 1,000 steady accurate Orange observations keep `e < 1.0`; 15 truly bad observations still alarm within the documented bound.

## Files
`src/monitor/guardrails.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (verbose log), `src/logger/stats.rs`, README guardrails section (via G8.2 constants + prose).

## Success criteria
- [ ] The field pattern (idle at Orange) no longer accumulates e-process credit toward alarm; documented in CHANGELOG with the reproduction.

Root cause reproduced in a unit test: the guard's fixed 10 B/s noise floor made the daemon's own few-hundred-B/s state/log writes count as 100% underestimations (predicted EWMA ~0), so 300 idle observations drive the e-process above 5 (field: 14.9 with median error 0.00 because the median was idle). title: Q1 reserve target sizing: reaction-window write-burst quantile (t-digest + GPD tail), sbh tune recommendation, doctor coverage ratio
description:
# Q1 — reserve target from burst statistics (split from 2.5)

Depends on 2.5 (headroom plan, uniform-size pools, shared discovery) and 2.8 (state.json v2 `reserve_target_bytes`).

## Design
`W_m` = reaction window per mount (poll + scan + preflight + delete; EWMA of observed cycle latencies, prior 300 s). Aggregate `ProcessIoHistory` per-process write bytes into per-mount window sums `X_k` (attribute a process to the mount of its cwd/open files, fallback busiest mount); keep a t-digest (100 centroids, persisted next to io_history.bin). `reserve_m = q0.99(X)`; with < 50 windows fit a generalized Pareto tail over exceedances of q0.90 and extrapolate; floor at 2 x file_size. `sbh tune` recommends `file_count_m = ceil(reserve_m / file_size)`; `doctor --system` reports `releasable_bytes / reserve_m` and FAILs below 1.0; `status.reserve_state.horizon_minutes` says how long the reserve buys at the current burst rate.

## Tests
Property: quantile monotone in the input stream; GPD extrapolation never below the empirical q0.90; a synthetic bursty writer (1 GiB in 30 s every 10 min) yields a reserve >= 1 GiB. Unit: attribution fallback. Snapshot: `tune --json` recommendation shape.

(See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md; created from the 2026-09-02 review passes.)

title: Loud degradation surfaces: status reclaim_capability/reserve_state per mount, doctor FAILs, ReclaimUnavailable notification, check gate, TUI badge
description:
# Loud degradation surfaces (split from 2.8 / merged G1.4)

Depends on 2.8 (C-STATE per-mount block) and 2.12 (catalog roots).

## Design
- Per mount in status/state: `reclaim_capability: configured|catalog|none`, `reserve_state {present_bytes, target_bytes, horizon_minutes, floor_limited: bool}`.
- `doctor --system` FAILs when a mount at Yellow+ has `reclaim_capability=none` or an empty reserve, with the exact remediation (catalog roots flag, `sbh ballast provision`, add a root).
- Notification `ReclaimUnavailable {mount, level, reason}` once per pressure epoch (throttled like special-location alerts).
- `sbh check` on a target mount at Orange+ with `reclaim_capability=none` exits **1** (C-EXIT pressure condition) with reason slug `unprotected_pressure`; `--allow-unprotected` downgrades to 0 with a warning.
- TUI Overview badge `UNPROTECTED` next to the mount.

Unit: capability derivation on a mock PAL (configured / catalog / none); doctor JSON snapshot; notification throttle; `check` exit code table. E2E: `host-layout-observe` shows the badge/notification; `host-layout-catalog` shows `catalog`.

(See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md; created from the 2026-09-02 review passes.)

title: Behavior matrix as configurable [behavior] presets (v0.6 default, v0.5 rollback) with the never-reduce rule
description:
# Make the memory x disk behavior matrix a documented, configurable policy

## Background
src/daemon/policy.rs `DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS` (3x3, rows memory Normal/Warn/Critical, cols disk Normal/Warn/Critical; `from_disk_pressure` maps Green->Normal, Yellow|Orange->Warn, Red|Critical->Critical). Row memory-Normal: disk Normal -> cleanup None; disk Warn -> `IdentifyOnly`, ballast None; disk Critical -> `DefiniteCandidates`, ballast Release. So at normal memory the daemon never deletes or releases ballast before Red. README and AGENTS.md promise "Orange: begin ballast release + cleanup". The matrix is not configurable and not visible.

## Design
- `[behavior]` config: `preset = "v0.6" | "v0.5" | "custom"`, nine optional cell keys `<memory>_<disk> = { scan, cleanup, ballast, notify }` used when `custom`, and `memory_never_reduces_cleanup = true`.
- v0.6 cells at normal memory: Green -> maintenance pass (`HighConfidenceCandidates`, ballast None, see W1.4); Yellow -> `HighConfidenceCandidates`/None; Orange -> `DefiniteCandidates`/Release; Red -> `AnyDefiniteCandidate`/ReleaseFirst; Critical -> same + Review escalation. Memory Warn/Critical rows may lower scan aggressiveness but never lower cleanup/ballast below the disk row when the never-reduce rule is on.
- v0.5 preset reproduces today's cells exactly (rollback path); `SBH_BEHAVIOR_PRESET` env override.
- Effective matrix logged as a table at startup and on reload; `sbh config show --effective` prints it; `state.json` carries the active cell per mount.

## Acceptance
Unit tests: preset resolution, custom cell validation (invalid enum value rejected with the allowed list), never-reduce rule, env override precedence. Golden test: sandbox stale target at Orange with v0.6 -> dispatched; with v0.5 -> not dispatched.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- The block on 2.1 was removed so the single highest-impact fix (R1) does not wait for the refactor; the per-mount active cell in state.json is 2.8's field.
- Golden test restated on `behavior_allows_delete_dispatch(cell, synthetic Delete decision)`; the end-to-end golden (stale target dispatched at Orange) lives in 11.2 after 2.3.
- Certainty-to-action table: `HighConfidenceCandidates` dispatches Definite only; `DefiniteCandidates` dispatches Definite + Likely with posterior >= floor; `AnyDefiniteCandidate` adds Review escalation; `MostPromisingCandidates` is retained for the v0.5 preset only. Quarantine (2.13) applies at Green and manual `clean`; Yellow+ unlinks.
notes: Interplay with quarantine-first deletion (bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.13): in the v0.6 preset, the cleanup action at Green (maintenance) and Yellow executes in DeletionMode::Quarantine (rename into <mount>/.sbh/quarantine, undo-able, no immediate space return), and Orange+ executes Unlink after draining the quarantine oldest-first. Express the mode in the cell (cleanup_mode: quarantine|unlink) so operators see it in the logged matrix.

title: Definite-artifact certainty classifier with a calibrated posterior floor so definite artifacts reach Delete at Orange
description:
# ArtifactCertainty::{Definite, Likely, Unclear} and the fast lane

## Background
`sbh scan --explain` on a 64 MiB cargo target with a valid CACHEDIR.TAG, deps/, incremental/, .fingerprint/, no open files, 42 min old (birth time), in a temp root: total_score 0.6475, final_confidence 0.65, action `Review`. The decision layer (src/scanner/scoring.rs `decide_action`, posterior via `posterior_from_score`, losses FN 30 / FP 50, review band `1 + 5u + 2(1-cal)`, delete requires posterior >= clamp(0.60+0.20u+0.20(1-cal), 0.60, 0.95) and keep/delete loss ratio >= `min_delete_advantage` 1.2-4.0) cannot reach Delete for the very artifact class the tool exists to remove, so the daemon never dispatches it.

## Design
- New src/scanner/certainty.rs: `fn classify(candidate, signals, rule) -> ArtifactCertainty` from structural evidence only: validated CACHEDIR.TAG at root; Rust `.fingerprint/` + `incremental/`; Go build-cache layout; `node_modules/` under a temp root; Xcode DerivedData child; Electron cache dir; rch marker dir with idle tree -> Definite. Name pattern >= 0.85 with one structural marker -> Likely. Else Unclear.
- Decision layer: after every veto (min-age, active references, sacred overlap, lease, source-tree, `.git`), Definite candidates use prior `posterior_floor_definite` (config `[scoring] posterior_floor_definite = 0.85`) in `decide_action`; Likely uses the existing posterior; Unclear may only reach Review. The fast lane changes the prior, never the vetoes.
- Q4 (W2.4) later tightens/loosens the floor per category from observed regret; this bead ships the static floor.
- `sbh scan --explain` prints `certainty` and the evidence rows used.

## Acceptance
Golden decision tests pinned to fixtures (kept under tests/fixtures): stale Definite target -> Delete at Yellow (maintenance cell) and Orange+; fresh (< min age) -> Keep; `.git` sibling -> Keep; leased -> Keep; open file -> Keep; Unclear dir named `target-backup` -> Review at most. Property test: for any input, certainty never overrides a veto.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: for Definite candidates `posterior = max(posterior, posterior_floor_definite)` and `uncertainty` is re-evaluated after the floor (so the keep/delete loss-ratio gate with FN 30 / FP 50 passes at 0.85); the golden test pins the resulting numbers. 2.10 (tree idleness age) is the safety half and is P0; 11.2 depends on it.
close_reason: Delivered in 640d72a: ArtifactCertainty + classify_certainty (structural evidence, temp-root aware), scoring.posterior_floor_definite (0.85) with env/validate, floor applied after all vetoes, DecisionOutcome.certainty/posterior_floor_applied, ledger terms, scan --json certainty, executor certainty gate driven by the behavior cell (HighConfidence->Definite, Definite/MostPromising->Likely, AnyDefinite->all). Tests: 3 scoring goldens, loop_main gate test, config test. FINDING recorded during implementation: at Orange the pressure multiplier already lifted the sandbox fixture's posterior past 0.85 before this change, so 2.2 alone unblocks Orange dispatch; the floor is what makes the Green/Yellow maintenance and predictive paths reach Delete. A fixture whose directory birth time is old but whose files are fresh ALSO reaches Delete, so 2.10 (tree-idleness age) is being done next before any e2e run. Closed by the implementing agent after re-executing the gate; not independently verified.

title: Green maintenance cadence and wiring VoiScheduler::schedule() as a hazard-driven index policy (Q6)
description:
# Routine maintenance at Green, driven by a real scheduler

## Background
The Green arm (src/daemon/loop_main.rs:2852-2915) never dispatches a scan unless the predictive policy is not `Clear` or the policy is in FallbackSafe. `VoiScheduler::schedule()` is never called anywhere in the daemon (only `register_path`, `record_scan_result`, `end_window`); scans always cover all `scanner.root_paths`. The README's VOI section describes code that runs only in unit tests.

## Design
- `[pressure] maintenance_interval_secs = 1800`: at Green a `HighConfidenceCandidates` pass runs over roots chosen by the scheduler with budget `[scheduler].scan_budget_per_interval`; obeys the duty-cycle limiter and empty-pass backoff; suppressed while memory is Critical.
- Scheduler index (Q6): per root `I_i = R_i * (1 - exp(-lambda_i * dt_i)) - w_c * C_i` where `R_i` expected reclaim, `C_i` visit cost (both already tracked), `lambda_i` EWMA of dirty transitions per hour from v2 events (prior 1/24 h), `dt_i` time since last visit. Dirty roots always first; then top-k by index within budget. Replaces the exploit/explore split with an equivalent principled rule; keep the MAPE fallback to round-robin.
- Under Yellow+ the scheduler still orders roots but the budget is the pressure-level budget.

## Acceptance
Unit: index monotonicity (lambda=0 & not dirty visited at most once per day; high lambda & high R dominates; budget never exceeded). Integration: a Green daemon with a stale Definite fixture deletes it within one maintenance interval (e2e `green-maintenance` scenario in W10). title: Ballast provisioning by headroom (uniform-size per-file admission, partial pools, re-plan triggers, install callback) and shared pool discovery for CLI and daemon
description:
# Reserve target from burst statistics (Q1) and shared pool discovery for CLI and daemon

Depends on bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.1 (graduated per-file admission against a threshold-derived floor), which owns the provisioning-floor change. This bead adds what G1.1 does not:

## Q1 — reaction-window reserve sizing
`W_m` = reaction window per mount (poll + scan + preflight + delete, EWMA of observed cycle latencies, prior 300 s). Aggregate `ProcessIoHistory` per-process write bytes into per-mount window sums `X_k` (attribute a process to the mount of its cwd/open files, fallback busiest mount); keep a t-digest (100 centroids, persisted next to io_history.bin). `reserve_m = q0.99(X)`; with < 50 windows fit a generalized Pareto tail over exceedances of q0.90 and extrapolate; floor at 2 x file_size. `sbh tune` recommends `file_count_m = ceil(reserve_m / file_size)`; `doctor --system` reports `releasable_bytes / reserve_m` and FAILs below 1.0; `state.json` carries `reserve_target_bytes` per mount.

## Shared discovery
`BallastCoordinator::discover(config)` is the single enumeration used by the daemon and by `sbh ballast status`, `sbh status`, `sbh check`, `doctor --system` (see also bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.4); output lists every pool (including `<mount>/.sbh/ballast`) with mount, dir, configured, present, health, floor.

## Tests
Property tests: quantile monotone in the input stream; GPD extrapolation never below the empirical q0.90; a synthetic bursty writer (1 GiB in 30 s every 10 min) yields a reserve >= 1 GiB. Unit: discovery on a mock PAL with three mounts (one skipped). E2E (W10 `partial-provision`).

## Context
Reality check 2026-09-02: operator host `/` pool empty for months (20% floor at 12% free); daemon provisioned 10 GiB on /data/.sbh/ballast invisible to the CLI; 2026-08-18 emergency released "all ballast" 100 times in one minute on an empty pool.

---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.1 — G1.1: Graduated ballast reserve — per-file admission against a threshold-derived floor
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G1.1 - Graduated ballast reserve: provision per-file against a threshold-derived floor instead of a flat 20%

## Context
`ballast/manager.rs:36` `MIN_FREE_PCT = 20.0`; `provision()` (about :405-460) checks the callback once and refuses the whole pool. On a 977 GB `/` at 12% free (118 GB free) a 10 GiB reserve is affordable and would leave 11% free, still above Orange (10%), yet nothing is provisioned. The README (L1136) promises "provisioning aborts if free space drops below 20%", which is the mechanism that leaves the pressured disk with no reserve. `install.rs:230` calls `provision(None)` and bypasses even that guard. Coordinator (`ballast/coordinator.rs:334`) and CLI (`cli_app.rs:4411`) pass the callback.

## Goal
A reserve is built incrementally whenever doing so keeps the volume above a reserve floor, so a low-but-not-critical volume gets a partial reserve instead of none, and release at Red is always net-positive.

## Design
- New `ReserveFloor` in `ballast/manager.rs`: `floor_pct = max(pressure.orange_min_free_pct, pressure.red_min_free_pct + 2.0)` unless `ballast.provision_floor_pct` is set explicitly. Admission per file: create file `i` only if `(free_bytes - file_size) / total_bytes * 100 >= floor_pct`. Stop (not fail) at the first refusal; report `ProvisionOutcome { created, skipped_for_floor, reason }`.
- Low-space band: when current free is between `floor_pct` and `green_min_free_pct`, use `ballast.low_space_file_size_bytes` (default 256 MiB, header-validated >= 4096) so partial reserves are fine-grained; the header records the per-file size so verify/inventory stay correct with mixed sizes.
- Never provision when the volume's level is Red or Critical (the daemon is releasing, not reserving); the callback carries the level.
- `install.rs:230` must pass the floor callback (build a `FsStatsCollector` there).
- Replenish path (`ballast/release.rs:155-235`) uses the same admission so replenishment after recovery also respects the floor.
- Config: `ballast.provision_floor_pct: Option<f64>`, `ballast.low_space_file_size_bytes: u64`; validation: floor within (red_min, 100), low-space size >= 4096 and <= file_size_bytes.
- Logging: `[SBH-BALLAST] provision volume=/ created=3 skipped_for_floor=2 floor_pct=10.0 free_after_pct=10.4 mode=low_space` and an `ActivityEvent::BallastProvisioned { created, skipped, reason }` so `stats` and the timeline show it.

## Files
`src/ballast/manager.rs`, `src/ballast/coordinator.rs`, `src/ballast/release.rs`, `src/cli/install.rs`, `src/core/config.rs` (fields + validation + docs comment), `src/cli_app.rs` (`ballast provision` output fields), README ballast section (via G8 regeneration), CHANGELOG.

## Tests (must ship with the change)
- Unit (`manager.rs`): mock volume 977 GB at 12% free, pool 5 x 2 GiB, floor 10% -> after 5 files free = 108 GB = 11.05% >= 10% so all 5 created; at 10.5% free -> creates until floor, `skipped_for_floor > 0`; at Red -> creates none, reason=`red`. Mixed-size inventory verifies and reports correctly.
- Unit (`release.rs`): release at Red after graduated provisioning never drives free below the pre-provision free bytes (proptest over random free/total/pool sizes).
- Unit (`config.rs`): validation errors for floor <= red_min, low-space size < 4096.
- Integration (`tests/integration_tests.rs`): `sbh ballast provision --json` on a tmpfs-sized fixture (small `file_size_bytes`) reports `skipped_for_floor` and `floor_pct`; second run is idempotent.
- e2e (`scripts/e2e_test.sh`): new case under the Ballast section asserting the JSON fields.

## Success criteria
- [ ] All tests above green via `rch exec "cargo test --lib ballast"` and the integration suite.
- [ ] `sudo sbh ballast provision` on this host creates a reserve on `/` (post-G0).
- [ ] `doctor --system` `ballast.reserve` distinguishes "floor prevents full reserve" (WARN with numbers) from "no reserve" (FAIL).

## Considerations
- Interaction with the 10 GiB emergency reserve of active leases (`scanner/active_lease.rs:43-51`): floors are independent; document it.
- APFS: purgeable space is excluded already (`free_excludes_purgeable`); use the same `Capacity` numbers.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.1
From the 2026-09-02 reality-check tree (bd-rc-master-ajg1): (1) re-plan triggers — recompute the admissible file count after every successful reclaim, every replenish tick, every maintenance interval, and `sbh ballast provision`, so a pool grows as space frees; (2) health `unconfigured-for-space` when zero files fit, distinct from `empty`; (3) reserve *target* sizing from data (Q1 in docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md): `reserve_m = q0.99(bytes written on the mount during the reaction window)` via a t-digest over ProcessIoHistory window sums with a GPD tail fit below 50 windows and a floor of 2 x file_size; `sbh tune` recommends file_count from it and `doctor --system` reports releasable/reserve coverage — tracked in bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.5 which depends on this bead; (4) shared `BallastCoordinator::discover(config)` for CLI and daemon (see G10.4).

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- OliveIbis note (from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.1 and .1.7): in addition to the headroom plan, size the reserve target as the fill over the action horizon at an upper quantile and report status.reserve_state.horizon_minutes (how long the reserve buys at the current burst rate); use a smaller low-space file size between the floor and Green so partial reserves are fine-grained; install.rs:230 provision(None) currently bypasses the free-space guard entirely.
- Verification addendum (OliveIbis): (a) unit: plan arithmetic at 12% free on a 977 GB volume with 5x2 GiB pool and orange 10% -> all 5 admitted (11.05% after); at 10.5% -> partial with skipped_for_floor > 0; at Red -> zero with reason=red; zero and negative headroom; mixed-size inventories verify; (b) property (proptest): release at Red after headroom-planned provisioning never drives free below the pre-provision bytes; (c) unit: install.rs:230 provision(None) path now receives the floor callback (regression test that install refuses at Red); (d) integration: 'sbh ballast provision --json' on a tmpfs fixture reports created/skipped_for_floor/floor_pct and is idempotent on a second run; (e) logging: one '[SBH-BALLAST] provision volume=.. created=.. skipped_for_floor=.. floor_pct=.. free_after_pct=..' line per volume per plan and an ActivityEvent::BallastProvisioned so stats/timeline show it; (f) doctor: ballast.reserve distinguishes 'floor prevents full reserve' (WARN with numbers) from 'no reserve' (FAIL).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- The stale self-dependency on the closed bridge bead was removed; this bead OWNS the former G1.1 (floor + per-file admission), the install callback (`install.rs:230` must pass the floor callback) and shared discovery. Q1 is split into its own P1 bead.
- DECISION: uniform-size plan-by-headroom (the release controller, `expected_count`, and C-STATE assume one file size); the merged mixed-size `low_space_file_size_bytes` band is dropped; re-plan triggers and `ProvisionOutcome {created, skipped_for_floor, reason}` are kept.
close_reason: Implemented in c6fbca1 (ballast headroom admission) by the implementing agent; not independently verified. Evidence: 8 new unit tests pass (manager admission x5, coordinator provision_all low volume, config floor); real-volume proof on this host: / at 89% used (11.5% free) -> 'sbh ballast provision' created 2/2 files, floor_pct=10, free_pct_after=11.47, skipped_for_floor=0 (legacy 20% floor refused this volume); files released afterwards. Not done from the bead text: re-plan triggers beyond reload/daemon start and an install-time callback (daemon provisions on start; CLI provision is idempotent), non-uniform file sizes.

title: Special-location horizon rule (Q2): time-to-harm thresholds, absolute floors, throttled warning-severity alerts
description:
# Stop alerting on percent alone

## Background
src/daemon/loop_main.rs:3271 emits an `error/critical` activity event every scan interval while a special location is below its percent buffer, with no rate limit. On the operator workstation this produced 35,692 events in three days for /data/tmp (UserTmp, 15%% buffer) on a 5.5 TiB btrfs volume at 13.9%% free — 760 GiB free. The daemon also sent a ScanRequest with urgency = priority/255 each time.

## Design
- Per location: `h_L = free_bytes / max(rate_L, r_min)` where `rate_L` is an EWMA of the location's write rate (fallback: the mount's rate). Alert when `h_L < 30 min` (RAM-backed: also when free < 20%%); for disk-backed temp roots the percent rule is replaced by `min(percent, absolute_floor)` with `absolute_floor = 32 GiB` default (`[special_locations] absolute_floor_bytes`).
- Severity `warning` for disk-backed, `critical` for RAM-backed; one activity event per location per 15 min (state change logs immediately); the `error` event type is reserved for failures (C-EVENT schema, W6.1).
- ScanRequest urgency from the horizon (`clamp(1 - h_L / 30min, 0, 1)`), not from the priority constant.

## Acceptance
Unit: horizon monotonicity; alert predicate invariant to volume size when expressed in horizon; throttle. E2E: injected 13.9%% free on 5.5 TiB -> zero alerts in 10 min; 10 GiB free with a 1 GiB/min synthetic writer -> one warning per 15 min and a scan request.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. ## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Config: new `[special_locations]` section (`absolute_floor_bytes`, `alert_horizon_minutes`, `alert_interval_minutes`) so 4.8's known-key derivation and the README fixture include it.

title: Failure classification (EROFS/ENOSPC), RecoveryMode, and an anytime-valid deletion-failure monitor (Q8)
description:
# A read-only or metadata-exhausted volume is an incident, not a retry loop

## Background
Daemon logs June-August: 10,362 `skipped: NotWritable` (as root), 3,609 `Symlink`, 999 `IdentityMismatch`, 570 `FileOpen`, plus "Directory not empty" IO failures; August: 0 successes out of 844. `is_writable` (src/scanner/deletion.rs:815-821) collapses EROFS, ENOSPC and permission into one `SkipReason::NotWritable`; the daemon attributes it to the ReadWritePaths sandbox (loop_main.rs:5756) even on hosts without one. /data is btrfs and reached 7.7%% free on 2026-08-11 — the profile of btrfs metadata exhaustion / read-only remount.

## Design
- `SkipReason::{ParentNotWritable(i32 errno), FilesystemReadOnly, NoSpaceForMetadata}` replace `NotWritable`; classification from the `access`/`statvfs` errno and `ST_RDONLY`.
- Executor returns `BatchOutcome::RecoveryNeeded(mount)` on the latter two after the first occurrence; the mount controller enters `Recovery`: release all ballast on that mount, emit a Critical notification with the exact commands (`sudo sbh emergency <root> --yes`, `btrfs filesystem usage`, balance hint), pause deletion retries; exit when a 4 KiB probe write succeeds and free >= red_min.
- Q8 monitor: an e-process over the executor's success/failure stream with H0 "failure rate <= 10%%", factors 1.5 (failure) / 2/3 (success), clamp [-5, 3.5], alarm at 20 (shared constants with the forecaster guard); alarm -> Recovery + Critical notification naming the dominant SkipReason.
- `stats` reports failures by reason (C-EVENT `skip_reason`, `errno`).

## Acceptance
Unit: errno mapping; e-process (20 consecutive failures alarm; 9 per 100 do not). E2E (W10 `read-only`): root on a `-o ro` bind mount -> batch stops, ballast released, Critical notification, zero retries for 5 min, exit from Recovery after remount rw.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Tests: MockPlatform integration test injecting EROFS/ENOSPC from `is_writable`/`statvfs` asserts `RecoveryNeeded` and the Recovery entry without root; the bind-mount case stays in 11.3 (P1). This bead adds `skip_reason`/`errno` to the deletion-failure activity event; 7.1 consumes them.
close_reason: Implemented in d1a7bb3 by the implementing agent; not independently verified. SkipReason::FilesystemReadOnly (EROFS via access(2) or ST_RDONLY via statvfs) split from NotWritable; deletion errors with EROFS/ENOSPC classified (error_recovery_cause); DeletionReport.read_only_paths/no_space_paths -> WorkerReport recovery_paths -> mount controller Recovery (releases all ballast on the mount, SBH-2004 log+notification with 'sudo sbh emergency <root> --yes' and btrfs usage/balance commands, deletions held until a 4 KiB probe write succeeds above red_min). DeletionFailureMonitor e-process (x1.5/x2/3, clamp [-5,3.5], alarm 20) in the executor thread; alarm -> SBH-2005 notification naming the dominant reason. Tests pass: errno classification, recovery-cause mapping, monitor (20-streak alarms, 9/100 does not). Deviations: SkipReason stays a unit enum (no errno payload; errno is not surfaced in events); notification level is Red (NotificationEvent::Error), not Critical; the e-process alarm notifies but does not force Recovery (no mount attached); stats has no failures-by-reason breakdown yet; no e2e on a real read-only bind mount (needs root or user namespaces; unshare -Urm is not permitted on this host).

title: Truthful emergency events and state.json v2 with per-mount rates, forecast, controller state and idle reason (C-STATE)
description:
# state.json v2 and honest events

## Background
`emergency` events carried `free_pct: 99.99999` while `/` was Critical (100 events in one minute on 2026-08-18 for an already-empty pool). `state.json` has one mount, `rate_bps` hard-coded `None` (src/daemon/self_monitor.rs:381, loop_main.rs:2754), no `rates`, no thread health, no idle reason; `check --predict` and the status rate block read `state.rates.*` which is never written.

## Design
Implement contract C-STATE (schema_version 2): `run_id`, per-mount `{path, fs_type, total, free, free_pct, level, urgency, controller, idle_reason, rates {bytes_per_sec, accel, confidence, seconds_to_red, seconds_to_full}, ballast {...}, last_scan {...}, behavior_cell}`, `memory`, `policy {mode, since, fallback_reason, guard}`, `threads {monitor, scanner, executor, logger}`, `counters` (incl. `deletion_failures`), `memory_rss_bytes`, `cpu_secs_total`, `stopped_at`/`exit_reason` on shutdown. Keep `#[serde(default)]`; readers accept v1. `emergency` events carry mount, real free_pct, files_released and are emitted once per state change (a repeat on an empty pool is a debug line).

## Acceptance
Schema round-trip test; v1 file parses with defaults; e2e asserts fields after Orange reclaim and after shutdown; `emergency` event count == state changes in the `red-ballast` scenario.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)
