## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.4 — G1.4: Loud degradation — reclaim_capability/reserve_state in status, doctor FAILs, ReclaimUnavailable notification
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G1.4 - Loud, actionable degradation: "pressured mount has no scannable root" and "no reserve on pressured mount" become doctor FAILs, status fields, and notifications

## Context
Today the only trace of "sbh cannot help this mount" is a stderr line once per `DEVICE_AFFINITY_WARN_INTERVAL` (`loop_main.rs:2827`) and an `ActivityEvent::Info`. `doctor --system` already has `ballast.reserve` (FAIL on this host) but nothing about reclaim capability. The README operator-perspective table promises the daemon reacts in seconds; silence is the worst failure class (bd-r7m7: "operator surprise is failure").

## Goal
Every mount in `status`/`check` carries a `reclaim_capability` and `reserve_state`; `doctor --system` FAILs when a mount at Yellow+ has neither; the daemon notifies at Orange+ when it is backing off.

## Design
- `status --json` `pressure.mounts[]` gains `reclaim_capability: "configured" | "catalog" | "none"` (computed from configured roots on that device, then catalog derivation from G1.2), `reserve_state: { configured_bytes, present_bytes, releasable_bytes, floor_pct }`, and `protection_summary: "protected" | "reserve_only" | "reclaim_only" | "unprotected"`. Human status prints an `UNPROTECTED` badge in red for any non-Green mount with `none`.
- `doctor --system` checks: `reclaim.pressured_mount_no_root` (FAIL when level >= Yellow and capability none; WARN when Green), `ballast.reserve_floor_limited` (WARN with numbers), `service.gated` (FAIL when a Condition gate disables the unit; from G1.3).
- Daemon notification: `NotificationEvent::ReclaimUnavailable { mount, level, reason }` at Orange+ with `min_notify_interval` throttling; journal + file channels by default.
- `check` (pre-build check) exits 2 with the same message when the target mount is unprotected and at Orange+ (opt-out `--allow-unprotected`).

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs` (status/check/doctor), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (event), `src/daemon/notifications.rs` (variant, template placeholders), `src/tui/adapters.rs` (badge), README status/doctor sections.

## Tests
- Unit: capability derivation for configured/catalog/none with mock PAL; doctor check matrix by level.
- Integration: `sbh status --json` on a fixture config with roots off-device -> `reclaim_capability=none`, `protection_summary=unprotected`; `doctor --system --json` FAIL entry with remediation text; `check` exit code.
- Unit (`notifications.rs`): event dispatch + throttle.
- e2e cases for status and doctor.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host (pre-G1.2) `sbh doctor --system` FAILs `reclaim.pressured_mount_no_root` for `/`; after G1.2 it PASSes with capability `catalog`.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.4
Related from bd-rc-master-ajg1: bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.8 defines state.json v2 (per-mount controller state, idle_reason, rates/forecast, threads, counters, cpu_secs_total, stopped_at/exit_reason); `reclaim_capability`/`reserve_state` should live in the same per-mount block.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Priority P0: single C-STATE schema owner. Adds `voi {…}` (4.11), keeps the map-shaped `threads {monitor, scanner, executor, logger}` and `stopped_at`/`exit_reason` (6.3 conforms), per-mount `behavior_cell`, `reserve_target_bytes` (Q1), `release_efficiency` (9.2). The `check` gate from the merged G1.4 text exits **1**, not 2 (C-EXIT). The G1.4 status/doctor/notification/TUI surfaces are split into the new "Loud degradation surfaces" bead.
close_reason: Implemented in c25629b by the implementing agent; not independently verified. DaemonState v2: schema_version, run_id, rates map per mount (bytes_per_sec/accel/confidence/seconds_to_red/seconds_to_full; check --predict and the status rate block now have data), threads (monitor/scanner/executor/logger status + seconds since heartbeat), cpu_secs_total, stopped_at/exit_reason via a final write on shutdown; pressure.mounts lists every mount with a real rate_bps; emergency events per mount, once on entering Critical, with that mount's free_pct and files released. Idle workers now beat on recv timeout so 'stalled' is truthful. Tests: v1 parses with defaults, v2 round-trips. Sandbox after SIGTERM: schema_version=2, run_id, rates for / and /data, all threads running, exit_reason='clean shutdown'. Deviations: no counters.deletion_failures (counters.errors counts them), no policy{since,fallback_reason,guard}/behavior_cell sections, flat layout (mount_controllers + rates keyed by mount) rather than nested per-mount objects, no e2e of emergency-event counts in a Critical (red-ballast) scenario.

title: Per-mount PID with forecast feedforward, capacity gain scheduling and anti-windup on actionability (Q3)
description:
# Control that cannot wind up while it has no actuator

## Background
The single PID (Kp 0.25, Ki 0.08, Kd 0.02, integral cap 100, setpoint = green_min_free_pct) integrates error while the daemon cannot act (observe-only mount, empty pool), which is why the kill-switch note describes "sits in Red urgency". Errors are in percent, so a 1%% error is 55 GiB on /data and 1 GiB on a small root. The predictive boost jumps urgency to 0.70 at 15 min to red instead of rising smoothly.

## Design
Per-mount controller: `raw = Kp_m e + Ki integral + Kd d/dt + Kf * clamp(1 - t_red / H_action, 0, 1)` with `Kf = 0.8`; `Kp_m = Kp * sqrt(total_m / 1 TiB)` clamped to [0.5, 2] Kp; integral frozen while the mount is ObserveOnly, Idle, or Recovery; urgency = 1 - exp(-max(0, raw)) as today. Config keys under `[pressure.controller]` with the README formulas regenerated from code.

## Acceptance
Property tests: integral does not grow with the actuator frozen; urgency monotone in -t_red; step response on the recorded sandbox trace converges without overshooting more than one level; existing PID tests updated.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Fixture: commit the sandbox daemon trace as `tests/fixtures/sandbox-trace-2026-09-02.jsonl` (source: the three sandbox runs recorded in the plan doc section 3.2); 2.14 uses the same trace.
close_reason:
Closed by the implementing agent, not independently verified.

Delivered (landed in another agent's sweep commits 165cfbe, e17c823, 03d320a, labelled bd-rc-master-ajg1.6 by mistake; this is the bead they belong to): src/monitor/pid.rs redesigned around PidConfig (gains, setpoint, thresholds, reference volume, Kp scale bounds; `From<&PressureConfig>`), capacity gain scheduling `Kp_m = Kp * clamp(sqrt(total / 1 TiB), 0.5, 2)`, forecast feedforward `Kf * clamp(1 - t_red / H_action, 0, 1)` (Kf 0.8) replacing the stepped 0.70/0.90/1.0 boosts, `freeze_integral` anti-windup driven each tick from the mount controller's state (ObserveOnly, Idle, Recovery freeze; level changes still reset), `apply_config` for SIGHUP, `FORMULAS` constant mirrored in the README with a test that keeps them identical. Config `[pressure.controller]` (kp, ki, kd, kf, integral_cap, hysteresis_pct, reference_total_bytes, kp_scale_min, kp_scale_max) validated finite/non-negative with min <= max; README and AGENTS updated. Fixture tests/fixtures/sandbox-trace-2026-09-02.jsonl (626 points at 1 s).

Evidence: pid.rs unit tests (feedforward smooth and monotone, capacity gain bounds, frozen integral does not grow and thaws in place, apply_config, README formulas match, step response on the trace: level within one step of the raw classification, no urgency jump above 0.5 without a 3-point move, settles Green with no positive integral) plus three proptest properties (integral stays put while frozen for any error sequence; urgency monotone non-increasing in seconds-to-red; scheduled Kp within bounds for any volume). Verified on HEAD d69513a (which also carries the test refinements swept into 0dd10bd/c4b6a51): `cargo test --lib -- pid::` 20 passed, `--test regression_issue_pid_slow_attack --test repro_pid_skew` 1+1 passed, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Deviations: (1) the "recorded sandbox trace" does not exist as numbers anywhere (the plan doc recorded the three runs' levels and outcomes, the host daemon log only holds 7 pressure_change events), so the fixture replays the runs' conditions at 1 s ticks followed by a synthesized fill/release/reclaim profile, and says so in its first line; 2.14 inherits that. (2) The old hard boost to 1.0 at <= 60 s to red is gone by design; urgency near red now comes from Kp_m * error + Kf, and the mount controller's own seconds_to_red input still forces Reclaim. (3) Overshoot is asserted as "level never above the raw classification + 1 and urgency moves smoothly", not as a formal control-theoretic bound. (4) No `sbh tune` recommendation for the new keys.

title: W2: Explainability that exists (persisted decision ledger, sbh explain, regret-calibrated thresholds)
description:
# W2 — Explainability that exists

## Background
README (six places), AGENTS.md and scripts/install.sh's post-install hints tell users to run `sbh explain --id <decision-id>`. There is no `Explain` variant in the clap `Command` enum; `PolicyEngine::evaluate` builds `DecisionRecord`s but the executor keeps only the approved list and drops the records (src/daemon/loop_main.rs:5585-5589); no `ActivityEvent` carries a decision; `src/logger` has zero references to decisions; `decision_id` is a per-process counter. Bead bd-izu.2 "Evidence ledger schema + explain command" was closed on 2026-02-15 without this existing.

## Children
W2.1 persist decisions with stable ids · W2.2 `sbh explain` · W2.3 dashboard explainability from the ledger · W2.4 regret labels and conformal risk control (Q4).

## Acceptance
E2E: a deletion in the sandbox produces a JSONL `decision` event and an `artifact_delete` with `decision_id`; `sbh explain --id` returns the record at all four levels in human and JSON modes; `sbh explain --last 1` works after a CLI `clean --dry-run` with no daemon.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Consolidation note (2026-09-02)
A parallel reality check produced the bead tree `bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx` (G0-G12) with overlapping scope. Duplicated children of this epic were closed in favor of the G-tree and their unique details appended there as notes; the remaining children here are the parts the G-tree does not cover. Cross-tree blocking and related edges record the interplay. See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md section 5b.

## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.3 — G2: Explainability — persist decision records and ship sbh explain
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G2 - Explainability: persist decision records and ship `sbh explain`

## Background
Design principle 4 in README and AGENTS.md: "Explainability is mandatory: every action has traceable evidence and rationale." The README headline table promises "Evidence ledger + `sbh explain` shows why each action happened", the architecture diagram has an "Evidence Ledger + Explain API" box, the Quick Example runs `sbh explain --id <decision-id>`, and the FAQ says to use it to audit deletions. Reality (2026-09-01 audit): `sbh explain` is an unrecognized subcommand. `scanner/decision_record.rs` defines `DecisionRecord` with four explain levels (24 tests); `daemon/policy.rs:478-679` builds one per decision; `daemon/loop_main.rs:5585-5589` reads only `approved_for_deletion` and `mode` and drops the record. No `ActivityEvent` carries it (`logger/dual.rs:48-116`), no SQLite table stores it, nothing persists it. `scan --explain` prints factors inline without an ID. The evidence ledger is a type, not a store.

## Goal
Every policy decision (daemon, and manual `clean`) is persisted with a stable ID and can be retrieved and explained at four levels; emergency mode prints but never writes (zero-write invariant).

## Design (children carry the detail)
- G2.1: decision IDs (12-hex prefix of SHA-256 over path, device, inode, decision-time bucket, mode), `ActivityEvent::DecisionRecorded`, SQLite `decisions` table, JSONL echo, retention prune, stats aggregates.
- G2.2: `sbh explain --id/--path/--last [--level 1..4] [--json]`; IDs surfaced in `scan --explain`, `clean`, notifications, `scan_complete`/`deletion` events.
- G2.3: tests (unit, integration, e2e) including the emergency zero-write assertion and JSON schema documentation.

## Why the ID scheme
Content-addressed IDs are reproducible across daemon and CLI runs for the same candidate epoch, short enough to paste, and change when a directory is recreated (inode) so "why was this deleted twice" is answerable.

## Acceptance
`sbh explain --id` on a real daemon decision returns the record; dashboard Explainability screen (G5) reads the same table.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Priority P0 (3.1 backs master invariant 1 and blocks 11.2, 2.13, 2.15).



## Consolidation correction (2026-09-02)
The earlier consolidation note is superseded: the parallel G-tree was merged INTO this tree; every child here is canonical and carries the merged text.

title: Stable decision ids, decision_log table, JSONL decision events, artifact_delete references
description:
# Persist every decision

## Design
- `DecisionId = "<run_id>-<seq:08>"`; `run_id` random base32 minted at daemon start (written to state.json); CLI runs mint `cli-<token>`.
- `ActivityEvent::Decision(DecisionRecord)`; SQLite table `decision_log(id, ts, run_id, path, action, certainty, posterior, keep_loss, delete_loss, guard_status, veto_reasons JSON, factors JSON, comparator_action, mode)` indexed by (run_id, seq) and path; JSONL `event: "decision"` (toggle `[telemetry] log_decisions_jsonl`, default true); retention shared with activity_log.
- Every `artifact_delete` event and every `sbh scan --explain` / `sbh clean` line carries the id.

## Acceptance
Unit: id minting uniqueness; record round-trip. Integration: insert/query/retention. E2E in W10 `orange-reclaim` asserts the id chain.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.3.1 — G2.1: Decision IDs, DecisionRecorded event, SQLite decisions table, JSONL echo, retention, stats aggregates
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G2.1 - Decision IDs, `DecisionRecorded` activity event, SQLite `decisions` table, JSONL echo, retention, stats aggregates

## Context
`scanner/decision_record.rs` has `DecisionRecord { path, factors, posterior, keep_loss, delete_loss, uncertainty, guard_status, vetoes, mode, action, explain levels }` and `format_explain(level)`. `daemon/policy.rs:478-679` builds it inside `decide()`. `loop_main.rs:5585-5589` discards it. `logger/dual.rs` `ActivityEvent` has no decision variant; `logger/sqlite.rs:375-414` creates three tables (`activity_log`, `pressure_history`, `ballast_inventory`); `dual.rs:231-233` prunes rows older than 30 days every 3,600 events.

## Design
- `DecisionRecord::id(&self) -> DecisionId`: `sha256(path_bytes || dev || ino || (decided_at.unix_secs / 60) || mode as u8)[..6]` hex (12 chars). Add `device_id`, `inode`, `decided_at`, `outcome: Option<DecisionOutcome { executed, freed_bytes, error, at }>` fields (serde default).
- `ActivityEvent::DecisionRecorded(Box<DecisionRecord>)` and `ActivityEvent::DecisionOutcome { id, outcome }`; `DualLogger` writes both to SQLite and JSONL (JSONL line `{"event":"decision_recorded", ...}`); the logger channel stays bounded (records are small; factors JSON < 4 KiB).
- SQLite: `decisions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ts INTEGER, path TEXT, dev INTEGER, ino INTEGER, mode TEXT, action TEXT, posterior REAL, keep_loss REAL, delete_loss REAL, uncertainty REAL, guard_status TEXT, vetoes TEXT /*json*/, factors TEXT /*json*/, explain_l1 TEXT, explain_l2 TEXT, explain_l3 TEXT, explain_l4 TEXT, outcome TEXT /*json*/)` with indexes on `ts` and `path`; schema migration is additive (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), version bump in the existing schema table if present. Prune with the same 30-day retention.

title: sbh explain --id/--last/--path/--since with four explain levels and JSON
description:
# The command the README has promised since February

## Design
`sbh explain (--id ID | --last N | --path P | --since DUR) [--level 0..3] [--json]` renders through `decision_record::format_explain` (the four galaxy-brain levels already exist); reads `decision_log` via the read-only SQLite open (W3.2) with JSONL fallback; exit 1 when no record matches with a hint listing the last three ids.

## Acceptance
CLI e2e: after a sandbox deletion, `explain --id` at levels 0-3 human and JSON; `--last 1` after `clean --dry-run` without daemon; unknown id -> exit 1 with hint. README command reference updated (W11).

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

# G2.2 - `sbh explain` command and decision IDs everywhere a decision is shown

## Context
README L60/L406/L1766/L1848 and AGENTS.md L379 document `sbh explain --id <decision-id>`; the binary has no such command (`cli_app.rs:110-162` command enum). `scan --explain` prints scoring factors but no ID; `clean` output has no ID; notifications carry none.

## Design

Exactly one of `--id/--path/--last` required (clap group). Output: human (the existing `format_explain(level)` text plus outcome line) or JSON (the full record). - Shell completion: `explain` added; `sbh --help` lists it (doc-parity test in G8 will enforce README/AGENTS tables).

`src/cli_app.rs` (enum, args, handler, scan/clean output), `src/logger/stats.rs` (queries), `src/scanner/decision_record.rs` (`format_explain` outcome line), README/AGENTS command tables, CHANGELOG.

title: Regret labels (decision_outcome) and conformal risk control of per-category delete thresholds (Q4)
description:
# Calibrate the fast lane from what actually happened

## Design
- Regret event: identity `(parent_dev, parent_ino, name)` recreated within 30 min of deletion while a process with cwd or open files under the parent is alive; recorded as `decision_outcome(decision_id, outcome regret|clean|unknown, observed_at)` by a lightweight watcher (v2 events or the maintenance pass).
- Per category Beta posteriors with an empirical-Bayes prior across categories; threshold `theta_c` chosen as the largest posterior threshold whose Clopper-Pearson upper bound (delta 0.05) on the regret rate is <= alpha_c (Definite 0.02, Likely 0.005); `calibration = 1 - UB(regret)` feeds the existing decision layer; the W1.3 floor is the initial threshold.
- Category-level e-process (H0 regret <= alpha) whose alarm demotes only that category to Canary.

## Acceptance
Property tests: zero regrets never raise the threshold above the initial floor; 10%% regret in one category tightens only that category; bound monotone in count. E2E: scripted regret (recreate the deleted target while a writer is alive) produces an outcome row and a threshold change visible in `sbh explain`.

title: sbh explain --why-not <path>, --counterfactual, and --replay <id> (W2)
description:
# G2.4 - `sbh explain --why-not <path>`, `--counterfactual`, and `--replay <id>`

## Why (ambition round 1)
The most common operator question in the README's own troubleshooting section is "No candidates found, but disk is full"; today the answer is "run scan with --min-score 0.0 and read". A first-class answer: score the path now, run pre-flight, and say which veto or which factor gap kept it.

## Design
- `explain --why-not <path>`: builds a `CandidateInput` for the path (walker metadata for one entry, structural markers, open-file check, lease probe, protection/sacred check), runs scoring + pre-flight, and prints, in order: protection/sacred hit; hardcoded source-tree refusal; lease; open files; each scoring factor with its contribution and the threshold gap; the decision-theoretic outcome; and the planner's view (G16) if a target is given (`--target-free`). JSON has the same structure.
- `--counterfactual`: the smallest single-factor change that flips Keep -> Delete (for example "age 1.9 h -> needs 2.0 h" or "posterior 0.58 -> needs 0.62"), computed by re-scoring with each factor moved to its next threshold; vetoes are reported as "not flippable by scoring".
- `--replay <decision-id>`: re-score the stored record's inputs with the current code and report factor/posterior/action drift (reuses the decision-plane replay harness in `decision_plane_tests.rs`/`tests/proof_harness.rs`); useful after tuning weights or upgrading.
- `sbh scan --explain` links: each candidate line ends with `explain: sbh explain --id <id>`; the troubleshooting section is rewritten around `--why-not`.

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs`, `src/scanner/{scoring,deletion,decision_record}.rs` (single-entry scoring API), README troubleshooting/FAQ.

## Tests
- Unit: `--why-not` on fixtures for each veto class and for a factor gap; counterfactual correctness (applying the suggested change flips the action).
- Unit: replay drift detection on a modified weight.
- e2e: troubleshooting scenario "disk full, no candidates" answered by one command.

## Success criteria
- [ ] The README troubleshooting entry becomes a single `explain --why-not` invocation that is tested.
close_reason: explain --why-not <dir> (scanner's own view of the entry via a one-level parent walk, live open-file/lease/sacred evidence, the executor's real preflight via DeletionExecutor::explain_preflight, first-rail verdict + ledger-style factor table, JSON), --counterfactual (bisected age/size/urgency flips with numeric thresholds; unit test applies each suggestion and gets Delete; vetoes reported as not flippable), --replay <id> (input rebuilt from the record incl. new stored name/structural confidences and the exact pressure-multiplier inverse; per-factor drift, approximations named). Scan rows carry ids; README troubleshooting rewritten; e2e 7b cases; explain_ledger tests for each rail class and replay drift. Landed in 0dddd10 + b313181/0fc1e48 (swept into the parallel agent's commits). Not done: --target-free planner view (planner bead not landed). Self-verified on rch: lib 1521, bin 130, explain_ledger 4/4, clippy clean with loop_main too_many_lines allowed.

title: W3: Truthful CLI on real installs (daemon probe, read-only opens, exit codes, uninstall, bootstrap, TUI by default, strict config)
description:
# W3 — Truthful CLI on real installs

## Background (all observed on the operator workstation with v0.5.1)
- `sbh --json status` -> `daemon_running: true` with the service dead (fallback scans /proc/*/cmdline for "sbh" and "daemon", src/cli_app.rs:7031-7070); human mode says "not running".
- `sbh stats` / `sbh tune` as user -> SBH-2102 "attempt to write a readonly database"; `sudo sbh stats` -> `no_database` at /root/.local/share (fix 32f1550 unreleased); `sbh log` -> permission denied.
- `check --predict` silently falls through (reads `state.rates` never written); status "Rate Estimates" dead.
- `sbh uninstall --dry-run` / `--keep-data` are clap errors; the 5-mode planner in src/cli/uninstall.rs is unreferenced; `--purge` deletes config/data/ballast with no backup.
- `sbh bootstrap` does not exist; src/cli/bootstrap.rs (2,860 lines) has zero callers; README says it runs during install.
- `sbh dashboard` -> "TUI feature not enabled. Rebuild with --features tui" on every distributed binary.
- The README config example is silently ignored (no deny_unknown_fields): `[monitor]`, `[logging]`, `[guardrails]`, `[scoring.weights]`, `[policy] mode`, `per_volume_*`, `file_size_mb`; default `initial_mode` is Enforce.
- Exit codes and streams are inconsistent; `--no-color`, `-q`, `-v` are no-ops.

## Children
W3.1 DaemonProbe · W3.2 read-only opens and path parity · W3.3 predict/rates surfaces · W3.4 exit-code contract · W3.5 uninstall planner wired · W3.6 bootstrap wired · W3.7 TUI by default · W3.8 strict config.

## Acceptance
CLI e2e in CI against a user install and a root-owned system-install fixture (sudo job) covering every child; README config example round-trips through `sbh config validate` with zero unknown keys.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- `sbh stats --window 24h` as an unprivileged user against the root-owned system DB fails: `[SBH-2102] SQL failure in rusqlite: attempt to write a readonly database` because `SqliteLogger::open` always uses `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_WRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` (`logger/sqlite.rs:32-36`); the v0.5.1 root-DB hint only fires on `no_database` and hard-codes `/root/.local/share/sbh/activity.sqlite3` (`cli_app.rs:2439`), ignoring `/var/lib/sbh` and XDG.
- `status`/`check` JSON on Linux emits, for every mount, `platform: { darwin: { apfs: { ...all null... } } }` plus a hard-coded `free_excludes_purgeable: true` (`cli_app.rs:7101-7141` calls `capacity_platform_json()` unconditionally). Docs describe the block as a macOS feature.
- `sbh version --verbose` prints `git_sha/profile/target/timestamp = "unknown"` for every build: `emit_version` (`cli_app.rs:10076-10085`) reads `option_env!` vars that nothing sets; there is no `build.rs`; `release.yml` exports nothing.

- Ballast: `verify()` takes no flock (`manager.rs:524`); `install.rs:230` `provision(None)` skips the free-space guard; unknown filesystem types default to random-data writes rather than probing `fallocate` (`coordinator.rs:567`).

title: DaemonProbe: pidfile + service manager + state freshness; delete the /proc cmdline scan; state_age fields
description:
# daemon_running must mean a live daemon

## Design
- Daemon writes `<data_dir>/sbh.pid` by default (existing `--pidfile` becomes an override) and removes it on clean shutdown.
- `DaemonProbe { pidfile_alive (kill(pid,0) && /proc/<pid>/comm == "sbh" or macOS proc name), service_active (systemctl is-active sbh.service / launchctl print), state_fresh }`; `daemon_running = pidfile_alive || service_active`; JSON gains `state_age_secs`, `state_stale`, `probe {...}`; human mode prints "state 3d stale" instead of "running"; `policy_mode` is only reported from fresh state.
- Delete `detect_daemon_running_fallback`'s cmdline scan.

## Acceptance
Unit tests with fake pidfiles and a fake service-manager runner; e2e: dead daemon with stale state -> `daemon_running: false, state_stale: true`; live sandbox daemon -> true.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.3 — G1.3: Daemon liveness via kernel-locked daemon.lock; remove /proc substring heuristic; report reasons and service gates
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G1.3 - Daemon liveness truth: a kernel-locked `daemon.lock` replaces the `/proc` substring heuristic; status reports why the daemon is not running

## Context
`cli_app.rs:6565-6595`: `daemon_running` is true if `state.json` is fresher than 90 s, else `detect_daemon_running_fallback()` (`:7031-7070`): `systemctl is-active sbh.service` == "active", or any `/proc/*/cmdline` containing both "sbh" and "daemon". During the audit this matched the auditor's own zsh process (its cmdline contained the words), so `sbh status` reported the daemon running three days after it was stopped. The dashboard adapter and `check --predict` reuse the same state-file logic. The state file itself is not an exclusive-ownership signal.

## Goal
Exactly one source of truth for "a daemon owns this state directory": an exclusive advisory lock held for the daemon's lifetime; everything else is diagnostic detail.

## Design
- `daemon/self_monitor.rs`: `DaemonLock::acquire(state_dir) -> Result<DaemonLock>` opens `<state_dir>/daemon.lock` (0o600, create), `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` via `nix`, writes `{pid, started_at, version}` JSON, keeps the fd open; drop releases. `DaemonLock::probe(state_dir) -> LockProbe { held: bool, owner: Option<{pid, started_at, version}> }` tries `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` on a fresh fd and releases immediately. A second daemon start fails fast with SBH-3003 "daemon already running (pid N)".
- `cli_app.rs` status/check/dashboard adapters: `daemon_running = probe.held`; `daemon_state_reason` in `{locked, no_lock, no_lock_stale_state, unit_inactive, unit_condition_failed, lock_dir_unreadable}`; when the CLI user cannot read the state dir (root daemon, user CLI) it reports `lock_dir_unreadable` and falls back to `systemctl is-active` / `launchctl print` only, never to `/proc` substrings. Remove `detect_daemon_running_fallback`'s Method 2 entirely.
- Service gates: on Linux, `systemctl show sbh.service -p ActiveState,SubState,ConditionResult,ConditionTimestamp,LoadState` and parse drop-ins (`systemctl cat`) for `ConditionPathExists=` lines; report `service_gates: [{kind: "condition_path_exists", path, satisfied}]` in status JSON and a human hint "service disabled by /etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED". macOS equivalent from `launchctl print` (`daemon/service/launchctl.rs`).
- Daemon: acquire the lock before spawning workers; include `lock_path` in the startup log; release on shutdown after the final state write (G3.2).

## Files
`src/daemon/self_monitor.rs`, `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs`, `src/tui/adapters.rs`, `src/daemon/service/{systemd,launchctl}.rs`, `src/core/errors.rs` (new code), README state-file protocol section.

## Tests
- Unit: acquire/probe/release; second acquire fails; probe after drop reports not held; JSON payload round-trip; permission-denied path yields `lock_dir_unreadable`.
- Integration (`tests/integration_tests.rs`): spawn `sbh daemon --config <tmp>` in the background, wait for the lock, `sbh status --json` -> `daemon_running=true reason=locked`; kill the daemon -> `false reason=no_lock_stale_state`; meanwhile run a decoy process whose argv contains "sbh daemon" (for example `sh -c 'sleep 30 # sbh daemon'`) and assert it does not flip the answer.
- Unit (`systemd.rs`): parse fixture `systemctl show`/`cat` output with a `ConditionPathExists=!/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED` drop-in -> gate reported unsatisfied when the file exists.
- e2e: status liveness case.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host today: `sbh status --json` -> `daemon_running=false`, `daemon_state_reason=unit_condition_failed`, gate path shown.
- [ ] `sbh daemon` refuses to start twice against one state dir.
- [ ] No reference to `/proc` cmdline scanning remains in `cli_app.rs`.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.1.3
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.1, closed as duplicate): also expose `state_age_secs` and `state_stale: bool` in status JSON and print "state N stale" in human mode; report `policy_mode` only from fresh state; keep `--pidfile` as an override of the default pidfile written next to daemon.lock. Observed on the operator host: JSON said daemon_running=true while human mode said "not running (degraded mode)" in the same minute.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: the kernel flock on `daemon.lock` is the liveness primitive (released on crash, no PID-reuse race; 4.9 and 6.3 build on it); the pidfile is informational; service-manager probe only when the lock dir is unreadable; never `/proc` cmdline. Keep `state_age_secs`, `state_stale`, fresh-only `policy_mode`. Lifecycle case "double start refused" lives here.

# G5.3 - LogSearch screen: query line, filters over SQLite/JSONL adapters, pagination

## Context
`tui/render.rs` `frame_log_search_header_styled` renders `query <not-yet-editable>`; `render_log_search` prints `mode=timeline-mirror` and "Timeline telemetry powers this preview."; `update.rs:454-463` has no LogSearch key arm; only mouse click/scroll (`:739-756`). The adapters (`tui/telemetry.rs:361-660`: SQLite read-only queries + JSONL tail) already load events for the Timeline. `docs/dashboard-information-architecture.md:130,345` specify `/` to search. README L462 promises search and filter.

## Design
- Model: `LogSearchState { query: String, editing: bool, filters: { event_type: Option<String>, min_level: Option<Level>, since: Option<Duration> }, results: Vec<EventRow>, cursor, page }`.
- Keys on screen 6: `/` starts editing (overlay-less inline input), `Enter` runs, `Esc` cancels editing, `n`/`p` next/prev page, `t` cycles event type, `l` cycles min level, `s` cycles since (15m/1h/24h/all), `c` clears.
- Query grammar: free text substring over `message`/`path`; tokens `type:<event>`, `level:<lvl>`, `path:<prefix>`, `id:<decision-id>` (G2). Case-insensitive.
- Data: `telemetry::search_events(query, filters, page)` — SQLite `activity_log` (indexed by ts; substring via `LIKE` with escaped wildcards) and, when SQLite is unavailable, a bounded JSONL tail scan (last N MiB). Results carry `source: sqlite|jsonl`.
- Rendering: header shows the query and active filters; empty state explains how to search; degraded mode explains which source is missing.

## Files
`src/tui/{model,update,input,render,telemetry,layout}.rs`, docs/dashboard-information-architecture.md (mark implemented), README.

## Tests
- Unit: grammar parser (tokens, escaping), key routing on screen 6, pagination math.
- Property (proptest): filtered result set is always a subset of the unfiltered set; `id:` token returns at most one row per id.
- Unit (`telemetry.rs`): SQLite search on a fixture DB; JSONL fallback on a fixture file; `LIKE` wildcard escaping.
- Snapshot (`test_snapshot_golden.rs`): LogSearch frame with a query and with the empty state.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `/ type:deletion path:/data/tmp` returns only deletion rows under `/data/tmp` on a fixture; screenshots in the signoff addendum (G5.5).

# G5.7 - Incident replay: `sbh dashboard --replay <activity.jsonl>` drives the cockpit from a captured log with a time scrubber

## Why (ambition round 1)
Postmortems today mean reading JSONL by hand. The TUI already has a deterministic replay harness (`tui/test_replay.rs`, `parity_harness.rs`) that feeds recorded telemetry through the update function. Expose it.

## Design

- `--export-frames <dir>` writes text frames for reports (reusing the e2e artifact renderer).

## Files
`src/tui/{runtime,adapters,model,update,render}.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs`, README dashboard section.

- Unit: JSONL -> timeline reconstruction (out-of-order and truncated lines tolerated); scrubber math.
- Scenario drill: replay the fixture from `tests/decision_plane_e2e.rs` and assert screen states at three timestamps; frames snapshot.

## Success criteria

title: Read-only SQLite/JSONL opens for stats, tune, status, log; sudo hint with real system paths; config path parity
description:
# Read-only commands must work on a system install

## Design
- `SqliteLogger::open_read_only(path)` (`?mode=ro`, then `immutable=1` fallback); `stats`, `tune` (read-only path), `status` recent activity, `log` use it; when unreadable, print the resolved system paths and the `sudo sbh ...` hint (extend the v0.5.1 hint to `/var/lib/sbh` and platform system dirs, not just /root).
- `sbh config path` resolves through the same function as `Config::load` and prints which candidate won and why.
- `sbh tune` read-only path must not open the stats DB at all unless `--apply`.

## Acceptance
CLI e2e on the root-owned fixture: all four commands succeed read-only as an unprivileged user; `config path` and `config validate` agree.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.1 — G10.1: stats/explain/blame/log open SQLite read-only; permission-aware hint resolves the real system data dir
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G10.1 - `stats`, `explain`, `blame`, `log` open the activity store read-only and give a permission-aware hint that resolves the real system data dir

## Context
See G10. `SqliteLogger::open` (`logger/sqlite.rs:32-36`) is used for both daemon writes and CLI reads. `run_stats` (`cli_app.rs:2430-2463`) hint logic. `core/config.rs:925-948` knows the platform system data dir (`/var/lib/sbh`, `/private/var/sbh`).

## Design
- `SqliteLogger::open_read_only(path)` with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX` and `immutable=0`; WAL read works for readers with directory read access; no schema creation on the read path.
- `StatsEngine`/`explain`/`blame`/`log` use the read-only opener. On `EACCES`/`readonly`/`unable to open`, the CLI resolves candidate DB paths in order: configured path, platform system data dir, XDG data dir of the invoking user, `/root/.local/share/sbh` (legacy) and reports which exists but is unreadable, with `hint: "sudo sbh stats ..."` and `root_db_path` set to the found path (not a hard-coded one). JSON error code stays SBH-2102 for genuine SQL failures; permission cases use SBH-3001 with `reason: permission_denied`.
- Human output: one line "activity database at /var/lib/sbh/activity.sqlite3 is owned by root; rerun with sudo" instead of the raw rusqlite message.

## Files
`src/logger/sqlite.rs`, `src/logger/stats.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (stats/blame/log/explain), README troubleshooting.

## Tests
- Unit: read-only open of a fixture DB succeeds and refuses writes; open of a 0o000 file yields the permission path (skip when running as root, logged).
- Unit: candidate-path resolution order with a mock platform (Linux user/system, macOS).
- Integration: `sbh stats --json` against a read-only fixture returns `hint` and `root_db_path`; exit code documented.
- e2e case in the Stats section.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host, unprivileged `sbh stats --window 24h` prints the sudo hint with `/var/lib/sbh/activity.sqlite3`, and `sudo sbh stats` works unchanged.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.1
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.2, closed as duplicate): `sbh tune` (read-only path) must not open the stats DB at all unless `--apply`; `sbh config path` must resolve through the same function as `Config::load` and print which candidate won (today it prints a nonexistent user path while every other command uses /etc/sbh/config.toml). bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.3 (check --predict and the status rate block from state.json v2 rates) is related.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: `mode=ro` first; `immutable=1` only when the DB directory is not writable by the caller (a WAL reader must create `-shm`, which is the real failure on root-owned /var/lib/sbh); log which path was used. Re-verify the `config path` bullet at HEAD (32f1550 unified resolution) and narrow it.
notes: Canonical bead (2026-09-02). The parallel tree's bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.1 were merged here and their descriptions appended above. An earlier note called this a duplicate; that was reversed.
close_reason: Done on main: fe8e7a7 (read-only SQLite opens for stats/status/tune + permission-aware hint resolving the real system data dir) and the config-path commit (one resolver shared by Config::load and 'config path' with source/reason/shadowed file; 'sbh log' structured refusal with daemon-log hint). Proof: lib test open_read_only_queries_but_never_writes_or_creates, resolver unit test, integration test config_path_and_validate_agree_and_log_explains_missing_file; live: unprivileged 'sbh stats --json' on this host reads the root-owned /var/lib/sbh DB. Self-verified by OliveIbis, not independently verified. Not done: root-owned fixture e2e for all four commands as an unprivileged user (would need a root-owned fixture), 'config set/reset' still write the per-user default path.

title: Exit-code contract (C-EXIT), stream discipline, and real -q/-v/--no-color
description:
# Exit-code and stream contract (C-EXIT)

Flag handling (-v/-q/--no-color) is owned by bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.5; this bead owns exit codes and streams.

## Contract
0 ok · 1 user error or pressure condition · 2 runtime/IO failure · 3 internal · 4 partial success. `clean`/`emergency` return 4 when `items_failed > 0` (today they return 0 after printing the summary); `check` pressure/`--need` unmet -> 1 (today 2, indistinguishable from I/O failure); `emergency` with no candidates -> 0 like `clean` (today 1). Human reports to stdout, diagnostics to stderr everywhere (`check` and `emergency` currently print reports to stderr). Vetoes are never an exit-code class; they are listed under `rejected`.

## Deliverables
Table in a `cli_app.rs` doc comment and README; a single mapping function; CLI e2e asserting code and stream per documented case; `sbh --help` epilog matches.

## Context

title: Wire the uninstall planner: --dry-run, --keep-data/--keep-config/--keep-assets, backup-first --purge, JSON plan
description:
# The README's uninstall matrix, for real

## Background
src/cli/uninstall.rs implements `CleanupMode` (Conservative/KeepData/KeepConfig/KeepAssets/Purge), 13 removal categories, `plan_uninstall`/`execute_uninstall`, backups and dry_run — with zero callers. The live `run_uninstall` (src/cli_app.rs:1985) only unregisters the service; `--purge` -> `run_uninstall_cleanup` (src/cli/install.rs:402-470) deletes ballast, data dir, config with no backup and no dry-run.

## Design
`UninstallArgs` gains `--dry-run`, `--keep-data`, `--keep-config`, `--keep-assets`, `--backup-dir`; `run_uninstall` -> `plan_uninstall` -> print plan -> `execute_uninstall` backup-first; `--purge` requires `--yes` when non-TTY and always backs up config plus the last 1 MiB of each log; add `BallastPool` to the planner; JSON = plan + results.

## Acceptance
installer_e2e: each mode against a fixture install asserts the exact matrix from README; dry-run changes nothing; backups exist; README matrix regenerated from a doc-test.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.7.2 — G6.2: Uninstall modes --keep-data/--keep-config/--keep-assets/--purge, --dry-run, --json wired to cli/uninstall.rs
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G6.2 - Uninstall cleanup modes: `--keep-data | --keep-config | --keep-assets | --purge`, `--dry-run`, `--json`, wired to `cli/uninstall.rs`

## Context
See G6. `uninstall.rs:23-33` `CleanupMode`, `:75-88` `RemovalCategory` (binary, config-file, data-directory, state-file, sqlite-db, jsonl-log, asset-cache, systemd-unit, launchd-plist, shell-completion, shell-profile-entry, ballast-pool, backup-file), `plan_uninstall`, `execute_uninstall`, `backup_first` semantics (`:62,573`). `cli_app.rs:1985-2050` `run_uninstall` removes the service then, for `--purge`, calls `install::run_uninstall_cleanup` (hard-coded flags).

## Design
- `UninstallArgs` gains `--keep-data`, `--keep-config`, `--keep-assets` (clap group, mutually exclusive with each other and with `--purge`; none = Conservative), `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--yes` (required for non-dry-run destructive modes unless stdin is a TTY and the operator confirms).
- Flow: service teardown (existing) -> `plan_uninstall(mode, paths, platform)` -> print plan (categories, backup_first flags) -> if not dry-run: `execute_uninstall(plan)` -> report (removed, backed-up, skipped, errors). `--json` emits plan and results.
- `install::run_uninstall_cleanup`: retired in favor of the module; its two call sites route through `plan/execute` (no compatibility shim per AGENTS.md).
- Ballast pools on other volumes (coordinator-managed, for example `/data/.sbh/ballast`) are included in the `ballast-pool` category from the coordinator's inventory, not only the configured dir.
- Safety: never remove anything outside the known footprint set; symlink-safe; `.sbh-protect`-irrelevant (not a scan).

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs`, `src/cli/uninstall.rs`, `src/cli/install.rs`, README uninstall section (table regenerated), AGENTS.md CLI table, CHANGELOG.

## Tests
- Unit (`--bin sbh`): flag group exclusivity; default mode Conservative.
- Integration (`tests/installer_e2e.rs`): a fixture install footprint (binary, config, sqlite, jsonl, state, completions, profile line, unit file, ballast dirs on two volumes) -> for each mode, `--dry-run --json` lists exactly the documented categories; executing `--keep-data --yes` leaves sqlite/jsonl in place and backs up config; `--purge --yes` removes everything and the backup dir holds the `backup_first` items.
- e2e section "Uninstall modes" (with `SBH_E2E_SKIP_DESTRUCTIVE` respected).

## Success criteria
- [ ] README uninstall table (5 modes x 6 columns) is generated from `CleanupMode` and true.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.7.2
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.5, closed as duplicate): `--purge` should always back up config plus the last 1 MiB of each log; the planner today never plans `BallastPool` (add it, including coordinator per-mount pools).

(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

2. `scripts/e2e_test.sh`: sections "Bootstrap" and "Uninstall modes" with per-case logs, destructive cases gated by `SBH_E2E_SKIP_DESTRUCTIVE`.
3. `sbh docs --json` (G8.2) exports `bootstrap.reasons`, `bootstrap.actions`, `uninstall.modes`; README tables regenerate from them; parity test.
4. Logging: `[SBH-BOOTSTRAP] reason=<id> action=<id> path=... backup=...` per action; `[SBH-UNINSTALL] category=<id> path=... backup_first=<bool> result=<ok|skipped|error>` per item.

title: Wire sbh bootstrap [--dry-run|--apply] and run it at the end of sbh install

# Bootstrap self-healing must be reachable

## Background
src/cli/bootstrap.rs: 15 `MigrationReason`s and 10 `ActionKind`s match README; `run_migration`/`scan_footprints` have no callers outside the file; only RemoveProfileLine, DeduplicateProfile, UpdateServicePath, RemoveOrphanedFile create backups. `Command::Bootstrap { dry_run, apply, json }`; `sbh install` ends with a dry-run report and applies automatically under `--auto`; every mutating action calls `create_backup` (FixPermissions, CopyLegacy*, CleanupBackup, CreateDirectory, InitStateFile added); a doc-test renders the reason/action tables for README; AGENTS.md count fixed.

# G6.1 - `sbh bootstrap [--dry-run] [--json]`, install-time safe repairs, `doctor --env` health report

## Context

- `doctor --env`: read-only scan -> health state + reasons (no mutation), sharing the check-id style of `--system`.
- Add `MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift` using G3.3's `UnitDrift`, and `LaunchdPlistDrift` for macOS.

# Users must get the dashboard the README describes

## Background
Cargo.toml: `tui` is not a default feature; release.yml, ci.yml, scripts/install.sh cargo fallback, `cargo install --git`, and Homebrew all build without it. `sbh dashboard` -> "TUI feature not enabled" (exit 2) on every shipped binary. ## Design
- `default = ["cli", "daemon", "sqlite", "tui"]`; verify `cargo install --git` on a clean machine resolves ftui from the pinned tag; CI `tui` lane (W0.2); release builds with tui.
- Quick-release executes through `BallastCoordinator::release_for_mount` after an Enter-confirmed overlay; `--start-screen <screen>`; `REDUCE_MOTION` honored in theme.rs; docs name `preferences.json`.
- `src/cli/dashboard.rs` and the runtime path that references it are gated behind `feature = "legacy-crossterm-dashboard"` (off) with a doc comment; deletion requires operator permission (AGENTS.md).

## Acceptance
`sbh dashboard` opens on a release build under a PTY in the e2e script (replace the 17a-17f cases that currently assert the error); TUI tests run in CI; `x` releases one file in the sandbox.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". # G5.2 - Ballast screen actions execute: confirmation Enter handler, release/replenish executor, result toasts, activity events

## Context
`tui/update.rs:401-410` opens `Overlay::Confirmation(ConfirmAction::BallastRelease)` on `x`; `tui/render.rs:3592-3630` draws "Enter Confirm"; `tui/input.rs:206-251` `resolve_overlay_key` has no Enter arm for `Confirmation` -> `consumed_without_action()`; no code anywhere in `src/tui` calls `BallastManager`/coordinator. `handle_ballast_key` (`update.rs:556-583`) only navigates. README L461/L471/L492 promise release/replenish controls and a one-keystroke quick-release.

## Design
- Elm-style: `Msg::ConfirmOverlay` -> `Cmd::Ballast(BallastCmd::{ReleaseOne(volume), ReleaseAll(volume), Replenish(volume)})`; the runtime executes commands on a worker thread (never on the render thread) through a `DashboardActions` trait implemented by `BallastCoordinator` (same flock and safety path as the CLI: `manager.release(n)` / `replenish_one()`), returning `Msg::BallastResult { volume, outcome }`. Model shows a toast (success: bytes freed; failure: error text) and refreshes the ballast telemetry.
- Overlay keys: `Enter`/`y` confirm, `Esc`/`n` cancel; confirmation text names the volume and file count; a second confirmation for ReleaseAll.
- Activity event: `ActivityEvent::BallastReleased { source: "dashboard" }` so `stats`/timeline attribute it; decision ID not applicable.
- Degraded mode (no daemon/state): actions still work (the coordinator is CLI-side), but the toast warns that the daemon will not replenish until it runs.
- Tests-first: `DashboardActions` has a mock in `tui/test_harness.rs`.

`src/tui/{model,update,input,render,runtime}.rs`, `src/tui/test_harness.rs`, `src/ballast/coordinator.rs` (trait impl), `src/logger/dual.rs` (event source field), README dashboard section.

- Unit (`tui/runtime.rs`): command executes on the worker thread and delivers the result message; failure path.
- Scenario drill (`tui/test_scenario_drills.rs`): "quick-release under Red" end to end with the mock actions.
- Integration (`tests/dashboard_integration_tests.rs`, tui-gated): real coordinator on a temp pool: release one file via the action trait; inventory decreases; flock respected (concurrent CLI release does not corrupt).

title: Strict config: deny_unknown_fields, config_version, did-you-mean diagnostics, tilde expansion, auto_provision honored, README example as a test fixture
description:
# A config file that is silently wrong is worse than one that fails

## Background
No `deny_unknown_fields` anywhere (src/core/config.rs); `sbh config validate` cannot flag unknown keys. README example keys that vanish on load: `[monitor]` (all), `[ballast] per_volume_file_count/per_volume_file_size_mb`, `[ballast.overrides.*] file_size_mb`, `[scoring.weights]`, `[policy] mode/canary_delete_cap_per_hour/fallback_safe`, `[guardrails]`, `[logging] sqlite_path/jsonl_path`. `[policy] initial_mode` defaults to Enforce, so `mode = "observe"` from the README leaves a deleting daemon. `[notifications.file] path = "~/..."` creates a literal `~` directory. `[ballast] auto_provision` is never read.

## Design
- `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on every config struct; `Config::load` collects unknown keys with a did-you-mean (Levenshtein over the real key set) and (a) `config validate` fails listing them, (b) the daemon warns per key at startup and refuses to start when `[core] strict_config = true` (default true for system services, false for user).
- `config_version = 2` at the top; v1 files migrated by bootstrap (`deprecated-config-key` with backup).
- Tilde and `$HOME` expansion for every path-typed field; `auto_provision` honored (daemon skips provisioning when false).
- The README config example is committed as tests/fixtures/readme-config.toml and parsed in CI.

## Acceptance
Unit: unknown key -> error with suggestion; expansion; version. CI: fixture validates; `config validate` on the operator workstation's /etc/sbh/config.toml reports zero unknown keys after the README rewrite.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.9.1 — G8.1: Config strictness — unknown keys detected with did-you-mean suggestions; config validate --strict; doctor check
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G8.1 - Config strictness: unknown keys are detected, warned with did-you-mean suggestions, and rejected under `config validate --strict`

## Context
`core/config.rs:20-35` `Config` and every section are `#[serde(default)]` with no `deny_unknown_fields`; `load()` (`:1135-1136`) parses leniently. Deprecated keys (`scan_interval_secs`, `max_ballast_mb`, `log_level`) are only detected by the (unreachable) bootstrap scanner (`cli/bootstrap.rs:878`). README's own example is mostly unknown keys; the operator's live config carries `[scoring.weights]`.

## Design
- Two-pass load: parse into `StrictConfig` (same structs re-declared via a derive attribute swap is not possible in serde; instead use `toml::Table` traversal): after lenient parse, walk the raw `toml::Table` and compare every key path against a generated `KNOWN_KEYS: &[&str]` (produced by a small `#[derive(KeyPaths)]`-free approach: a hand-maintained list is unacceptable; generate it in `build.rs` from a JSON schema emitted by `schemars`? No new heavy deps: derive the key list by serializing `Config::default()` to `toml::Value` and walking it, plus explicit entries for map-like sections such as `ballast.overrides.*` and `notifications.*`). Unknown paths produce `ConfigWarning { path, suggestion }` where `suggestion` is the nearest known key by Damerau-Levenshtein distance <= 3 within the same section, with special-case aliases table for the known README mistakes (`scoring.weights.location` -> `scoring.location_weight`, `monitor.pressure_green_pct` -> `pressure.green_min_free_pct`, `ballast.per_volume_file_count` -> `ballast.file_count`, `logging.sqlite_path` -> `paths.sqlite_db`, `policy.mode` -> `policy.initial_mode`, `guardrails.calibration_floor` -> `scoring.calibration_floor`, and the three deprecated keys).
- Surfaces: `[SBH-CONFIG] unknown key <path> (did you mean <suggestion>?)` on stderr at daemon start, `install`, and every CLI load (once per process); `config validate` lists them as WARN; `config validate --strict` (and `SBH_CONFIG_STRICT=1`) exits 1; `doctor --system` check `config.unknown_keys`.
- JSON: `config validate --json` gains `unknown_keys: [{path, suggestion}]`.

## Files
`src/core/config.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (validate/doctor/install), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs` (startup log), README configuration section (example rewritten in G8.3; here, add the "Unknown keys" paragraph), CHANGELOG.

## Tests
- Unit: every key in the README example (as of G8.3) is known -> zero warnings; the pre-fix README example yields exactly the documented set of unknown keys with the expected suggestions; deprecated keys map to their replacements; map sections (`ballast.overrides."/data".enabled`) are not flagged.
- Unit: `KNOWN_KEYS` derivation covers every field (test: serialize `Config::default()`, assert each leaf path is known; assert a deliberately unknown path is flagged).
- Integration: `sbh config validate --strict` exit 1 on a fixture with `[scoring.weights]`; exit 0 after correction.
- e2e case.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh config validate --strict` flags `scoring.weights.*` with suggestions.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.9.1
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.4.8, closed as duplicate): also `config_version = 2` at the top with bootstrap migration of v1 files; tilde and $HOME expansion for every path-typed field (`[notifications.file] path = "~/..."` currently creates a literal `~` dir); honor `[ballast] auto_provision` (never read today); strict mode default true for system services; commit the README example as tests/fixtures/readme-config.toml parsed in CI.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: the merged G8.1 lenient two-pass design (no `deny_unknown_fields`, no refuse-to-start default): unknown keys warn with did-you-mean at every load, `config validate --strict` / `SBH_CONFIG_STRICT=1` fail, `doctor` check; `config_version` at top level (no `[core]` section). Blocked by 4.6 (v1 migration action). Fixture: the operator's `/etc/sbh/config.toml` (redacted) must load with warnings and exit 0 unless `--strict`.

title: Daemon control socket: ping, live status, scan-now, reload, policy promote/demote, explain, ballast release, shutdown (W3)
description:
# G13 - Daemon control socket: `ping`, live `status`, `scan-now`, `reload`, `policy promote|demote`, `explain`, `ballast release`, `shutdown` over a Unix domain socket

## Why (ambition round 1)
Control today is signals (SIGHUP reload, SIGUSR1 scan) plus a 30-second state file. That leaves no authoritative liveness answer (G1.3 adds the lock), no way to promote policy without editing config and signalling, no live data for the dashboard, and no way to ask the daemon what it is about to do. A tiny request/response socket fixes all four without an async runtime.

## Design
- `daemon/control.rs` (new module; genuinely new functionality): `std::os::unix::net::UnixListener` bound at `<state_dir>/control.sock` (unlink stale socket after the daemon lock is held; mode 0o600; owner = daemon user), one listener thread, one short-lived handler thread per connection (bounded to 8 concurrent), JSON-lines protocol: request `{ "cmd": "...", "args": {...}, "token": "..." }`, response `{ "ok": bool, "result": ..., "error": {code, message} }`. The per-boot token is written into `daemon.lock` (G1.3) so a client that can read the lock file can talk; root daemon + user CLI cannot read it and fall back to the state file (`daemon_state_reason = socket_unreadable`).
- Commands: `ping` -> {pid, started_at, version, uptime_s, policy_mode}; `status` -> the same document `status --json` builds, from live memory; `scan-now {paths?, force?}` -> enqueues a forced `ScanRequest` (same path SIGUSR1 uses); `reload` -> same as SIGHUP; `policy {action: promote|demote|status}` -> calls `PolicyEngine::promote()`/`demote()` (G9.1 semantics) and persists the new `initial_mode` to config with a backup so restarts keep it; `explain {id}` -> live record if still in memory else ledger lookup; `ballast {release: n | replenish}` -> coordinator under the daemon's flock; `shutdown` -> graceful.
- CLI: `sbh daemon ping|scan-now|reload|shutdown`, `sbh policy promote|demote|status` (G9.3), `status` prefers the socket when reachable (`source: "socket" | "state_file"` in JSON), dashboard adapter uses it for sub-second refresh and for G5.2 actions when the daemon runs.
- Safety: every mutating command is logged as an activity event with the client's uid (from `SO_PEERCRED` via `nix`) and echoed in `explain`; rate-limited (10 req/s); unknown commands rejected; the socket is excluded from scanning (it lives in the state dir).
- macOS: same code (Unix sockets); launchd path under Application Support.

## Files
`src/daemon/control.rs` (new), `src/daemon/{loop_main,self_monitor,policy}.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs`, `src/tui/adapters.rs`, `src/core/config.rs` (`daemon.control_socket_enabled`, default true), README (new "Controlling the daemon" section), AGENTS.md CLI table.

## Tests
- Unit: protocol framing, token check, peer-cred logging, rate limit, concurrency bound, stale-socket cleanup.
- Integration (`tests/daemon_lifecycle.rs` from G3.4): `ping` < 50 ms; `scan-now` produces `scan_complete reason=forced`; `policy promote` observe -> canary persisted; `shutdown` exits 0; socket absent after exit; a client without the token is refused.
- Fuzz (G7.6): protocol parser.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `sbh daemon ping` is the answer `status` uses when it can; the `/proc` heuristic is gone (G1.3) and the state file is the last resort.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Blocked by 6.1 (lifecycle harness) and 2.16 (`sbh policy` owner); stale bridge edge removed.

title: W4: One release asset contract, a working updater, and a live pipeline (v0.5.2)
description:
# W4 — Release contract, updater, pipeline

## Background
- v0.5.0/v0.5.1 assets: `sbh_darwin_amd64`, `sbh_darwin_arm64`, `sbh_linux_amd64`, `sbh_linux_arm64`, `SHA256SUMS` (hand-published; no workflow run). The Rust updater (`ReleaseArtifactContract::asset_name_for_tag`, src/cli/mod.rs:262-270; `artifact_url_for_tag`, src/cli/update.rs:1096) constructs `sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz` + `.sha256` and never probes: `sbh update --version v0.5.0 --dry-run` on the workstation resolved a URL that does not exist. Every future `sbh update` on the fleet 404s. scripts/install.sh already probes raw names (commits 4837603, 702367e).
- v0.5.1 macOS binaries: arm64 has an ad-hoc signature only (CodeDirectory slot, flags 0x20002, no CMS blob), amd64 has no LC_CODE_SIGNATURE. scripts/install.sh's trust check refuses them unless `--no-verify`; the updater's codesign check would too. v0.4.28 (2026-06-08) was the last Developer-ID signed, notarized, workflow-built release.
- Release workflow: failed at the clippy gate for v0.4.30..v0.4.40, then disabled; Homebrew tap frozen at v0.4.28; no `.sigstore.json` has ever shipped; README Option 3 (`--pattern "sbh-*.tar.xz"`) matches nothing.
- `sbh version --verbose` shows all-"unknown" build metadata.

## Children
W4.1 contract + updater probe · W4.2 Release workflow restored · W4.3 post-publish audit + manual fallback parity · W4.4 build metadata · W4.5 cut v0.5.2 and verify.

## Acceptance
`sbh update` 0.5.1 -> 0.5.2 succeeds on the operator workstation, one rch VPS and one Mac; both asset layouts verify; tap at v0.5.2; bd-t951 closes on the post-publish audit.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Consolidation note (2026-09-02)
A parallel reality check produced the bead tree `bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx` (G0-G12) with overlapping scope. Duplicated children of this epic were closed in favor of the G-tree and their unique details appended there as notes; the remaining children here are the parts the G-tree does not cover. Cross-tree blocking and related edges record the interplay. See docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md section 5b.

(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G4 - Release contract: one source of truth for asset names, checksums, provenance, updater, installers, workflow, and Homebrew tap

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- Three asset naming schemes coexist: `release.yml` emits `sbh-v{tag}-{triple}.tar.xz` + `.sha256` + `SHA256SUMS.txt` + `release-provenance.json`; the legacy scheme is `sbh-{triple}.tar.xz`; the v0.5.0/v0.5.1 releases were hand-published (no workflow run exists for those tags) with raw binaries `sbh_linux_amd64`, `sbh_linux_arm64`, `sbh_darwin_amd64`, `sbh_darwin_arm64` and one aggregate `SHA256SUMS`.
- `scripts/install.sh:398-535` probes versioned -> legacy -> raw; root `install.sh` (91 lines, a different file) knows only raw; `src/cli/mod.rs:263-275` (`ReleaseArtifactContract::asset_name_for_tag`) and `update.rs:1096-1102` know only the first two. `curl -I` on `.../v0.5.1/sbh-v0.5.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz` -> 404; `.../sbh_linux_amd64` -> 200. So `sbh update` (apply) is broken for every v0.5.x user the moment a newer release appears; `--check` passes only because the binary is current.
- Updater `curl` calls (`update.rs:1178-1204`) send no User-Agent; AGENTS.md requires `OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0` on every web request.
- `release.yml` last succeeded for v0.4.28 (2026-06-08); the 12 later tag runs failed or were cancelled; all three workflows are `disabled_manually`; the Homebrew tap `Dicklesworthstone/homebrew-sbh` formula is at v0.4.28; the in-repo `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` holds v0.4.8 placeholder hashes.
- `SigstorePolicy::Optional` is unreachable in product code; checksum parsing handles GNU `hash  file` but not BSD `SHA256 (file) = hash`; no cosign step exists in the workflow although `cli/mod.rs:1098` models a `.sigstore.json` asset.
- bd-t951 (open) covers only a post-publish asset audit.

## Goal
The updater, both installers, the release workflow, the provenance manifest, and the tap formula are generated from or validated against one Rust `ReleaseContract`, so a naming change in one place cannot silently break another; the updater resolves today's live release; every web request carries the required User-Agent.

## Children
G4.1 `ReleaseContract` module + updater + UA; G4.2 installers/workflow/formula/tap consume it + asset audit job (absorbs bd-t951); G4.3 doctor --release drift + network/static tests; G4.4 external operator actions (re-enable workflows, republish v0.5.x contract assets, tap update, branch protection).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- The earlier consolidation note is superseded: the parallel G-tree was merged INTO this tree; every child here is canonical and carries the merged text.

# The updater must find what the release actually contains

## Design
- Contract C-ASSET in src/cli/mod.rs: canonical `sbh-<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz` + `.sha256` + `.sigstore.json`; mirror `sbh_<os>_<arch>` + `SHA256SUMS`; `release-provenance.json`. A test asserts scripts/install.sh's probe strategy block equals the contract's rendering (`--print-install-strategies`).
- `probe_release_assets(tag)`: GitHub API asset list (with the required user agent), then HEAD probes of `releases/download/<tag>/<name>` in contract order, then the offline manifest; select canonical if present else mirror; checksum mandatory for both (`.sha256` sidecar or `SHA256SUMS` entry); sigstore `Required` when a bundle exists.
- Actionable error when nothing matches, naming the assets found.

## Acceptance
