# G4.1 - `ReleaseContract` module: ordered asset schemes, checksum layouts, provenance manifest; updater resolves the live release; User-Agent on every request

## Context
See G4. `src/cli/mod.rs` `ReleaseArtifactContract` (`:230-330`) knows `Tag`/`Latest` locators and one tarball naming; `update.rs:1096-1102` builds download URLs; `update.rs:1178-1185` fetches `releases/latest` JSON with `curl -sL`; `assets.rs` verifies sha256 via `.sha256` sidecars; `mod.rs:640-658` checksum parser takes the first whitespace token.

## Design
- New `src/cli/release_contract.rs` (genuinely new functionality; `mod.rs` shrinks): `ReleaseContract { schemes: Vec<AssetScheme>, checksum_sources: Vec<ChecksumSource>, provenance_name: "release-provenance.json", signature_scheme: Option<...> }`. `AssetScheme::{VersionedTarXz, LegacyTarXz, RawBinary}` each with `name_for(tag, target) -> String`, `archive: Archive::{TarXz, None}`, and `checksum: ChecksumSource::{Sidecar(".sha256"), Aggregate("SHA256SUMS"), Aggregate("SHA256SUMS.txt")}`. Target mapping `Triple <-> {os}_{arch}` (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` <-> `linux_amd64`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` <-> `linux_arm64`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` <-> `darwin_amd64`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` <-> `darwin_arm64`). `contract.resolve(release_assets: &[AssetName], tag, target) -> Resolved { scheme, asset, checksum_source }` picks the first scheme whose asset exists in the release's asset list (from the GitHub API JSON already fetched), instead of guessing a URL.
- Provenance-first: if `release-provenance.json` exists in the release, parse it (`assets[] { name, target, sha256, archive, signature: Option<{ kind: "sigstore"|"codesign"|"notarized", ref } > , built_from: sha }`) and use it as the authoritative map; fall back to scheme probing when absent (v0.5.x). The workflow (G4.2) emits this manifest.
- Checksums: parse sidecar hex, GNU aggregate `hash␠␠name`, BSD `SHA256 (name) = hash`; aggregate lookups match on basename.
- Updater (`update.rs`): use `contract.resolve`; extract tarballs as before; for `RawBinary` install the file directly with mode 0o755; keep backup/rollback flow; `sbh update --check --force --dry-run` reports the resolved asset and its HTTP status without downloading.
- User-Agent: a single `http::fetch(url, opts)` helper in `cli/mod.rs` that adds `-A "OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0"` to every `curl` invocation (updater, assets, install from-source, `doctor --release`); grep-based test forbids raw `curl` `Command::new` outside the helper.
- `sbh release-contract --json` prints the contract (schemes in order, mapping table, checksum sources) for consumption by `scripts/install.sh` generation and CI validation (G4.2).

## Files
`src/cli/release_contract.rs` (new), `src/cli/mod.rs`, `src/cli/update.rs`, `src/cli/assets.rs`, `src/cli/from_source.rs` (UA), `src/cli_app.rs` (`release-contract` subcommand, `update --check --force --dry-run` output), README update section.

## Tests
- Unit: `resolve` over the exact asset lists of v0.4.28 (tarballs + sidecars + provenance), v0.4.40 (mixed, typo asset present), v0.5.1 (raw + SHA256SUMS) fixtures captured from `gh release view --json assets`; all four targets resolve for each; provenance preferred when present.
- Unit: checksum parsers for the three layouts; aggregate basename matching; BSD form.
- Unit: UA helper adds the header; grep test over `src/cli/**` for `Command::new("curl")` outside `http::fetch`.
- Network (opt-in `SBH_NET_TESTS=1`): `sbh update --check --force --dry-run --json` against the live latest release resolves an asset with HTTP 200 for the host target.
- Integration (`tests/installer_e2e.rs`): offline bundle path still works with the new resolver.

## Success criteria
- [ ] Against the v0.5.1 release fixture, resolution yields `sbh_linux_amd64` + `SHA256SUMS`, not a 404 tarball name.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.5.1
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.1, closed as duplicate): resolution order when the API is unreachable — HEAD probes of releases/download/<tag>/<name> in contract order, then the offline manifest; checksum mandatory for both schemes; sigstore Required when a bundle exists. Test matrix for a local fake release server: tarball-only, raw-only, mixed, checksum mismatch (Deny), missing sigstore with Required (Deny), offline manifest. Observed: `sbh update --version v0.5.0 --dry-run` on the operator host resolved sbh-v0.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz (404).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: new module `src/cli/release_contract.rs`, type `ReleaseContract`, re-exported from mod.rs. Fake release server: std `TcpListener` in `tests/common/fake_release.rs` serving the releases API JSON and download paths, with `SBH_RELEASE_API_BASE` override. Raw-mode `SHA256SUMS` fail-closed is part of this bead's contract tests; the skill-asset and Windows decisions move to 5.2.
notes: Additional installer/updater findings (2026-09-02 audit): (1) scripts/install.sh extracts a skill.tar.gz release asset into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills (lines ~655-700); no such asset exists in v0.5.x, so it fails quietly — either publish it from the workflow (G4.2 asset list) or remove the step; (2) scripts/install.ps1 (584 lines) targets *-pc-windows-msvc.zip assets that no release has ever shipped and the Rust contract defines Windows targets (src/cli/mod.rs:768-775) — decision: mark Windows unsupported in docs and gate the script, or add Windows to the release matrix (out of scope unless the operator asks); (3) raw mode in install.sh only warns when SHA256SUMS is missing — must fail closed like the tarball path.
close_reason: Updater asset contract + fake-release e2e landed (78238ec, 5c965d7). Network path proven end to end against a loopback fake release: tarball-only, raw+SHA256SUMS, mixed, legacy, manifest/sidecar mismatch denied with the seeded binary untouched, foreign-only assets named, listed-but-404. install.sh name parity for all 4 CI targets. Base-URL override only under SBH_TEST_MODE=1. Sigstore-Required denial covered at unit level (offline bundle only; network path downloads no bundle). Self-verified on rch (installer_e2e 49/49, lib cli:: 352/352, clippy clean on lib+installer_e2e); no independent verifier.

(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G4.2 - Installers, release workflow, Homebrew formula, and tap consume the ReleaseContract; publish both tarball and raw schemes; asset audit job (absorbs bd-t951)

## Context
See G4. `scripts/install.sh` hand-codes three probe strategies (`:398-535`); root `install.sh` hand-codes one; `release.yml` (596 lines) names assets at `:330-332`, verifies tarball arch (`:341-381`, bd-t951 guard), writes `release-provenance.json` (`:456-464`), and updates the tap (`:476-580`) by grepping `sbh-v${version}-{aarch64,x86_64}-apple-darwin.tar.xz`; `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` has v0.4.8 placeholders; `cert-expiration.yml` exists. CI/release both still run a dead "Strip local-only TUI path deps" `sed` step (`ci.yml:39-43`, `release.yml:82-88`).

## Design
- `scripts/install.sh`: the probe table becomes a generated block between `# BEGIN sbh-release-contract` / `# END` markers, produced by `sbh release-contract --shell` and checked by a static test (`cli/mod.rs` already has installer-contract tests at `:2600-2650`; extend them to compare against the contract). Root `install.sh`: DECISION for the operator: (a) replace with a 5-line shim that `exec`s `scripts/install.sh` fetched from the same ref, or (b) remove. Default action: shim (no deletion).
- `release.yml`: matrix names come from `cargo run -- release-contract --json` (built once in the quality-gate job); publish BOTH `sbh-v{tag}-{triple}.tar.xz` (+ `.sha256`) and `sbh_{os}_{arch}` raw binaries plus one `SHA256SUMS`, plus `release-provenance.json` listing every asset with target, sha256, archive kind, signature/notarization status, and `built_from`. The bd-t951 arch check runs for both schemes. Remove the dead path-dep `sed` step. Add a final `asset-audit` job that downloads the published assets with `gh release download`, recomputes hashes, validates against provenance, and fails the workflow on drift (bd-t951 follow-up items 2-3).
- Homebrew: formula template renders from the contract (URLs for the two darwin tarballs, sha256 from provenance); the tap job pushes only when provenance validates; `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb` keeps placeholder markers but the placeholder version is bumped to the current contract shape and documented as a template in the file header.
- `cert-expiration.yml`: unchanged, but `doctor --release` (G4.3) surfaces its last result.
- CHANGELOG: document the dual scheme and that v0.5.0/v0.5.1 were hand-published.

## Files
`scripts/install.sh`, `install.sh` (shim or decision), `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (dead step), `packaging/homebrew/Formula/sbh.rb`, `src/cli/mod.rs` (installer contract tests), docs/installer-dx-parity-matrix.md.

## Tests
- Static: installer generated block == `sbh release-contract --shell` output (test regenerates and diffs).

# G10.3 - Build metadata: `build.rs` embeds git SHA, target, profile, and a reproducible timestamp so `sbh version --verbose` is never "unknown" in repo builds

## Context
`emit_version` (`cli_app.rs:10076-10085`) reads `option_env!("TARGET")`, `("PROFILE")`, `("VERGEN_GIT_SHA" | "GIT_SHA")`, `("VERGEN_BUILD_TIMESTAMP" | "BUILD_TIMESTAMP")`. Cargo exposes `TARGET`/`PROFILE` only to build scripts, there is no `build.rs`, and `release.yml` exports nothing, so all four are always "unknown". `doctor --release` and bug reports cannot identify the build.

- `emit_version` reads the `SBH_BUILD_*` vars; `--json` shape unchanged (`build.git_sha` etc.); `release.yml` sets `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the tag commit time so artifacts are reproducible; provenance (G4.2) includes the same SHA.
- `rch`: the remote build runs `build.rs` on the synced tree; verify the `.git` dir is synced or set `SBH_GIT_SHA` in the rch profile (document in AGENTS.md).

## Tests
- Unit (`--bin sbh`): `version --json` fields are non-"unknown" when built in the repo (assert on `SBH_BUILD_GIT_SHA` presence at compile time via `option_env!` in the test, so tarball builds skip).
- Reproducibility: two builds with the same `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` produce identical `version --verbose` output (unit test on the formatting function).

## Success criteria
- [ ] `sbh version --verbose` on the next release shows the tag SHA, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `release`, and the tag time.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Env names: `SBH_BUILD_GIT_SHA` / `SBH_BUILD_TIMESTAMP` (the `SBH_BUILD_*` family).

title: W5: systemd correctness (READY=1, watchdog, derived ReadWritePaths, shutdown state, thread health)
description:
# W5 — systemd correctness

## Background
The generated system-scope unit is `Type=notify` with `WatchdogSec=60` (src/daemon/service/systemd.rs:119-127) but the daemon never sends `READY=1` (no occurrence in src/) and `WATCHDOG_USEC` is never read; `ExecStart={binary} daemon` passes no `--watchdog-sec`, so heartbeats are disabled. A system-scope `sbh install --systemd` therefore produces a unit that systemd times out and restarts. `ReadWritePaths` is a hardcoded list (systemd.rs:414-431), not derived from `scanner.root_paths`; under `ProtectSystem=strict` the daemon cannot delete outside /tmp, /var/tmp, /data, /var/lib/sbh and the installer's $HOME dotdirs. `shutdown()` (loop_main.rs:3597-3636) joins workers 5 s each and writes no final state; `ShutdownCoordinator` (signals.rs:157-201) is dead code; thread health never reaches state.json. (closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G3 - systemd lifecycle honesty: READY=1, coordinated shutdown, self-monitor truth, unit drift detection

## Background (2026-09-01 audit)
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs:120-124` emits `Type=notify` + `WatchdogSec=60` for system-scope units; `sd_notify_linux` (`:339-347`) sends only `WATCHDOG=1\nSTATUS=...` over a `UnixDatagram`. There is no `READY=1`, `STOPPING=1`, or `MAINPID=` anywhere (`rg READY=1 src tests` -> 0). With `Type=notify`, systemd keeps the unit in `activating` until READY=1 and kills it at `TimeoutStartSec` (default 90 s), then `Restart=on-failure` loops. No test starts a real unit; the unit on this host is a hand-written `Type=simple` file, which is presumably why nobody noticed.
- Abstract `NOTIFY_SOCKET` paths (`@...`) are not handled; send errors are silently discarded.
- Shutdown (`loop_main.rs:3597-3640`): shutdown flag checked at the top of the loop (no "complete current cycle"), no final `state.json` write, worker join timeout 5 s (`WORKER_SHUTDOWN_JOIN_TIMEOUT`), logger joined unbounded. `ShutdownCoordinator` (`signals.rs:160-195`, 30 s) is dead code with tests. README L1440-1445 describes a different sequence.
- Self-monitor (`self_monitor.rs`): only scanner and executor heartbeat (`loop_main.rs:1767-1768`); `ThreadStatus::Dead` is never produced; stall threshold passed is 10 s (README says 60 s); README says thread statuses are in the state file (they are not; the TUI Diagnostics screen therefore has nothing to show).
- Unit drift: bootstrap only detects a stale `ExecStart` binary; the hardened directives (Nice, IOSchedulingClass, ProtectSystem, MemoryMax, CPUQuota, WatchdogSec) are not verified against the installed unit; operator drop-ins and `Condition*` gates are invisible to `doctor`.

## Goal
A system-scope install starts and stays `active` under systemd's own supervision; shutdown leaves a truthful final state; the self-monitor reports all workers; `doctor` can tell an operator that the installed unit is not the one sbh generates.

## Children
G3.1 sd_notify protocol + unit text; G3.2 shutdown + self-monitor; G3.3 unit drift in doctor; G3.4 tests (fake NOTIFY_SOCKET, opt-in `systemd-run` transient unit, state schema).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- The earlier consolidation note is superseded: the parallel G-tree was merged INTO this tree; every child here is canonical and carries the merged text.

title: Send READY=1 and STOPPING=1, honor WATCHDOG_USEC, add a systemd-run integration test

# G3.1 - sd_notify protocol: READY=1 after startup, STOPPING=1 on shutdown, STATUS= updates, MAINPID, abstract sockets, TimeoutStartSec

## Context
See G3. `systemd.rs:316-347`: `systemd_notify_socket()`, `systemd_watchdog_enabled()`, `sd_notify_watchdog()` -> `sd_notify_linux(status, socket_path)` sends `WATCHDOG=1\nSTATUS={status}\n` via `UnixDatagram::unbound().send_to`. ## Design
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs`: `pub struct SdNotify { socket: Option<UnixDatagram>, target: SocketTarget }` with `SocketTarget::{Path(PathBuf), Abstract(Vec<u8>)}` parsed from `NOTIFY_SOCKET` (`@` prefix -> abstract; use `std::os::linux::net::SocketAddrExt::from_abstract_name`). Methods: `ready()` -> `READY=1\nMAINPID=<pid>\n`, `stopping()` -> `STOPPING=1\n`, `status(&str)`, `watchdog()` -> `WATCHDOG=1\n`, `errno(i32)` on fatal startup errors. First send failure logged once at `[SBH-DAEMON] sd_notify unavailable: <err>`; subsequent failures counted in self-monitor diagnostics.
- `loop_main.rs`: call `ready()` after config load, PAL detection, lock acquisition (G1.3), worker spawn, and the first successful state write; call `status()` with a compact pressure summary every state write; `stopping()` at the start of shutdown.
- Unit text: system scope adds `TimeoutStartSec=30` and keeps `Type=notify`/`WatchdogSec=60`; user scope unchanged (`Type=simple`). `NotifyAccess=main` explicit.

# The sandbox must match the deletion scope

## Design
`SystemdConfig::read_write_paths(&Config)` = root_paths + special locations + every ballast dir (incl. `<mount>/.sbh/ballast`) + data/config dirs + `/var/lib/sbh`; `/proc/sys` never included; rendered with quoting; `sbh install --systemd`, `sbh config set scanner.root_paths ...`, and `sbh bootstrap --apply` (reason `systemd-unit-stale-paths`, new) re-render and `daemon-reload`; a snapshot test for the unit (tests/snapshots has none today).

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

## Design

# G3.2 - Coordinated shutdown with a final state write; self-monitor heartbeats for all workers and a real `Dead` status; thread statuses in state.json

## Context
See G3. `loop_main.rs:3597-3640` `shutdown()`: drops senders, `join_worker_with_timeout(5 s)` per worker, logger joined without bound; no final `state.json`. `signals.rs:160-195` `ShutdownCoordinator` unused. `self_monitor.rs:176-197` `status()` returns Running/Stalled only; heartbeats registered for scanner+executor only (`loop_main.rs:1767-1768`); `THREAD_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10 s` used as the stall threshold; `DaemonState` (`self_monitor.rs:50-61`) has no thread field.

## Design
- Shutdown sequence (documented in README exactly as implemented): (1) set flag + `sd_notify STOPPING=1`; (2) finish the in-flight tick (move the flag check to after the tick's act phase, bounded by the tick's own budget); (3) drop channel senders; (4) join workers with `shutdown_join_budget = min(config.daemon.shutdown_join_secs, TimeoutStopSec - 5)` (default 25 s) split across workers; (5) write final `state.json` with `shutdown_at`, `shutdown_reason`, `clean_exit: true`; (6) release `daemon.lock`; (7) exit 0. `ShutdownCoordinator`: DECISION for the operator: wire it as the implementation of steps 3-4 (preferred; it exists and is tested) or remove it. The bead implements the wiring; removal needs explicit permission.
- Self-monitor: heartbeat handles for monitor, scanner, executor, logger, and the memory-pressure thread; `ThreadStatus::Dead { error }` produced when the supervisor observes a finished join handle that was not respawned (`loop_main.rs:2387-2451` respawn path); stall threshold = `max(3 * tick_interval, 30 s)` documented as a constant `THREAD_STALL_THRESHOLD`.
- `DaemonState` gains `threads: Vec<ThreadHealth { name, status, last_heartbeat_age_ms, restarts }>` (serde default; empty for old daemons) so the TUI Diagnostics screen (G5.4) and `status --json` can show them.

## Files
`src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/daemon/signals.rs`, `src/daemon/self_monitor.rs`, `src/core/config.rs` (`daemon.shutdown_join_secs`), `src/cli_app.rs` (`status` prints thread health), README daemon/self-monitor sections.

## Tests
- Unit: shutdown writes `state.json` with `shutdown_at` and `clean_exit`; lock released after write (probe succeeds).
- Unit: a worker that panics past the respawn limit yields `Dead` with the panic message in the next state write.
- Unit: heartbeat staleness -> `Stalled` at the documented threshold for each of the five workers.
- Unit (`self_monitor.rs`): `DaemonState` JSON with and without `threads` deserializes (schema-default).
- Integration: SIGTERM to a running `sbh daemon` (binary) exits 0 within `shutdown_join_secs + 2`, and the final state has `clean_exit=true`.

## Success criteria
- [ ] README shutdown sequence and thread table are regenerated from constants and match tests.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.4.2
From bd-rc-master-ajg1 (bd-rc-master-ajg1.6.3, closed as duplicate): stall threshold should be the documented 60 s (code passes THREAD_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL = 10 s); the scanner heartbeats only per request so an idle scanner reads Stalled; `ThreadStatus::Dead` only when the respawn budget is exhausted; align the worker join budget with the unit's TimeoutStopSec=30 (or document 5 s); write `stopped_at`/`exit_reason` in the final state. Removing `ShutdownCoordinator` (dead code) requires operator permission per AGENTS.md rule 1; mark `#[deprecated]` until then.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- DECISION: join budget `min(daemon.shutdown_join_secs, TimeoutStopSec - 5)` default 25 s; stall threshold `max(3 x tick, 60 s)` with heartbeats on a timer independent of the tick; wire `ShutdownCoordinator` (already tested; no deletion needed); C-STATE names. Creates the `[daemon]` config section. Owns lifecycle case (d).

title: doctor --service unit drift detection (systemd + launchd) and service reinstall-unit (W5)
description:
# G3.3 - Unit drift detection: `doctor --service` compares the installed systemd unit (and launchd plist) with what sbh generates; `service reinstall-unit` remediation

## Context
On this host `/etc/systemd/system/sbh.service` is a hand-written `Type=simple` unit with none of the documented hardening (no Nice/IOSchedulingClass/ProtectSystem/MemoryMax/WatchdogSec), plus drop-ins (`10-scanner-v2.conf` env, `hotloop-guard.conf` and `zz-hotloop-disabled.conf` Condition gates, `system.control/50-CPUQuota.conf` etc.). `cli/bootstrap.rs:958-978` detects only a stale `ExecStart` binary (`SystemdUnitStaleBinary`). Nothing tells the operator the unit is not sbh's. README L1485-1515 describes the hardened unit as if it were what runs.

## Design
- `daemon/service/systemd.rs`: `UnitDrift::compute(installed_text, generated_text, dropins: &[(path, text)]) -> DriftReport { missing_directives, changed_directives, foreign_dropins, condition_gates, exec_start_matches }` using a simple `[Section] key=value` parser (multi-value keys like `ReadWritePaths` compared as sets).
- `doctor --service` (new flag; `--pal` on macOS does the plist equivalent via `launchd.rs`): PASS when no drift; WARN for foreign drop-ins that only add limits; FAIL for missing hardening directives, a different `Type=`, or a Condition gate currently disabling the unit. Remediation text: `sudo sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit` and, for gates, the exact path.
- `sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit [--keep-dropins]`: backs up the installed unit (`.bak-<stamp>` like the writeback snippet), writes the generated one, `daemon-reload`, prints the diff; never touches drop-ins unless `--purge-dropins` (explicit).
- Bootstrap (G6.1) gains `MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift` reusing `UnitDrift`.

## Files
`src/daemon/service/systemd.rs`, `src/daemon/service/launchd.rs` (plist compare), `src/cli_app.rs` (doctor/service), `src/cli/bootstrap.rs`, README doctor/service sections.

## Tests
- Unit: drift on fixtures (this host's unit + drop-ins captured as test data) reports the exact missing directives and both Condition gates; identical text -> no drift; set semantics for `ReadWritePaths`.
- Unit: `reinstall-unit` on a temp unit dir writes backup + new unit and preserves drop-ins.
- Integration: `sbh doctor --service --json` against a fixture unit dir (`SBH_SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR` override for tests) FAILs with the expected ids.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh doctor --service` FAILs today (hand-written unit + gate) and PASSes after G0 step 3.

- `daemon/service/systemd.rs`: `UnitDrift::compute(installed_text, generated_text, dropins: &[(path, text)]) -> DriftReport { missing_directives, changed_directives, foreign_dropins, condition_gates, exec_start_matches }` using a simple `[Section] key=value` parser (multi-value keys like `ReadWritePaths` compared as sets).
- `doctor --service` (new flag; `--pal` on macOS does the plist equivalent via `launchd.rs`): PASS when no drift; WARN for foreign drop-ins that only add limits; FAIL for missing hardening directives, a different `Type=`, or a Condition gate currently disabling the unit. Remediation text: `sudo sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit` and, for gates, the exact path.
- `sbh service --systemd reinstall-unit [--keep-dropins]`: backs up the installed unit (`.bak-<stamp>` like the writeback snippet), writes the generated one, `daemon-reload`, prints the diff; never touches drop-ins unless `--purge-dropins` (explicit).
- Bootstrap (G6.1) gains `MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift` reusing `UnitDrift`.

## Files
`src/daemon/service/systemd.rs`, `src/daemon/service/launchd.rs` (plist compare), `src/cli_app.rs` (doctor/service), `src/cli/bootstrap.rs`, README doctor/service sections.

- Unit: drift on fixtures (this host's unit + drop-ins captured as test data) reports the exact missing directives and both Condition gates; identical text -> no drift; set semantics for `ReadWritePaths`.
- Unit: `reinstall-unit` on a temp unit dir writes backup + new unit and preserves drop-ins.
- Integration: `sbh doctor --service --json` against a fixture unit dir (`SBH_SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR` override for tests) FAILs with the expected ids.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh doctor --service` FAILs today (hand-written unit + gate) and PASSes after G0 step 3.

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Logging addendum (OliveIbis): doctor --service prints each missing/changed directive and each foreign drop-in with its path; reinstall-unit logs the backup path and the diff; a '[SBH-SERVICE] unit drift detected: missing=[..] foreign_dropins=[..] gates=[..]' line at daemon startup (read-only) so journal readers see it without running doctor.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W0-W5 pass)
- Blocked by 4.6 (`MigrationReason::SystemdUnitDrift`).
close_reason: 62de9a2: UnitDrift::compute (section/key parser, drop-ins in order, set-valued ReadWritePaths, 10%==10.00%, condition gates evaluated for path conditions, exec binary match) + severity; SystemdConfig::dropin_dirs/read_dropins; SBH_SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR under SBH_TEST_MODE; doctor --service [--user] with six checks (present/hardening/execstart/gates/dropins/other) + launchd plist diff; service --systemd reinstall-unit [--purge-dropins] (backup beside unit, daemon-reload, drop-ins kept or moved into the backup dir, never deleted); bootstrap SystemdUnitDrift reason + ReinstallServiceUnit action. Tests: this host's unit + drop-ins as fixtures (exact gaps, both gate states), parser, set semantics, WARN/FAIL classes; integration test drives doctor → reinstall → purge to all-PASS. title: W6: Logging and stats integrity (ballast/policy events, degradation constants, C-EVENT schema)
description:
# W6 — Logging and stats integrity

## Background
No production code emits `BallastProvisioned/Released/Replenished` events or calls `upsert_ballast`; there is no `PolicyTransition` event or table; so `sbh stats` ballast figures are always zero and README's "ballast operations and policy transitions stored in SQLite" is untrue. SQLite trips after 3 failures (src/logger/dual.rs:305), not 50 (50 is the reopen interval); the daemon configures JSONL at 50 MiB / 30 s fsync with `fallback_path: None` (loop_main.rs:1675-1684) while README says 100 MiB / 10 s / /dev/shm fallback; every open runs `VACUUM` when auto_vacuum differs; `stats.avg_age_hours` is hard-coded 0.0.

## Children
W6.1 events + inventory + stats from real rows (C-EVENT) · W6.2 degradation constants unified and tested.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- W13 now depends on W6 (v0.6.0 gate). The dead `related` edge to closed bd-2f8 was removed; 7.4 carries that promise.

title: Emit ballast and policy-transition events, upsert ballast inventory, implement the C-EVENT schema, stats from real rows
description:
# Log what the daemon does

title: Prometheus textfile export: <data_dir>/metrics.prom written with every state write (W6)
description:
# G10.7 - Prometheus textfile export: `<data_dir>/metrics.prom` written with every state write

## Why (ambition round 1)
Fleets already run node_exporter; its textfile collector reads `*.prom` files from a directory. Zero network surface, zero dependencies, and the operator gets graphs for exactly the questions this reality check had to answer by hand (is the daemon alive, is there a reserve, how much CPU, what did it decide).

## Design
- On every `maybe_write_state` (30 s), render atomically (tmp + rename, 0o644 so the collector can read it; path configurable `paths.metrics_file`, default `<data_dir>/metrics.prom`; `telemetry.metrics_enabled` default true):
  - `sbh_up 1`, `sbh_info{version,git_sha,policy_mode} 1`, `sbh_daemon_uptime_seconds`, `sbh_daemon_cpu_seconds_total`, `sbh_daemon_rss_bytes`, `sbh_daemon_cpu_budget_deficit_seconds` (G1.7)
  - per mount: `sbh_mount_free_bytes{mount}`, `sbh_mount_free_ratio`, `sbh_mount_pressure_level{mount,level}` (one-hot), `sbh_mount_fill_rate_bytes_per_second`, `sbh_mount_tte_seconds` and `sbh_mount_tte_lo_seconds` (G15), `sbh_mount_reclaim_capability{mount,capability}`
  - ballast: `sbh_ballast_present_bytes{mount}`, `sbh_ballast_target_bytes`, `sbh_ballast_horizon_seconds`, `sbh_ballast_releases_total`
  - scanner: `sbh_scans_total{engine,reason}`, `sbh_scan_cpu_seconds_total`, `sbh_scan_entries_total`, `sbh_deletions_total{result}`, `sbh_bytes_freed_total`, `sbh_quarantine_bytes` (G14)
  - decisions: `sbh_decisions_total{action}` (G2), `sbh_guard_e_value`, `sbh_forecast_coverage_empirical` (G15), `sbh_policy_transitions_total{to,reason}`
  - logger: `sbh_log_events_dropped_total`
- Emergency mode never writes it (zero-write). A `sbh metrics` subcommand prints the same text from the state file for hosts without the collector (and for tests).

## Files
`src/daemon/self_monitor.rs` (render), `src/daemon/loop_main.rs`, `src/cli_app.rs` (`metrics`), `src/core/config.rs`, README "Observability" (new subsection), docs/testing-and-logging.md.

## Tests
- Unit: renderer output validates against the Prometheus text exposition rules (a small in-repo validator: metric name regex, label escaping, one HELP/TYPE per family); snapshot.
- Integration: after a daemon run the file exists, is atomic (no partial reads under a concurrent reader loop), and counters are monotonic across writes.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep sbh_` on a fleet host shows the family after enabling the collector.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- DECISION: the daemon renders metrics.prom from in-process counters; `sbh metrics` cats the file (no C-STATE churn). Mandatory core set: up/info/uptime/cpu/rss, per-mount free/level/rate, ballast present/target, deletions/bytes_freed; the rest (scans by engine/reason, scan CPU, dropped log events, guard e-value, quarantine, forecast coverage) land when their source beads (2.11, 2.13, 2.14, 3.1) do.
- Tests: `telemetry.metrics_enabled=false` -> no file written and no stale file left; zero-write rule: file mtime unchanged during emergency (W10 red-ballast/emergency).
- Scheduling: v0.6.x, not a v0.6.0 gate.

title: Startup and doctor check: activity DB/JSONL/state must not live on a monitored filesystem (bd-2f8 promise)
description:
# Startup check: the activity database and JSONL must not live on a monitored/pressured filesystem (bd-2f8 promise, never implemented)

## Background
Project memory and the bd-2f8 design note promised "startup check that SQLite db is NOT on a monitored filesystem" because a full disk breaks the logger exactly when it matters (the August logs show the daemon on a Red /data with 0/844 successful deletions; had the DB been on /data it would have been unwritable too). No such check exists: grep for `st_dev`/`MetadataExt`/"monitored filesystem" in src/daemon, src/core, src/logger, src/cli_app.rs finds only service-file checks; the daemon opens `config.paths.sqlite_db` unconditionally (src/daemon/loop_main.rs:1675-1676).

## Design
- At daemon startup and in `sbh doctor --system`: resolve the device id of `paths.sqlite_db`, `paths.jsonl_log`, `paths.state_file`; compare with the device ids of every `scanner.root_paths` entry, every special location, and every ballast pool mount. If the log/state device is also a reclaim target, emit a WARN (`logging.on_monitored_fs`) with the remediation "move [paths] to a volume sbh does not reclaim, or accept degraded logging"; if that device is currently at Orange or worse, escalate to FAIL and enable the RAM/JSONL fallback (W6.2) immediately.
- state.json carries `logging: { device, on_monitored_fs: bool }`; `sbh status` prints a one-line warning.
- Not a hard refusal (single-volume hosts are common), but the daemon must keep writing state to the RAM fallback path when the primary is on a Red volume.

## Tests
- Unit: device-id comparison over a MockPlatform with two mounts; single-volume host yields WARN not FAIL.
- Integration: daemon with DB on the injected-Orange mount (W10 injection) -> FAIL check in doctor, fallback enabled, state still written.

## Context
Reality check 2026-09-02 (W6 logging integrity).

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- Blocked by 7.2 (fallback), 2.8 (`logging` block in state.json v2), 2.5 (`BallastCoordinator::discover` for pool mounts); related 11.1 (injection).
- DECISION: no second state path. state.json is preallocated at a fixed size and rewritten in place (no new blocks on a full disk) so DaemonProbe/status readers keep one path.
- Logging: one `[SBH-DAEMON] logging.on_monitored_fs=true device=.. level=..` line at startup and per level change (never per tick); doctor JSON snapshot for the new check.

- v1 remains in the tree as the opt-out path; the design doc planned to remove it after promotion.

title: Index replay re-scores each persisted candidate with fresh vetoes and generation checks before dispatch
description:

title: Move the bounded stowaway sacred scan into DeletionExecutor::preflight_check
description:
# Every route to the executor gets the same sacred check

## Design
`preflight_check` step 6 (README numbering) performs `scan_stowaways_bounded` (depth 3, existing caps, per-batch cache); CLI `clean`/`emergency` no longer depend on score-time checks alone; fail-closed on truncation as today.

## Acceptance
Existing protection tests pass; new executor test: candidate with a `.beads/` three levels down is skipped with `SacredStowaway`.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

- DECISION: the executor position wins (only route shared by daemon, clean, emergency); 12.1 documents the pre-flight order with the stowaway step.
- Tests: 50 candidates under one ancestor -> stowaway walk count == 1 (per-batch cache counter); entry-cap hit -> `SacredStowaway`/truncated skip, never delete; `preflight.stowaway_ms` logged in `artifact_delete`.
close_reason: Implemented in bdd93d6 by the implementing agent; not independently verified. DeletionExecutor::preflight_check step 6c runs find_sacred_overlaps_with_config (depth 3, existing entry/dir caps, stop-after-first) against DeletionConfig.sacred_paths (default cross-platform catalog; daemon passes platform catalog + protected_paths; clean/emergency pass their active catalog); refusal = SkipReason::SacredStowaway; truncation and read errors fail closed. Per-batch reuse of matched sacred paths (nested candidates: 1 walk). Cost visible as DeletionReport.sacred_scans/sacred_scan_ms and in the daemon batch summary line. Tests (5, pass): .beads three levels down refused; nested reuse walk count 1; exhausted walk fails closed; protected_paths glob refused at executor; clean target still deleted. title: Fix and un-ignore the path-traversal regression (core::paths lexical .. escape across a missing root); give the three placeholder test files real tests (W7)
description:
# G7.4 - Placeholder test files get real tests; the ignored path-traversal regression is fixed and un-ignored

## Context
- `tests/repro_issue.rs`: `//! Reproduction test for issue verification (placeholder).` (1 line). `git log --follow` should reveal which issue it was created for; recreate that regression or, if the case now lives elsewhere, DECISION: operator approves deletion, otherwise the file gets the pointer test.
- `tests/repro_glob.rs`: 3 lines, "File cleared to avoid compilation errors due to broken shell environment. The relevant test case has been moved to src/scanner/patterns.rs." Same treatment (verify the moved test exists by name; add a cross-reference test or delete with permission).
- `tests/repro_tui_panic.rs`: asserts that slicing `"aé"` at byte 1 panics; imports nothing from sbh. The original bug was a `truncate_path`-style helper; find it (`rg -n "fn truncate_path|char boundary" src/`) and test the real helper with multi-byte input instead.
- `tests/regression_path_traversal.rs:9`: `#[ignore = "documents current behavior; enable once path-resolution contract is hardened"]`; `core::paths::resolve_absolute_path` lexically collapses `..` across a nonexistent root so `/nonexistent_root/../etc/passwd` resolves to `/etc/passwd`. `resolve_absolute_path` is used for config normalization and (post scanner-v2) not on hot paths.

## Design
- `core/paths.rs`: `resolve_absolute_path` returns `Err(SbhError::InvalidPath)` when any component that must be traversed does not exist, and never collapses `..` past a missing component; callers that accept not-yet-existing paths (lease targets, ballast dirs) use a new `normalize_lexically_within(base, path)` that refuses escapes from `base`. Un-ignore the regression and flip its assertion.
- Replace the three placeholder files with the real tests described above; document in docs/testing-and-logging.md.

## Tests
- `tests/regression_path_traversal.rs` (un-ignored): nonexistent root -> error; existing root with `..` inside -> resolved; symlink-loop -> bounded error.
- Unit for `normalize_lexically_within` escape refusal (`../../etc`).
- The two repro files exercise real sbh code paths.

## Success criteria
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` reports 0 ignored on Linux.

- Scope: 8.6 owns core::paths and the four placeholder test files; 11.4 keeps only the root-skip helper and a root CI job (its duplicate paragraphs are void).
- DECISION per call site of `resolve_absolute_path`: `src/monitor/fs_stats.rs:42,57` -> nearest existing ancestor; `src/core/config.rs:617` (source-tree veto comparison) -> a resolution error counts as "is source tree" (fail closed); unit tests for both.

title: W8: Ballast integrity (locking, read-only status, per-mount enumeration, APFS parity, cooldown reset, snapshot accounting)
description:
# W8 — Ballast integrity

## Background
`verify()` (src/ballast/manager.rs:524-552) and `prune_orphans()` (called from the constructor and `update_config`) run without the flock; `sbh ballast status` constructs `BallastManager::new`, which `create_dir_all`s and deletes ballast files with index > file_count — a read-only command that mutates; CLI commands only see `[paths] ballast_dir` while the daemon provisions `<mount>/.sbh/ballast` per mount; APFS is not in `FALLOCATE_FRIENDLY` so the daemon writes N GiB of random data on macOS while the CLI preallocates; the release controller's interruption/cooldown reset is only reachable in the Green arm.

## Children
W8.1 locking + read-only status + enumeration · W8.2 APFS parity + snapshot-aware release effectiveness (Q10) · W8.3 cooldown reset every tick.

## Context (self-contained; see also docs/internal/reality-check-and-bridge-plan-2026-09-02.md)

Reality check 2026-09-02 (HEAD 320d04d, v0.5.1): the code base is large and real (133k lines, 2,833 tests, 0 failures) but the shipped product does not deliver the README vision. On the operator's own workstation the daemon is disabled by a hand-made kill switch (/etc/sbh/HOTLOOP_DISABLED) because it spun at its CPU quota while unable to act: `/` at 12% free (Orange) has no ballast pool (20% provisioning floor) and no configured root_path, so every tick logs "cannot reclaim, backing off". Across June-August the daemon attempted 22,652 deletions and succeeded 7,065 times (31%); in August it went 0 for 844. With normal memory pressure the default behavior matrix (src/daemon/policy.rs DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CELLS) makes Yellow and Orange identify-only with no ballast release, so nothing is reclaimed until Red. Green never scans unless the predictive policy fires. Several README commands (`sbh explain`, `sbh bootstrap`, `sbh uninstall --dry-run`, the TUI dashboard in shipped binaries) do not exist for users. The updater builds asset names (`sbh-v<tag>-<triple>.tar.xz`) that the hand-published v0.5.x releases do not contain, all GitHub workflows are disabled, CI has been red at the clippy gate since 2026-08-14, and clippy fails locally with 62 errors.

title: Hold the flock for verify and prune; make ballast status read-only; enumerate per-mount pools in the CLI
description:
# `sbh ballast status` must be read-only; prune only from provision/replenish

Locking of verify() is owned by bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.5; per-mount enumeration in status by bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.4 and bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.5.

## Problem
`run_ballast status` constructs `BallastManager::new`, which `create_dir_all`s the pool dir and calls `prune_orphans()` (src/ballast/manager.rs:299-311), deleting any `SBH_BALLAST_FILE_N.dat` with N > file_count — a read-only command that mutates the pool, unlocked.

## Design
`BallastManager::open_read_only(dir)` for status/verify paths (no create, no prune); `prune_orphans()` runs only inside `provision()`/`replenish_one()` under the flock; constructor no longer prunes; document `<mount>/.sbh/ballast` pools in README.

## Tests
`ballast status` on a pool with an orphan leaves it in place and reports it as `orphan`; provision under the lock prunes it; concurrency test: status during provision observes either the old or the new inventory, never a half-written file.

---
## Merged from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.4 — G10.4: ballast status shows every coordinator volume pool; state.json missing vs released semantics; explicit health reasons
(closed 2026-09-02 by the parallel reality-check session; canonical home is this bead. Files/Tests/Success-criteria below are part of this bead's contract.)

# G10.4 - `ballast status` shows every volume pool from the coordinator; `state.json` distinguishes missing from released; health reasons are explicit

## Context
See G10. `run_ballast` status path (`cli_app.rs:4292-4420`) builds `BallastManager` for the configured dir only; the daemon uses `BallastCoordinator` (`ballast/coordinator.rs:179-308`) to create per-mount pools (`/data/.sbh/ballast` on this host). `state.json` `ballast: { available, total, released }` is computed as `total - available` and labels missing files as released.

## Design
- `ballast status [--json]`: iterate the coordinator's `pools_for_config()` (same derivation the daemon uses, including skip reasons for RAM/network/read-only/override-disabled mounts) and print one section per volume: mount, pool dir, configured count/size, present, releasable bytes, health, `floor_pct` and `skipped_for_floor` (G1.1), last provision/release timestamps from the header/inventory. `--json` gains `volumes: [...]` and keeps the top-level fields for the primary pool for compatibility (schema version bump shared with G10.2).
- `state.json`: `ballast: { configured, present, missing, released_this_epoch, per_volume: [...] }`; `released_this_epoch` counted by the release controller and reset on Green. Old readers ignore new fields (`serde(default)`); the TUI adapter and `status` use the new ones when present.
- Health reason strings (`Unconfigured`, `Empty`, `Partial{floor}`, `Indeterminate{unreadable}`) shared by `status`, `doctor`, and the TUI.

## Files
`src/cli_app.rs`, `src/ballast/{coordinator,manager,release}.rs`, `src/daemon/self_monitor.rs`, `src/tui/adapters.rs`, README ballast section.

## Tests
- Unit: coordinator pool enumeration on a mock PAL with three mounts (one skipped) -> `ballast status --json volumes[]` shape (snapshot).
- Unit (`release.rs`): `released_this_epoch` increments on release and resets on Green.
- Integration: this-host-like fixture (configured dir empty, second pool populated) shows both.

## Success criteria
- [ ] On this host `sudo sbh ballast status` lists `/` (empty, floor-limited) and `/data` (5 files) instead of only `/`.

### Notes carried from bd-rc-bridge-2026-09-btcx.11.4
Related from bd-rc-master-ajg1: bd-rc-master-ajg1.2.5 (shared BallastCoordinator::discover for CLI and daemon + Q1 reserve target) and bd-rc-master-ajg1.9.1 (ballast status must be read-only: today `BallastManager::new` prunes orphan files from a status command).

## Refinement (folded 2026-09-02 from review comments)
- Verification addendum (OliveIbis): (a) unit: verify() and prune_orphans() contend with provision() on the flock (thread test with a barrier); (b) unit: 'ballast status' opens the pool read-only and never creates the directory or lock file (assert directory absent after status on a fresh config); (c) unit: per-mount enumeration on a mock PAL with three mounts (one skipped as tmpfs/network/ro) matches the coordinator's discover() output; snapshot of the volumes[] JSON; (d) integration: fixture like threadripperje (configured dir empty, second pool on another mount populated) lists both with health full|partial|empty|unconfigured-for-space; (e) logging: skip reasons per mount at -v.

## Review fixes (2026-09-02, W6-W13 pass)
- Corrections: the verify()/prune flock and the fallocate probe are owned HERE (4.4's merged G10.5 text is void for those); the install floor callback is owned by 2.5.
- DECISION: C-STATE (2.8) wins: ballast lives per mount under `mounts[].ballast {dir, configured, present, missing, released_since_green, health, releasable_bytes, release_efficiency}`; no top-level ballast block; blocked by 2.8; related 4.14. `released_since_green` is owned by 9.3's per-mount controller; 9.1 reads it.
- Tests: status on a missing dir -> `Unconfigured`, dir still absent; thread test: provision holds the lock while verify runs -> verify sees only complete files.
close_reason: Shipped on main (fix(ballast) commit): opening a BallastManager never creates the dir nor prunes (mutating paths create+lock+prune; config reload no longer prunes unlocked); verify holds the flock; orphans()/orphan_ballast_files report leftovers; coordinator plan_pools + inventory_for_config observe every daemon volume read-only; ballast status prints orphans + volumes (JSON orphans/volumes); ballast_discovery_paths shared with the CLI; README updated. Proof: manager tests (open creates nothing/prunes nothing, verify never prunes, provision prunes under the lock, reduced file_count leaves orphans until provision), coordinator read-only enumeration test (orphan reported, disabled volume skipped with reason, no dirs created; discovery agrees), integration test (status on an absent pool creates nothing; an orphan survives and is reported; volumes lists the configured pool; human output); full suites green on rch hz3. Self-verified by OliveIbis, not independently verified. Not done: state.json ballast block redesign (per_volume/released_this_epoch) + TUI adapter; status-during-provision concurrency test.

title: APFS preallocation parity between daemon and CLI; snapshot-aware release effectiveness (Q10)
description:

## Acceptance
Unit: with eta 0.25 the controller requests 4x files capped; macOS lane test for preallocation path selection.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
ENHANCEMENT (idea-wizard): Centralize filesystem type detection and strategy selection. Currently ad-hoc across beads (bd-25g uses fs_type for fallocate, bd-1w9 has cross-device checks). Add to Platform trait:
  fn fs_strategy(&self, path: &Path) -> FsStrategy
Where FsStrategy encodes:
  - ballast_method: Fallocate | RandomData | Skip (for tmpfs/NFS)
  - deletion_method: Standard | CowAware (btrfs/zfs may not free space immediately)
  - scan_strategy: Full | ReadOnly | Skip (NFS mounts: read-only scanning, skip deletion, warn user)

This prevents each bead from independently querying fs_type.

title: Release-asset audit: catch label/content drift before shipping
description:
## Context

v0.4.23 shipped with the macOS aarch64 binary packaged inside `sbh-v0.4.23-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz`. Every Linux fleet self-update failed with `Exec format error (os error 8)` and the daemons stayed pinned at v0.4.22.

## Root cause

- v0.4.23 CI release run (id 25841144289) was cancelled mid-flight.
- Somebody hand-uploaded artifacts to the GitHub Release.
- The bare `sbh` asset (3.7 MB) was the macOS arm64 binary.
- The same wrong binary was repackaged into the linux x86_64 tarball.
- A legacy-name mirror was uploaded with a stray "v" (`sbh-vx86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz`).
- release.yml had no guardrail to catch label/content drift before publish.

## What was done

- Deleted the 8 broken assets from the v0.4.23 release.
- Re-ran the v0.4.23 CI workflow (run 25841144289) to rebuild artifacts via the proven pipeline.
- Added a "Verify tarball binary matches matrix target" step to release.yml (commit b15e1e0).

## Follow-up

- After CI completes, run sbh update --refresh-cache across the 14-machine fleet.
- Consider adding the validator to the legacy-mirror step too.
- Consider an end-of-workflow audit that downloads the published GitHub release assets and re-runs the same file check.
- Decide whether to keep allowing manual uploads to releases.

## Why P2

The shipping pipeline silently corrupted a fleet-wide self-update. Worst-class CI defect but not P1 since it didn't cause data loss or security incident.
close_reason: Absorbed by bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.2 (release workflow: both asset layouts + post-publish asset audit job) and bd-rc-master-ajg1.5.3 (sbh doctor --release --assets audit + manual release parity); the v0.4.23 mislabeled-tarball guard is the negative test there.

title: Multi-volume ballast pool coordinator
description:
## Deliverable
Support ballast files distributed across multiple volumes so each monitored filesystem has its own relief pool. Fixes the fundamental gap where ballast on /var can't help /data.

## The Problem
The current design has a single ballast.location. On machines with multiple data volumes (/data, /scratch, /home), ballast on /var/lib/sbh/ballast can only relieve pressure on the root filesystem. If /data fills up, deleting ballast on /var does nothing. This breaks the ballast feature for the most common production setup.

## The Solution: Per-Volume Ballast Pools

### Architecture
Each monitored filesystem gets its own ballast pool:
- /data has ballast at /data/.sbh/ballast/
- /scratch has ballast at /scratch/.sbh/ballast/
- /home has ballast at /home/.sbh/ballast/
- Root filesystem uses /var/lib/sbh/ballast/ (default)

### Configuration
```toml
[ballast]
auto_provision = true           # Auto-create pools on each monitored mount
per_volume_file_count = 5       # Default files per volume
per_volume_file_size_mb = 1024  # Default size per file

# Override for specific mounts
[ballast.overrides."/data"]
file_count = 10
file_size_mb = 2048             # /data is large, bigger ballast

[ballast.overrides."/scratch"]
file_count = 3
file_size_mb = 512              # /scratch is small

[ballast.overrides."/tmp"]
enabled = false                 # Never ballast tmpfs (defeats purpose)
```

### BallastPoolCoordinator
```rust
pub struct BallastPoolCoordinator {
    pools: HashMap<MountPoint, BallastPool>,
}

pub struct BallastPool {
    mount_point: PathBuf,
    ballast_dir: PathBuf,          // e.g., /data/.sbh/ballast/
    manager: BallastManager,       // existing manager, per-pool instance
    fs_type: String,               // ext4, xfs, btrfs, etc.
}

impl BallastPoolCoordinator {
    /// Provision all pools (auto-detect from watched_paths + overrides)
    pub fn provision_all(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<ProvisionReport>, SbhError>;
    
    /// Release ballast for a SPECIFIC filesystem under pressure
    pub fn release_for_mount(&mut self, mount: &Path, count: usize) -> Result<ReleaseReport, SbhError>;
    
    /// Replenish a specific pool when its filesystem recovers
    pub fn replenish_for_mount(&mut self, mount: &Path) -> Result<ProvisionReport, SbhError>;
    
    /// Get inventory across all pools
    pub fn inventory(&self) -> Vec<PoolInventory>;
    
    /// Total releasable bytes across all pools
    pub fn total_releasable(&self) -> u64;
}
```

### Auto-Detection Logic
On startup:
1. Enumerate all mount points from scanner.watched_paths
2. Resolve each path to its mount point (e.g., /data/projects -> /data)
3. Deduplicate by mount point
4. For each unique mount: check if ballast pool exists, provision if needed
5. Apply overrides from config
6. Skip tmpfs/ramfs mounts (ballast on RAM defeats the purpose)
7. Skip read-only mounts

### Filesystem Type Awareness
Different provisioning strategies per filesystem type:
- ext4/xfs: use fallocate() for instant provisioning
- btrfs/zfs: write random data (CoW prevents fallocate from reserving actual blocks)
- tmpfs: skip entirely (warn in logs)
- NFS: skip by default (warn: network ballast is unreliable)

### Integration with Pressure Response
When PID controller says ReleaseBallast for mount /data:
1. Coordinator routes to /data's pool
2. Releases N files from that specific pool
3. Verifies space freed on /data (not on /var or anywhere else)
4. If /data has no pool (e.g., not provisioned), log warning and skip to artifact scanning

### sbh ballast status (enhanced)
```
Volume    │ Pool Location           │ Files │ Available │ Reclaimable
/data     │ /data/.sbh/ballast      │ 10/10 │ 10        │ 20.0 GB
/scratch  │ /scratch/.sbh/ballast   │ 3/3   │ 3         │ 1.5 GB
/         │ /var/lib/sbh/ballast    │ 5/5   │ 5         │ 5.0 GB
/tmp      │ (skipped: tmpfs)        │  -    │ -         │ -
Total:    │                         │ 18/18 │ 18        │ 26.5 GB
```

## Design Rationale
This is a genuine architectural gap. The single-volume ballast breaks on the most common production setup (separate data and system volumes). Agent swarms often use machines with /data on a large partition and / on a smaller root — ballast on root can't help when /data fills up. Implementation extends BallastManager from a single inventory to a HashMap<MountPoint, BallastPool> — significant but well-contained.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each monitored filesystem gets its own ballast pool
- Auto-detection correctly identifies mount points from watched_paths
- Per-volume overrides work correctly
- Filesystem type detection selects correct provisioning strategy
- tmpfs and NFS mounts are skipped with warnings
- Release targets the correct volume's pool
- sbh ballast status shows per-volume inventory
- Provisioning respects per-volume free space (don't provision if < 20% free)
- Unit tests: pool coordination, mount point resolution, override merging
- Integration test: two mock volumes -> provision both -> release on specific volume -> verify
- Test: volume with no pool -> graceful fallback to artifact scanning
close_reason: Implemented BallastPoolCoordinator with per-volume pool management, auto-detection, config overrides, targeted release, and 12 comprehensive tests. All 36 ballast tests pass.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: MINOR: Ballast file index design — each BallastPool (per-filesystem) maintains its OWN index of ballast files (Vec<BallastFile>). The BallastPoolCoordinator holds a HashMap<PathBuf, BallastPool> keyed by mount point. There is NO global ballast file index. This keeps pools independent and avoids cross-pool coordination complexity.

title: [macOS E7] Self-monitoring (don't be the problem; respect Energy Impact)
description:
# Epic 7: Self-monitoring on macOS (don't be the problem)

## Why this matters

A disk-pressure helper that itself uses 2% CPU continuously, balloons to 800 MB RSS, and shows up red in Activity Monitor's Energy Impact column will rightly be uninstalled. `src/daemon/self_monitor.rs` (37 KB) tracks own resource use and self-throttles. On Linux it reads `/proc/self/status`. On Mac it needs Mach calls.

## Mac self-monitoring APIs

1. **`mach_task_self()` + `task_info(TASK_BASIC_INFO_64, ...)`** → resident_size (RSS), virtual_size, etc.
2. **`task_info(TASK_THREAD_TIMES_INFO, ...)`** → user_time, system_time across all threads.
3. **`proc_pid_rusage(getpid(), RUSAGE_INFO_V4, ...)`** → I/O totals, idle wakeups (`ri_pkg_idle_wkups`, `ri_interrupt_wkups`). Critical for Energy Impact awareness.
4. **`thread_info`** for per-thread CPU.

## Energy Impact considerations

macOS calculates Energy Impact from: CPU time, idle wakeups, GPU use, network I/O, location use. Background daemons should:
- Use NSURLSession for any network (we have none, so OK).
- Avoid timers under 30s when possible. Our daemon polls every 15s default — borderline. Document tradeoff.
- Use `dispatch_source` instead of polling timers where possible.
- Set `ProcessType=Background` in plist (handles I/O priority + scheduling).
- Mark with `LowPriorityIO=true` in plist.

## Required sbh behavior

- Daemon tracks its own RSS, CPU, idle wakeups continuously.
- If RSS exceeds threshold (default 100 MB), log warning + run smaller scan windows.
- If RSS exceeds hard cap (default 500 MB), self-restart via `launchctl kickstart` (controlled crash).
- Per-tick budget: each daemon tick must complete in < 200 ms. If consistently over, increase tick interval.
- `sbh status` reports own RSS, CPU%, idle_wakeups/sec, last_tick_duration_ms.

## Tasks (see child beads)

1. Mach FFI bindings: `mach_task_self`, `task_info` with `TASK_BASIC_INFO_64`, `TASK_THREAD_TIMES_INFO`, `THREAD_BASIC_INFO`.
2. `SelfStats` struct cross-platform: `rss_bytes`, `vm_bytes`, `cpu_user_us`, `cpu_system_us`, `idle_wakeups`, `bytes_read`, `bytes_written`.
3. Wire to existing daemon self-monitor loop: replace `/proc/self/*` with PAL call.
4. Add `ProcessType=Background` and `LowPriorityIO=true` to launchd plist (linked from E5 plist generation).
5. Energy Impact CI test: run daemon for 60 seconds, capture `taskinfo`, assert idle_wakeups < 100/sec, RSS < 50 MB at idle.
6. Self-restart on RSS exceeded: implement controlled crash → exit nonzero → launchd restarts.
7. Self-throttle: under sustained pressure, increase tick interval from 15s → 30s → 60s adaptively.

## Why this matters specifically for Mac

The operator runs many Electron apps + agents. Activity Monitor is a daily ritual. If sbh shows up red, the operator (and other Mac users) will kill or disable it. We have one shot to be invisible. Linux operators tolerate higher daemon overhead because they're usually on servers; Mac users are on laptops with battery anxiety.

## Failure modes

- RSS measurement off by 10x because we confused units (Mach uses bytes, /proc uses kB-as-strings). Always normalize to bytes internally.
- Self-restart loop: RSS exceeded → exit → launchd restarts → RSS exceeded → ... Mitigation: ThrottleInterval=60 in plist, exponential backoff after 3 restarts.
- Idle wakeups inflated by polling timer at 1s interval → energy red. Use 15s minimum, dispatch_source for events.

title: EWMA disk usage rate estimator
description:
## Deliverable
Exponentially Weighted Moving Average estimator that tracks the RATE of disk consumption, enabling predictive intervention before storage actually runs out.

## Technical Approach
### Theory (Alien Graveyard: EWMA from time-series analysis)
EWMA smooths noisy measurements while giving more weight to recent observations:
  EWMA_t = α × x_t + (1 - α) × EWMA_{t-1}
where α ∈ (0, 1) is the smoothing factor (higher = more reactive).

For sbh, we track:
- bytes_consumed_per_second: how fast disk is being consumed
- time_to_exhaustion: estimated seconds until disk is full at current rate
- acceleration: is the consumption rate itself increasing? (second derivative)

### Implementation
```rust
pub struct DiskRateEstimator {
    alpha: f64,                     // smoothing factor (default 0.3)
    ewma_bytes_per_sec: f64,        // smoothed consumption rate
    ewma_acceleration: f64,         // smoothed rate of rate change
    last_free_bytes: u64,
    last_sample_time: Instant,
    samples_count: u64,
    min_samples_for_prediction: u64, // need at least N samples (default 3)
}

pub struct RateEstimate {
    pub bytes_per_second: f64,       // current smoothed rate (positive = consuming)
    pub seconds_to_exhaustion: f64,  // predicted time until 0% free
    pub seconds_to_threshold: f64,   // predicted time until red threshold
    pub acceleration: f64,           // rate change (positive = accelerating)
    pub confidence: f64,             // 0.0-1.0 based on sample count and variance
    pub trend: Trend,
}

pub enum Trend {
    Stable,        // consumption rate is constant
    Accelerating,  // consumption rate is increasing (agent swarm ramping up)
    Decelerating,  // consumption rate is decreasing (builds finishing)
    Recovering,    // disk is being freed (negative consumption rate)
}
```

### Prediction
time_to_exhaustion = free_bytes / bytes_per_second (when rate > 0)
With acceleration correction: t = (-v + sqrt(v² + 2*a*d)) / a (quadratic model)
where v = current rate, a = acceleration, d = free bytes remaining

### Adaptive Alpha
When disk consumption is very bursty (e.g., cargo build starts), increase alpha temporarily to be more responsive. When stable, decrease alpha for smoother estimates.

### Why This Matters
Without rate estimation, sbh can only react AFTER thresholds are crossed. With EWMA prediction, sbh can start preparing BEFORE the threshold is crossed:
- If time_to_exhaustion < 5 minutes → start preemptive cleanup
- If acceleration is positive → start monitoring more frequently
- If trend is Recovering → reduce scan frequency to save CPU

## Design Rationale
EWMA is the right tool because: (1) disk consumption is noisy (builds start/stop), (2) we need recency-biased smoothing, (3) it's O(1) memory and O(1) per update, (4) the alpha parameter lets us tune reactivity. The acceleration term (second derivative) catches the "10 agents started compiling simultaneously" scenario before it fills the disk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- EWMA correctly smooths noisy input sequences
- Predictions are reasonable for linear consumption patterns
- Quadratic prediction handles acceleration correctly
- Confidence increases with sample count
- Trend detection correctly identifies all four states
- Thread-safe (the monitoring loop updates this from a single thread, but readers may be concurrent)
- Unit tests with synthetic consumption patterns
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit tests validate EWMA smoothing, acceleration estimates, and confidence computation across synthetic traces. 2. Integration tests verify estimator outputs feed controller thresholds without instability. 3. E2E pressure timelines validate early-warning trigger quality against known workloads. 4. Estimator remains deterministic for fixed sample streams and alpha settings. 5. Detailed estimator logs include raw samples, EWMA value, derivative estimates, confidence, and trend state.
close_reason: EWMA rate estimator implemented in monitor/ewma.rs (255 lines): DiskRateEstimator with adaptive alpha, EWMA rate/acceleration/confidence, Trend classification (Stable/Accelerating/Decelerating/Recovering), quadratic projection with linear fallback, unit tests.

title: Multi-factor deterministic candidacy scoring engine
description:
The scoring engine that computes a file_deletion_candidacy_score for every discovered artifact, combining multiple independent factors into a single deterministic score with hard safety vetoes.

## CRITICAL CONTRACT: Pure Computation, Zero I/O
The scoring engine is a PURE FUNCTION. Given identical inputs, it produces identical outputs. It NEVER performs filesystem I/O, network calls, or any side effects. All data it needs is provided by callers:
- Path + metadata → from DirectoryWalker (bd-1w9)
- Artifact classification → from PatternRegistry (bd-1sw)
- pressure_multiplier → from PID controller output (bd-3po), passed in by main loop
- Structural markers → pre-collected by walker as part of WalkEntry.structural_markers: Vec<String>

This means the walker must collect structural markers (checking for subdirs like incremental/, deps/, .fingerprint/) during traversal, and attach them to WalkEntry. The scoring engine then uses these pre-collected markers without touching the filesystem.

## Scoring Formula (Alien Artifact: information-theoretic multi-factor scoring)

```
candidacy_score = pressure_multiplier × Σ(weight_i × factor_i)
```

With hard vetoes that force score to 0.0 regardless of other factors.

## Factor Functions (each normalized to [0.0, 1.0])

**f_location(path)**: Location safety factor
```
/tmp, /data/tmp, /dev/shm     → 0.95  (temp dirs, very safe)
/data/projects/*/target        → 0.80  (build output, safe)
/data/projects/*/.target*      → 0.85  (hidden build output, safe)
/data/projects/*/.tmp_*        → 0.90  (explicitly temporary)
~/.cache/*                     → 0.60  (caches, usually safe)
/home/*/projects/*             → 0.40  (user projects, moderate risk)
/home/*/Documents/*            → 0.10  (user data, high risk)
/ system directories           → 0.00  (never touch)
```

**f_name(entry, classification)**: Name/type classification factor
```
classification.combined_confidence directly (0.0-1.0)
Boost +0.1 if name contains "tmp", "temp", "cache"
Boost +0.15 if classification category is RustTarget
Penalty -0.3 if name contains "backup", "save", "important"
```

**f_age(modified_time, now)**: Age sweet-spot factor (bell curve, not linear)
Note: "now" is passed explicitly for determinism (never call SystemTime::now())
```
< 30 minutes      → 0.00  (too recent, may be in active use)
30 min - 2 hours   → 0.20  (probably still in use)
2 - 4 hours        → 0.70  (cooling off)
4 - 10 hours       → 1.00  (sweet spot: old enough to be stale)
10 - 24 hours      → 0.85  (definitely stale)
1 - 7 days         → 0.60  (old, but user might remember it)
7 - 30 days        → 0.40  (very old, ambiguous)
> 30 days          → 0.25  (ancient - might be intentional)
```

**f_size(bytes)**: Size-efficiency factor (prefer deleting large items)
```
< 1 MB             → 0.05  (not worth the syscall overhead)
1 - 10 MB          → 0.20
10 - 100 MB        → 0.40
100 MB - 1 GB      → 0.70
1 - 10 GB          → 1.00  (maximum value - huge space recovery)
10 - 50 GB         → 0.90  (enormous, slight extra caution)
> 50 GB            → 0.75  (suspiciously large, extra caution)
```

**f_structure(structural_markers)**: Internal structure indicators
Uses pre-collected structural_markers from WalkEntry (NO filesystem I/O here):
```
Contains .fingerprint/ or incremental/  → 0.95  (definitely build artifacts)
Contains deps/ + build/                 → 0.85  (very likely build artifacts)
Contains .git/                          → 0.00  (VETO: this is a repo!)
Contains Cargo.toml at root             → 0.05  (this is a project, not a target)
Contains only .d, .o, .rlib files       → 0.90  (build outputs)
```

## Weights
Default weights (configurable):
```
w_location  = 0.25
w_name      = 0.25
w_age       = 0.20
w_size      = 0.15
w_structure = 0.15
```

## Pressure Multiplier
From PID controller urgency (0.0-1.0), passed in by caller:
```
urgency 0.0    → multiplier 1.0  (normal scoring)
urgency 0.3    → multiplier 1.3  (slightly lower bar)
urgency 0.5    → multiplier 1.5  (moderate pressure)
urgency 0.8    → multiplier 2.0  (aggressive)
urgency 1.0    → multiplier 3.0  (emergency - almost anything goes)
```

## Hard Vetoes (override score to 0.0)
These CANNOT be overridden even under maximum pressure:
1. structural_markers contains ".git" → VETO (never delete repos)
2. Path matches system directory pattern → VETO
3. File age < min_file_age_minutes (default 30) → VETO (age computed from passed-in "now")
4. Path matches any user-configured exclusion → VETO
5. File is currently open by a process → VETO (this is the ONE check that requires I/O — but it's done by the CALLER before invoking the scoring engine, and passed as an `is_open: bool` flag)

## Implementation
```rust
pub struct ScoringEngine {
    weights: ScoringWeights,
    pattern_registry: ArtifactPatternRegistry,
    excluded_paths: Vec<PathBuf>,
    min_file_age: Duration,
}

/// All inputs needed to score a single candidate. No I/O needed.
pub struct ScoringInput {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub size_bytes: u64,
    pub modified_at: SystemTime,
    pub structural_markers: Vec<String>,  // pre-collected by walker
    pub is_open: bool,                     // pre-checked by caller
    pub now: SystemTime,                   // explicit timestamp for determinism
    pub pressure_urgency: f64,             // from PID controller
}

pub struct CandidacyScore {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub total_score: f64,
    pub factors: ScoreFactors,
    pub vetoed: bool,
    pub veto_reason: Option<String>,
    pub classification: ArtifactClassification,
    pub size_bytes: u64,
    pub age: Duration,
}
```

## Determinism
Given the same ScoringInput, the scoring engine MUST produce identical CandidacyScore. No randomness, no implicit time-dependency (all time-dependent computations use the passed-in `now` field). This enables testing and reproducibility.


## Acceptance Criteria
- Deterministic scoring and ordering for identical inputs
- Hard vetoes always dominate computed score
- Pressure scaling monotonic with urgency
- Boundary-value tests for all factors
- Pure-computation contract (no I/O in scorer)
- Integration ranking test with realistic fixtures
acceptance_criteria: 1. Deterministic scoring: identical ScoringInput yields identical CandidacyScore and ordering. 2. Hard vetoes always override score for git/system/excluded/recent/open-file paths. 3. Pressure multiplier mapping is monotonic in urgency. 4. Factor boundary values are unit-tested. 5. Pure-function contract holds: no filesystem or network I/O inside scoring engine. 6. Explainability fields are always populated for decision traces. 7. Integration test validates realistic ranking and veto behavior.

title: [macOS E14] Testing + CI (macos runners, snapshot tests, integration)
description:
# Epic 14: Testing & CI for macOS

## Why thorough testing is non-negotiable here

Mac port introduces dozens of FFI calls, unsafe Mach syscalls, plist generation, launchctl shelling. Every one is a potential silent failure mode. Without comprehensive tests, "works on my machine" becomes "broken on operator's machine" with no warning.

## Test layers required

1. **Unit tests on Mac syscall wrappers.** PAL methods called individually: assert returned data has expected shape, units, ranges.
2. **Integration tests on launchd.** Install LaunchAgent, query via launchctl, kickstart, bootout — in CI on macos-latest runner.
3. **Snapshot tests on plist generation.** Generated XML matches frozen golden files. Canonicalize before comparison (sort keys, normalize whitespace).
4. **Property tests on cleanup heuristics.** Generate random dir trees, assert sacred paths never touched, assert dir contents drive confidence correctly.
5. **End-to-end tests.** Spin up disk-pressure scenario (create N GB ballast, fill remaining), run scan + clean, assert recovery, restore baseline.
6. **Regression tests.** Each bug we fix gets a test case named after the issue.
7. **Bench tests on hot paths.** Daemon poll tick must complete in <200 ms; PAL syscalls < 5 ms each on average.

## CI matrix expansion

GitHub Actions:
- `ubuntu-latest` (existing — Linux x86_64)
- `ubuntu-latest-arm64` (existing or new — Linux arm64)
- `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon — new)
- `macos-13` (Intel — for at least one matrix entry — keep until x86_64 Mac demand drops)

For each: cargo test (unit + integration), cargo build (release binary smoke check), and selected E2E tests.

## Tasks (see child beads)

1. Add `macos-latest` and `macos-13` to GitHub Actions test matrix.
2. CI step: install required Mac tools (xcode-select --install if missing — usually present on runners).
3. CI step: codesign verify on built binary (using ad-hoc signing in CI; real Developer ID signing happens in release workflow only).
4. Test fixture infrastructure: helper to create temp APFS-aware tree mimicking real Mac dir structure (Library/Caches, Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData, etc.). Use temp dir with synthetic markers.
5. Snapshot test crate setup (`insta`) for plist outputs.
6. Property test crate setup (`proptest`) for cleanup confidence engine.
7. Integration test: launchd lifecycle (bootstrap → kickstart → bootout in single-user runner).
8. Coverage tracking: add `cargo-llvm-cov` step; report coverage delta per PR; fail if Mac-side coverage drops.
9. CI fail-fast on UnsupportedPlatform errors (those should never appear in green CI).
10. Document in CONTRIBUTING.md: how to run Mac tests locally; how to run Linux tests on a Mac dev machine (cross-compile + run in a Linux VM via lima/utm).

## Test philosophy specific to Mac

- **Don't mock libc/Mach unless absolutely necessary.** Run real syscalls in tests; the temp dir / /tmp / fork-and-exec patterns work fine in CI runners. Mocking syscalls hides FFI bugs.
- **DO mock launchctl in unit tests** (it's a system service we don't want to actually install). Integration tests can install for real with `Label = com.dicklesworthstone.sbh.test.<random>` to avoid colliding with real installs.
- **Avoid time-based flakiness.** No `sleep(60)`-based "wait for daemon to start" — use polling with timeout.
- **Snapshot tests are golden, not floor.** Updating snapshots requires explicit `cargo insta accept`.

## Failure modes

- Skipping CI on Mac when budget tight → regressions land.
- macOS runners are slow (10+ min for full test suite). Mitigation: parallelize, skip slow E2E tests on PR runs, run them on nightly cron.
- launchctl in CI runner has weird state from previous test run. Mitigation: aggressive bootout in test setup; use unique per-test labels.

title: fanotify/inotify event source (Linux) + reconciliation fallback
description: Implement Linux event-source abstraction with fanotify where permitted. If fanotify is unavailable, not privileged, or unsuitable, use inotify only with watch-budgeted recursive watches for selected roots/subtrees; plain root watches do not observe deep changes. When recursive watches exceed budget, mark the root dirty and rely on bounded reconciliation. Events only mark roots/subtrees dirty; overflow, backend restart, permission loss, and watch exhaustion force bounded reconciliation. macOS/other platforms use reconciliation until a safe backend exists. The main crate forbids unsafe code: use a safe dependency with audited public API, or defer that backend and keep reconciliation fallback. Ref docs/scanner-redesign-event-driven.md section 3.1.
acceptance_criteria: Event source has capability detection, overflow tests, watch-budget behavior, recursive-inotify coverage tests where enabled, and dirty-root reconciliation fallback when watches are incomplete. Deletion remains gated by final preflight. Unsupported or unsafe-unavailable platforms fail conservative and still run bounded reconciliation. No local unsafe code is introduced.
notes: Implemented safe scanner event-source abstraction: Linux recursive inotify with safe crate and default stream features disabled, capability probes with fanotify explicitly deferred, watch-budget recursive planning, dirty-root invalidation, overflow/backend-loss generation bump, v2 daemon integration before index checkpointing, non-Linux reconciliation-only fallback. title: Pressure-gated effort ladder + CPU budget + failure backoff
description: Implement pressure-gated scanner effort ladder, in-process CPU/time budget, resumable cursor, and durable failed-delete backoff. Green drains events/statfs and does no deep recursive work; yellow refreshes dirty indexed candidates; orange/red rank from index and stop after enough safe bytes. Backoff applies to source/protection/open/permission/identity failures and resets only when evidence changes. Ref docs/scanner-redesign-event-driven.md sections 3.2 and 3.8.
acceptance_criteria: Green steady-state stays below the configured CPU budget and avoids recursive root walks. Under pressure, scanning stops after meeting target bytes or budget. Failed-delete retry rate is bounded by cooldown and existing successful delete/recreate dampening remains intact.
notes: Implemented v2 pressure-gated effort ladder and durable failure backoff. Green/Yellow v2 scans now do no recursive work when event invalidation has no dirty roots and scan only dirty roots otherwise. Orange+ drains ranked persistent-index candidates before walking and stops once the current batch has enough safe candidate bytes. V2 walker parallelism is capped by pressure level, and existing wall-clock/entry budgets plus the scan cursor remain the in-process budget mechanism. Deletion safety/preflight failures feed ScannerIndexFeedback into the persistent candidate index; unchanged failed evidence preserves exponential cooldown and is retried only after cooldown expires, while evidence changes reset backoff. Repeat successful delete/recreate dampening remains unchanged.
